Companion to the round-3 design review of issue #4525

Verification votes and corrections, round 3

Every new finding on the round-3 review page was put to three verifiers who tried to refute it (a source-truth lens, a design-text-fairness lens, an intent lens). This page holds their reasons and corrections verbatim. A finding survived when at least two of the three could not refute it. Rejected candidates are listed at the end. The disposition rows of section 3 (one checker plus two re-graders per known item) are here too, under dispo-N.., dispo-M.., dispo-F.. and dispo-C.. anchors. The round-1 votes are on their own page and the round-2 votes on theirs.

Checker assessment: The round-2 STILL NEEDED list had three parts. Two are met, one is met by a substitute, and one is not met. (1) Replace the wrong sentence at old :221: MET. design-r3.txt:247 now says a missing override uses the base's fp32 conversion fallback and a wrong signature can fail compilation. Verified against h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:111-117@2880c3aa9b (if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk); identical at f46e48ba and live main 1400fa4481). The S15 "[bf16 override detection]" link points at expr.hpp#L110-L117. (2a) Replace "silently takes a lossy fallback" with "bit-exact for stored bf16 but slower": HALF MET. "lossy" is gone and :440 says "the bit-exact fallback" (verified: h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109 changes bits only when the exponent field is saturated and the low 16 bits are nonzero; even_part/odd_part at kv_cache.hpp:2000-2007 leave the low 16 bits zero). The word "slower", or any statement of the fallback's cost, is absent from :247, :328 and :440 (grep of design-r3.txt for slower/extra/round trip finds only :326, about append). Same gap as N13. (2b) Add "exact bf16 row reads (bf16_chunk)" to the objdump regions: NOT DONE at :486/:488 (regions are even/odd V append, packed token copy, weighted sums, allocation/restore). SUBSTITUTE ACCEPTED: :440 adds decltype(&Row::bf16_chunk) against bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept. That check distinguishes the inherited base member (whose pointer type is bf16s (expr<Row,D>::*)(size_t) const noexcept) from a derived override, so it detects an omitted override at compile time. The round-2 N13 corrected recommendation allowed "the static_assert or the instruction record" as the detector, so I do not demand the objdump region. It remains useful as an optional extra, because only the instruction record would show an override body that itself performs a float round trip. (3) Re-grader addition: name a runtime path that actually calls bf16_chunk: NOT MET. :440 still says "Construct a host tensor from the packed matrix view. Check row chunks and exact bf16 copies" and keeps the hardware-tensor fixture optional ("only if it already accepts this input"). A host tensor never calls bf16_chunk: h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:272-274@2880c3aa9b builds rows with std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]), and the rank-1 constructor and assignment at tensor.hpp:79-85 and :125-129 call store_chunk(i, rhs.chunk(i)); tensor<N> holds float (tensor.hpp:32-34 using scalar = float; using element = float;), so "exact bf16 copies" through a host tensor is not a bf16_chunk path. Checker assessment: Three parts of the corrected recommendation. (1) Mechanism: named at :438 ("dependent requires concepts and STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE in the existing suite"); "dependent" is the right nuance, because a non-dependent ill-formed requires-expression is a hard error, not false. The case is only paraphrased ("existing typed-slot compile checks"); the real case is TEST_CASE "attention operations resolve to typed KV slots" at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:316 with the STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE block at :338-342, and the constants at :84-123 are reachable only through the S16 link "Compile-time access requirements" (t_llama_unit.cpp#L84-L123, design-r3-links.tsv:209), which is the right range. (2) get_v form: "Wrap or accept" is replaced by "Accept an aligned typed destination and call load_row" (:269; wdiff "OLD: Wrap or accept a / NEW: Accept an aligned"), which is the typed-view parameter form matching set_v (:268) and load_row's destination "view<Destination, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> dst" (:255). No reason clause is given; the intent lens asked for one. (3) Consequence: :269 and :439 say page_supports_uniform_kv_access is rewritten and "the existing positive uniform-layout and negative heterogeneous-layout assertions" are preserved; those are STATIC_REQUIRE at t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:483 (true, uniform page) and STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE at :779 (false, heterogeneous page), and the probe at :105-109 does call page.get_v(kv_slot_id(0), 0, 0, output) with "bf16* output". The full.hpp callback at :269 matches h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2656 (v_head_fn calls get_v into bf16* dest and returns dest). The six raw-pointer get_v test callers (t_llama_unit.cpp:819, :1575, :2038, :2539, :2761, :2824) are not enumerated; the rg pattern at :382 contains get_v, which the intent lens accepted as sufficient. The intent lens's include point is moot: t_llama_unit includes tron/models/model.hpp (:66), model.hpp includes self_attention.hpp (model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:53), which includes amx_attn_iface.hpp (self_attention.hpp:21), so the kernel declarations are visible for kernel-call rejections. AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:53-54 ("Prefer extending the closest existing test") is honored by :445. Substance is present; the verbatim case name and the reason for the chosen form are missing, so partly.

Still needed: At design-r3.txt:438 replace the row header "Typed function boundaries: existing typed-slot compile checks" with "Typed function boundaries: the case 'attention operations resolve to typed KV slots' (t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:316-342) and the requires-expression constants at :84-123". At :269 add one reason clause after "Accept an aligned typed destination and call load_row": "matching set_v's typed source row; this rewrites page_supports_uniform_kv_access (:105-109), the six raw-pointer get_v test callers (:819, :1575, :2038, :2539, :2761, :2824) and full.hpp:2652-2656."

In the parent the two kernel cache-plane parameters are const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> and v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> (design-r3.txt:277; today both are const bf16* at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:219-222 and :230-233). source re-grader (Resolved): The design now names the mechanism, rewrites the probe, and picks one get_v form. Mechanism: the Typed function boundaries row says to use dependent requires checks with STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE in the existing suite [design-r3.txt:438]. That is the repository precedent: constexpr bool variable templates holding requires-expressions at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:84-123, asserted with STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE inside TEST_CASE 'attention operations resolve to typed KV slots' at :316-342. The row's title 'existing typed-slot compile checks' paraphrases that case name, and the S16 link [Compile-time access requirements] points at t/t_llama_unit.cpp#L84-L123 at 2880c3aa9b [design-r3-links.tsv:209], so the location is given. Probe rewrite: the get_v row says to rewrite the existing compile-time page_supports_uniform_kv_access probe to use the new destination type [design-r3.txt:269], and the Typed get_v destination row says to supply an aligned destination view and preserve the positive uniform-layout and negative heterogeneous-layout assertions [design-r3.txt:439]. Those facts are right: the constant takes bf16* output [t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:105-109], is asserted true at :483 on the uniform empty_cache_t page and false at :779 on the heterogeneous page. The negative assertion stays false after the rewrite because the non-template get_v requires layout_t::uniform_geometry [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1634-1642]. Chosen form: 'Wrap or accept' is gone (design-wdiff.txt:806); the row now says 'Accept an aligned typed destination and call load_row' [design-r3.txt:269], and step 6 names the concept probe and the aligned row wrappers [design-r3.txt:377]. The consequences of that choice are handled and correct. full.hpp's v_head_fn receives bf16* dest and returns it [full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2651-2657]; its scratch is alignas(64) std::array<bf16, HW_MAX_KV_HEADS * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE> [src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203] with HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE = 128 [h/libpos.hpp@2880c3aa9b:72], so each per-head offset is 256 bytes and 64-byte aligned; the design's 'wraps its aligned scratch and returns that same buffer' is right. The six test callers (t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:819, 1575, 2038, 2539, 2761, 2824) already pass 64-byte-aligned scratch (alignas(64) arrays at :818, :1574, :2036, :2759, :2822; tensor<head_size> storage is alignas(chunk_alignment) [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:34]), and today's get_v already stores with aligned instructions [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2420, 2427, 2456, 2464], so the 'aligned' destination adds no new precondition. The rg pattern with get_v finds all callers [design-r3.txt:382]. The section 9 row matches the body [design-r3.txt:530]. Two minor residuals do not change the grade: the case name is paraphrased rather than quoted, and the reason for choosing the typed-view form (asked by the intent lens) is not stated. Correction: One addition to the design's fix is advisable. The round-2 row named the kernel boundary ('Reject raw pointers and packed V at native-K kernel calls; reject native K at packed-V calls'); the round-3 row says only 'Reject implicit raw-pointer arguments and wrong packed view types' [design-r3.txt:438, design-wdiff.txt:1569-1589]. t/t_llama_unit.cpp does not include tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (its tron includes at :57-73 end with tron/threading.hpp); only t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:39 and t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:26 include it at 2880c3aa9b. A dependent requires-expression that calls an undeclared kernel name is simply false, so a STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE on it passes for the wrong reason, which AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:39-41 forbids as a tautology. Suggested sentence for the row at design-r3.txt:438: 'Kernel-argument rejections either live in t_amx_dispatch_dtype / t_amx_numerics, which already include amx_attn_iface.hpp, or t_llama_unit adds that include; pair each STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE with a STATIC_REQUIRE that the correct typed argument is accepted.' Also a term nit: the existing checks are constexpr bool variable templates, not C++ concepts; 'dependent requires concepts' [design-r3.txt:438] and 'uniform-access concept' [design-r3.txt:530] should read 'requires-expression constants'.

fairness re-grader (Partly): The substance of the corrected recommendation is present, and its checkable facts are right, but three concrete parts the recommendation asked for are still missing from the text. Present: (1) The mechanism is named: "Use dependent requires concepts and STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE in the existing suite. Reject implicit raw-pointer arguments and wrong packed view types. Check read-only writes, const-row mutation, reverse const conversion, and rvalue-owner views. Accept writable-to-read-only conversion. Keep explicit native-view pointer construction legal." [design-r3.txt:438]. (A requires-expression is a C++ compile-time check that yields true when a call is well-formed and false when it is not; STATIC_REQUIRE is Catch2's compile-time assertion macro.) This matches the repository precedent: constexpr bool constants holding requires-expressions at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:84-123, asserted with STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE at :338-342. (2) One get_v form is chosen, replacing round-2's "Wrap or accept" [design-revised-text.txt:253]: "Keep the name. Accept an aligned typed destination and call load_row ." [design-r3.txt:269]; this is the typed-view form, matching set_v [design-r3.txt:268]. Its callback fact is right: full.hpp's v_head_fn calls get_v into the caller's dest and returns dest [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2657]; the caller's scratch is alignas(64) std::array<bf16, HW_MAX_KV_HEADS * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE> v_scratch and each head gets v_scratch.data() + h * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE [src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203,213]; HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE = 128 [h/libpos.hpp@2880c3aa9b:72], so each per-head slice starts at a multiple of 256 bytes and is 64-byte aligned, as the design's "aligned scratch" says. (3) The probe rewrite is specified with its truth values preserved: "Rewrite the existing compile-time page_supports_uniform_kv_access probe to use the new destination type." [design-r3.txt:269] and "Update page_supports_uniform_kv_access and its get-V requirement to supply an aligned destination view. Preserve the existing positive uniform-layout and negative heterogeneous-layout assertions." [design-r3.txt:439]. Those assertions are STATIC_REQUIRE at t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:483 (uniform cache, TEST_CASE at :433) and STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE at :779 (heterogeneous cache, TEST_CASE at :761), so the description is right. Step 6 names "the typed-access concept probe" [design-r3.txt:377], and the section-9 row [design-r3.txt:530] links to #tests where this body text lives. Missing: (a) The recommendation asked the row to name the case "attention operations resolve to typed KV slots" (t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:316-342) and the constants' location (:84-123). The row says only "existing typed-slot compile checks" and "the existing suite" [design-r3.txt:438]. The one exact pointer, S16's "[Compile-time access requirements]" link to t_llama_unit.cpp#L84-L123 [design-r3-links.tsv:209], sits in the sources table [design-r3.txt:580] and is not cited from the row. (b) The intent-lens correction asked the row to say that kernel-call rejections need the amx_attn_iface.hpp declarations included in t_llama_unit. t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:8-73 has no include of tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp. The design's row does not say where the kernel-signature rejections compile, and the generic sentence "Include full definitions in real/fake function definitions and callers that need them" [design-r3.txt:284] does not name this test. (c) The intent-lens correction asked the get_v row to state the reason for the chosen form; :269 gives the choice and its callback consequence but no reason. The design-text-lens correction asked, for the typed-view form, to name the six raw-pointer test callers (t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:819, 1575, 2038, 2539, 2761, 2824); the design leaves them to the rg search, which does include get_v [design-r3.txt:382], and to step 6's "explicit aligned row wrappers" [design-r3.txt:377]. Part (c) is low risk because the search finds every caller. One terminology slip, no status change: "dependent requires concepts" [design-r3.txt:438] describes constexpr bool variable templates holding requires-expressions, not C++ concept declarations; "dependent" is right, since the requires-expression must sit in a template so a failed constraint yields false instead of a hard compile error. Severity stays minor. Correction: To the design's fix, three text additions would close the item: in the row at design-r3.txt:438 add "next to the constants at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:84-123, in the case 'attention operations resolve to typed KV slots' (:316-342); kernel-signature rejections need #include \"tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp\" in t_llama_unit, which does not include it today"; in the get_v row at :269 add one reason clause, for example "typed view, matching set_v, so the six raw-pointer test callers found by the rg search are rewritten with aligned row views". To the checker's evidence: add t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:8-73 (no amx_attn_iface.hpp include) and src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203,213 with h/libpos.hpp@2880c3aa9b:72 (HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE = 128), which verify the design's "aligned scratch" claim.

Partly M04. Heterogeneous construction pass: the compile-time geometry dispatch helper is unnamed although book already has one (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:348 "Run the construction helper in book::allocate_kv_group after installing a successful allocation, before publishing access. Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path. Preserve the early return for zero-byte arenas." design-r3.txt:350 "For heterogeneous geometry, enumerate physical storage offsets once and select only slots in the just-allocated arena. Restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart objects in the retained arena. Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which dispatches the physical slot to its compile-time geometry. Filter on layout_t::storage_location(offset, logical_slot_count()).reclaimable for the arena being constructed. layout_t::storage_location identifies its arena; slot_base gives arena + n_pages * byte_offset. Construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at that address. Do not construct the same region again for a logical alias." design-r3.txt:373 step 2 "Check sizes, offsets, EAGLE, geometry dispatch, and failure paths." design-r3.txt:521 "| N25 M04 | Use existing geometry dispatch and filter by arena. ... |" design-r3.txt:580 S16 "[Allocation, publication, and geometry dispatch]" -> kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b#L1188-L1248 and "[Random fill entry point]" -> #L1054-L1064 (design-r3-links.tsv:200-201). fill_random appears in the body only at design-r3.txt:262 and :274, as the layout-blind fill exception, not as the dispatch precedent. grep of design-r3.txt for storage_slot_count and kv_storage_offset: no match.

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation (all three verifier lenses agree on this core) asked the heterogeneous bullet to: name book::for_each_active_slot as the compile-time geometry dispatch; describe it as calling a lambda with <slot, geometry> for each active logical slot, as fill_random does; filter by layout_t::storage_location(kv_storage_offset(slot), logical_slot_count()).reclaimable; construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at slot_base(kv_storage_offset(slot)); and state that storage_slot_count_ is set before allocate_kv_group runs. The lenses disagree about the slot_base null-check sentence (source lens: include a corrected version; intent lens: drop it or keep it as a note), so I do not require it. What the design now has (design-r3.txt:350), checked against kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b. for_each_active_slot is named; it exists at :1242-1249 and for_each_slot_impl :1236-1240 passes kv_slot_specs[slots].geometry as the template argument. The filter storage_location(offset, logical_slot_count()).reclaimable matches :727-735, and storage_location takes a kv_storage_offset (:728). slot_base = arena + n_pages * byte_offset matches :1188-1197. The block count geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages matches kv_block_at_storage's index blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] (:1334) and fill_storage_slot's loops (:1368-1369). The S16 links now reach the helper (L1188-L1248 covers slot_base, allocate_kv_group and for_each_active_slot) and the precedent (L1054-L1064 covers fill_random). Section-9 row 521 links #lifetime and matches the body. Three concrete parts of the corrected recommendation are missing. (a) fill_random is not named as the dispatch precedent in the bullet; it appears only as the fill exception (design-r3.txt:262, :274). (b) The bullet writes storage_location(offset, ...) but never says offset = kv_storage_offset(slot). Both storage_location (:728) and slot_base (:1188) take a kv_storage_offset, and fill_random shows the conversion at :1061. (c) The validity fact is absent: storage_slot_count_ and support_eagle_ are set in the constructor's initializer list (:1091-1093) before allocate_kv_group runs (:1101-1102), so logical_slot_count() (:920-922, which reads both) and slot_base are valid inside allocate_kv_group, where line 348 places the construction. These are small omissions; an implementer who follows the S16 links finds them in the source. The substance (the helper, the filter, the count) is present, so the status is partly.

Still needed: In design-r3.txt:350 replace "Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which dispatches the physical slot to its compile-time geometry." with "Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which calls the lambda once per active logical slot index with that slot's compile-time geometry (kv_cache.hpp:1243-1249). Form the physical offset as kv_storage_offset(slot), as fill_random does (:1060-1061)." Delete the sentence about a logical alias: a fixed layout maps each logical slot to one distinct physical region, so no deduplication is needed (G19).

New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: the new sentence labels the helper's loop variable wrongly. Design quote: design-r3.txt:350 "Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which dispatches the physical slot to its compile-time geometry." Source: for_each_active_slot iterates slot indices into kv_slot_specs and keeps only slot < logical_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1244-1247]; the code comment calls these "logical K/V slots" [:918-922]; fill_random converts each to a physical offset with kv_storage_offset(slot) [:1061]. The effect is unchanged for the heterogeneous pass: storage_location indexes slot_specs[offset.i] [:732], so physical offset i equals logical slot i for every i below logical_slot_count, and the only extra physical slot (EAGLE) cannot exist in a heterogeneous layout [:1158-1159]. Recommendation: write "for each active logical slot" and add "use kv_storage_offset(slot) as the physical offset", as the residual wording does. No behavior risk; worth knowing because the same bullet opens with "enumerate physical storage offsets", so a reader may look for a physical-offset loop that the helper does not provide.

source re-grader (Resolved): The heterogeneous bullet now names the helper and the filter [design-r3.txt:350]: "Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which dispatches the physical slot to its compile-time geometry. Filter on layout_t::storage_location(offset, logical_slot_count()).reclaimable for the arena being constructed. layout_t::storage_location identifies its arena; slot_base gives arena + n_pages * byte_offset. Construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at that address." Each fact checks at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b. for_each_active_slot is a const member that calls a generic lambda (a lambda with template parameters) as function.template operator()<slot, geometry>() for every slot < logical_slot_count() [:1242-1249], built on for_each_slot_impl over std::index_sequence with kv_slot_specs[slots].geometry [:1236-1240]. storage_location(kv_storage_offset offset, size_t logical_slot_count) returns {reclaimable, byte_offset} [:727-735]. slot_base returns arena->get() + n_pages * location.byte_offset with a checked multiply [:1188-1197]. Each slot region holds geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks: make_kv_slot_offsets sizes a slot as specs[slot].geometry.n_kv_heads * block_bytes per page [:664-666] and kv_block_at_storage indexes blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] [:1334]. Filtering by storage_location(...).reclaimable in both passes is what the three verifier corrections asked for in place of a null test on slot_base; the intent-lens correction dropped the null-check and initializer-list sentences from the recommended text, so their absence is not a gap. The helper is callable inside allocate_kv_group: storage_slot_count_ and support_eagle_ are set in the constructor's initializer list [:1092-1093] before the two allocate_kv_group calls [:1101-1102]. The phrase "dispatches the physical slot" is loose but not wrong: the helper iterates active logical slots, and for those slots the physical offset index equals the slot index (fill_random builds kv_storage_offset(slot) from the same lambda argument [:1061]); the only other physical slot, EAGLE, is excluded for heterogeneous layouts by design-r3.txt:351. Step 2 "Check sizes, offsets, EAGLE, geometry dispatch, and failure paths" [design-r3.txt:373] and the section 9 row [design-r3.txt:521] match the body. Sources row S16 links the dispatch region kv_cache.hpp#L1188-L1248 and fill_random #L1054-L1064 [design-r3-links.tsv:200-201], so the precedent is reachable from the design. Checker quotes confirmed at design-r3.txt:348, 350, 373, 521, 580. Correction: Minor precision to the design fix (low risk if not applied). The bullet uses offset without saying how the lambda's slot becomes one, and the body names fill_random only as the layout-blind fill exception [design-r3.txt:262, 274], not as the dispatch precedent; the checker's grep is right that design-r3.txt has no match for kv_storage_offset or storage_slot_count. Suggested wording for design-r3.txt:350: "Filter on layout_t::storage_location(kv_storage_offset(slot), logical_slot_count()).reclaimable == reclaimable, as fill_random does around for_each_active_slot (kv_cache.hpp:1058-1065), and construct at slot_base(kv_storage_offset(slot))."

fairness re-grader (Resolved): Severity: none remaining (note only). The recommendation, as corrected by the intent lens, asked the bullet to name book::for_each_active_slot as the compile-time geometry dispatch helper, to filter inside it on layout_t::storage_location(...).reclaimable for the arena being constructed, and to construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at slot_base(...). The null-check sentence was to be dropped or kept as a note. The design does this at design-r3.txt:350: "Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which dispatches the physical slot to its compile-time geometry. Filter on layout_t::storage_location(offset, logical_slot_count()).reclaimable for the arena being constructed. layout_t::storage_location identifies its arena; slot_base gives arena + n_pages * byte_offset. Construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at that address." The construction form for those blocks is fixed at design-r3.txt:344 (default-initialization, no parentheses or braces). Every checkable fact is right. for_each_active_slot calls the lambda with <slot, geometry> for each slot below logical_slot_count() (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1242-1249). storage_location returns {reclaimable, byte_offset} (:727-735). slot_base returns arena->get() + n_pages * byte_offset with a checked multiply (:1188-1197). A slot region holds n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks, indexed [kv_head * n_pages + pg] (:1334). The filter by storage_location in both passes removes the null-check hazard the verifiers described (reclaimable pass :1102 and restore :968, where both arenas exist), so no separate sentence is needed; the intent lens allowed dropping it. The design-text verifier's complaint that no design link reached kv_cache.hpp 1055-1065 or 1236-1249 is also addressed: S16 now links "[Allocation, publication, and geometry dispatch]" -> kv_cache.hpp#L1188-L1248 (covers for_each_slot_impl and for_each_active_slot at 1236-1248) and "[Random fill entry point]" -> #L1054-L1064 (design-r3.txt:580; design-r3-links.tsv:200-201). Section 7 step 2 names "geometry dispatch" (design-r3.txt:373), and section 9 row design-r3.txt:521 matches the body. Two notes, no change required. (a) fill_random is not named in the bullet as the precedent. It appears in the body only as the layout-blind fill exception (design-r3.txt:262, :274). The S16 link supplies the precedent instead. (b) The phrase "dispatches the physical slot" is loose. The helper iterates logical slots 0 .. logical_slot_count() - 1 (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1244-1247). For those slots the physical offset equals the logical index, which is why fill_random passes kv_storage_offset(slot) (:1061). The bullet also does not spell out that its "offset" means kv_storage_offset(slot). Neither can mislead an implementer, because design-r3.txt:351 excludes the only physical slot without a logical index (EAGLE) from this enumeration. Correction: The checker's note "grep of design-r3.txt for storage_slot_count and kv_storage_offset: no match" should not count as a residual. The intent-lens correction removed the storage_slot_count_ sentence from the required text. The spelling kv_storage_offset(slot) appears only in that lens's suggested wording; its absence is a wording note, not a missing rule.

Partly N20. v_vnni_row constructor not covered by no-public-pointer rule (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:248: "| View copy and conversion | Copying a view rebinds access. Allow writable-to-read-only conversion only. Owners, views, and rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion. Rows are constructed only by the matrix view. |" design-r3.txt:240: "v_vnni_view<T,R,D> inherits expr<view_type,R,D>. v_vnni_row<T,D> inherits expr<row_type,D>. Restrict T to bf16 or const bf16. A row stores its pair address and parity by value. It outlives a temporary matrix view while the owner remains alive." design-r3.txt:245: "A const matrix returns a read-only row. A const row returns a read-only element, even when its element type is bf16." design-r3.txt:249: "| Internal storage access | Use detail::v_vnni_access , a friend declared with the V types, only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels. ... Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers. |" design-r3.txt:438: "Reject implicit raw-pointer arguments and wrong packed view types. Check read-only writes, const-row mutation, reverse const conversion, and rvalue-owner views. Accept writable-to-read-only conversion." design-r3.txt:518 (section 9): "Restrict row construction."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked the contract row to cover v_vnni_row: no public pointer constructor, the matrix view as its only producer, no exposed pointer. The row now says rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member or pointer conversion, and "Rows are constructed only by the matrix view" [design-r3.txt:248]; the word diff confirms this sentence is new (OLD "conversion for packed views" -> NEW "conversion. Rows are constructed only by the matrix view") [design-wdiff.txt:619-622]. That is the private-constructor-plus-friend rule in prose, and it matches Ben's rule for views ("The private constructor prevents routine callers from relabelling an arbitrary row-major pointer as packed data", comment 5765866077 in evidence/github-review.json). The design-text verifier's item (2) is satisfied by omission of the contested sentence: the design no longer says detail::vnni_access is "the only pointer reader"; it says v_vnni_access is a friend declared with the V types and used only inside typed operations and V kernels [design-r3.txt:249]. Verifier item (1), a friend declaration so v_vnni_row<const bf16,D> can be built from v_vnni_row<bf16,D>, was conditional on the design requiring row conversion. The design does not require it: read-only rows come from a const matrix [design-r3.txt:245], and no consumer named in the design converts a writable row to a read-only one. The optional compile-check addition ("reject a packed row built from a raw pointer") is not in design-r3.txt:438, which names only "implicit raw-pointer arguments and wrong packed view types"; it was optional, so it does not block resolved. Facts checked: the sketch's friend list and private constructor (Ben's comment), the round-2 text of the row (design-wdiff.txt:615-630).

Still needed: In design-r3.txt:248 add one clause: either "Rows have no cross-constness conversion; obtain a read-only row from a read-only matrix view" or "v_vnni_row<const bf16,D> is constructible from v_vnni_row<bf16,D> through a friend declaration". In :438 say that the accepted writable-to-read-only conversion is between views (and rows, if chosen), and add STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_view<bf16,R,D>, bf16*>) and the row equivalent so the private-constructor rule has a test (G40).

New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: the same table row says "Allow writable-to-read-only conversion only" and then "Rows are constructed only by the matrix view" [design-r3.txt:248]. Section 8 asks tests to "Accept writable-to-read-only conversion" without saying for which types [design-r3.txt:438]. A converting constructor v_vnni_row<const bf16,D>(v_vnni_row<bf16,D>) is a constructor the matrix view does not call, so an implementer cannot tell whether rows convert (which needs template <typename, size_t> friend class v_vnni_row;, as Ben's sketch does for views with template <typename, typename> friend class vnni_view;, comment 5765866077) or do not convert (then a test that converts a row fails to compile). No named consumer needs the conversion: read-only rows come from a const matrix [design-r3.txt:245]. Recommendation: add one clause to design-r3.txt:248, either "Rows have no cross-constness conversion; obtain a read-only row from a read-only matrix view" or "v_vnni_row<const bf16,D> is constructible from v_vnni_row<bf16,D> through a friend declaration", and say in design-r3.txt:438 that the accepted conversion is between views (and rows, if chosen).

source re-grader (Partly): The contract row now covers rows: 'Owners, views, and rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion. Rows are constructed only by the matrix view.' [design-r3.txt:248]. That states a non-public (pair address, parity) constructor and the matrix view as the only producer. It matches Ben's rule that the private constructor prevents relabelling an arbitrary pointer as packed data [evidence/github-review.json, comment 5765866077]. The row stores its pair address and parity by value [:240]. It reads through its own chunk(i) and bf16_chunk(i) [:246-247]. detail::v_vnni_access is limited to typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels [:249]. That follows the verifier correction that the access helper need not read rows. The friend-for-conversion point is moot under this text. Rows have no converting constructor because they are constructed only by the matrix view. Read-only rows come from a const matrix or from a const-element view [:245]. One concrete part is missing. The compile-check row [:438] lists 'Reject implicit raw-pointer arguments and wrong packed view types. Check read-only writes, const-row mutation, reverse const conversion, and rvalue-owner views.' It has no check that a packed view or a packed row cannot be constructed from a raw pointer. The intent-lens correction asked for that check. Section 9 says 'Restrict row construction' [:518] and the body change exists at :248, so this is a body fix with one test entry missing. Severity: minor. Correction: Add to design-r3.txt:438: 'STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_row<bf16, D>, bf16*, bool>) and STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_constructible_v<v_vnni_view<bf16, R, D>, bf16*>)', so the private-constructor rule has a test. Optionally state at :248 that rows also have no converting constructor between element types; today's text only implies it. The checker's design evidence quotes exist at the cited lines.

fairness re-grader (Partly): The core of the corrected recommendation is met. The contract row now says: "Owners, views, and rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion. Rows are constructed only by the matrix view." [design-r3.txt:248]. The row stores its pair address and parity by value [design-r3.txt:240]. Together these state the rule the recommendation asked for: no public pointer constructor on the row, the matrix view as the only producer, no pointer exposure. Verifier item (2) is met: the design no longer names detail::v_vnni_access as the row's pointer reader; it limits that helper to typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels [design-r3.txt:249]. Missing piece: the intent-lens correction asked to add "construct a packed row from a raw pointer" to the reject list of the compile-check row. That row rejects "implicit raw-pointer arguments and wrong packed view types" and checks "const-row mutation" [design-r3.txt:438], but it does not test row construction from a raw pointer. The design-text lens marked this addition optional; the intent lens did not. If the lead treats it as optional, this item is resolved. Verifier item (1), a friend declaration so a writable row converts to a read-only row, is moot under the design's own rule: "Rows are constructed only by the matrix view" [design-r3.txt:248] excludes a row-to-row conversion, and a const matrix returns a read-only row directly [design-r3.txt:245], so no consumer needs the conversion. One ambiguity remains, severity minor: the same cell says "Allow writable-to-read-only conversion only" [design-r3.txt:248], so an implementer may read that as applying to rows as well. One clause would settle it, for example: "Rows do not convert; obtain a read-only row from a const matrix."

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:389 "- At port time, remeasure shared files with git diff --name-only and conflicts with git merge-tree against the recorded current main/parent and saved child head. Section 9, design-r3.txt:523 "| N29 N30 | Remove the fragile historical overlap count. Remeasure shared files and conflicts against the final parent scope at port time. [Design section] | The old common.hpp conflict is historical evidence only. |"

Checker assessment: The core of the corrected recommendation is present: :389 now tells the implementer to re-run git merge-tree (and git diff --name-only) at port time against the parent head and the saved child head, and it says the historical common.hpp result "does not predict the final conflict set". The design also follows the intent-lens correction by not writing the dated eleven-file list into the page. Two concrete parts of the corrected recommendation are missing. (1) The commit of the historical check is not named. Every corrected version of the recommendation begins "That measurement is from main 98bb8cb22f94". :389 says only "The historical check", and nothing links it to the 98bb8cb2 row at :148. grep for "98bb8cb2" in design-r3.txt finds it only at :148 and :576. git log -1 98bb8cb22f94 confirms the commit (2026-09-19T17:25:58Z, "Merge pull request #4503"). (2) Semantic review of auto-merged files is limited to self_attention.hpp. The intent-lens correction asked to "give the auto-merged ones (build files and headers restructured on main) a semantic review before rework". The verified case is src/tron/CMakeLists.txt: main changed it by 130 lines (git diff --stat c7844ca2ce 2880c3aa9b -- src/tron/CMakeLists.txt = 112 insertions, 18 deletions, from commit 0128331632 "cmake: compile model specializations per architecture", 2026-09-21T21:37:46Z, merged in 6fc67383a5 at 2026-09-22T00:53:07Z); the child adds 16 lines there (git diff c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb -- src/tron/CMakeLists.txt: the TRON_K_VNNI block, which requires TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, at 30c4ac82cb:src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:209-215); main's gate that compiles amx_attn.cpp only under TRON_AMX_DISPATCH is at 2880c3aa9b:src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:219-223. Files changed on both sides since c7844ca2ce (comm -12 of the two git diff --name-only lists) are 11 at 2880c3aa9b and still 11 at live main 1400fa4481: config/test-benchmarks.json, .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml, h/tron/models/common.hpp, model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, ingest/src/TronCpp.hs, ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs, README.ci.md, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt, t/CMakeLists.txt, t/t_llama_unit.cpp. None of this needs to be listed in the design (the intent lens said not to), but the general instruction to review auto-merged build files is missing. The section-9 row (:523) matches the body change; this is not a table-only claim. Severity of the gap: minor. The re-measure instruction is what protects the implementer, and it is there.

Still needed: In design-r3.txt:389 replace "The historical check found an include conflict in common.hpp." with "The historical check, made against main 98bb8cb22f94, found one include conflict in common.hpp." Replace "Review self_attention.hpp semantically even when Git merges it automatically." with "Give every file changed on both sides a semantic review before rework even when Git merges it automatically, in particular self_attention.hpp and build files restructured on main such as src/tron/CMakeLists.txt (the file that gates amx_attn.cpp on TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, where the child's TRON_K_VNNI block lands)."

source re-grader (Partly): The corrected recommendation asked child step 2 to say at which main commit the historical merge check was made (98bb8cb22f94), to re-run git merge-tree or a trial rebase at rebase time, to list the files changed on both sides, and to give auto-merged files a semantic review, naming build files and headers restructured on main. The design now has the re-measure instruction: "At port time, remeasure shared files with git diff --name-only and conflicts with git merge-tree against the recorded current main/parent and saved child head. The historical check found an include conflict in common.hpp. It does not predict the final conflict set. Review self_attention.hpp semantically even when Git merges it automatically" [design-r3.txt:389]. That is the substance of the finding, and the common.hpp conflict claim matches the round-1 F15 evidence (one conflict hunk in the common.hpp include block at 98bb8cb2) [r1-findings.md, F15 Evidence]. Two concrete parts of the recommendation are missing. First, the sentence does not say which commit "the historical check" used. The design dates 98bb8cb22f94 only in the revision table [design-r3.txt:148] and never links that commit to the merge check, so an implementer cannot tell whether the check was made at f46e48ba, 98bb8cb2 or 2880c3aa9b. Second, the semantic-review instruction names only self_attention.hpp. The recommendation asked for auto-merged build files and headers restructured on main, and the concrete case is src/tron/CMakeLists.txt, which the design never names (grep of design-r3.txt for "CMakeLists" hits only t/CMakeLists.txt at line 152). Main commit 0128331632 ("cmake: compile model specializations per architecture", 2026-09-21 21:37 UTC, merged in 6fc67383a5 at 2026-09-22 00:53 UTC) changed 130 lines of that file. It is not an ancestor of 98bb8cb22f94 and is an ancestor of 2880c3aa9b (git merge-base --is-ancestor). The child adds 16 lines to the same file, a TRON_K_VNNI block that requires TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, directly after the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH block [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt, git diff c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb]. The files changed on both sides since c7844ca2ce grew from 10 at 98bb8cb2 to 11 at 2880c3aa9b and stay 11 at live main 1400fa4481 (comm -12 of the two git diff --name-only lists). The alternative "or a trial rebase in a scratch worktree" is also absent, which is minor. Section 9 says "Remeasure shared files and conflicts against the final parent scope at port time" and "The old common.hpp conflict is historical evidence only" [design-r3.txt:523], which matches the body. Residual severity: minor. Correction: Suggested text to add after the common.hpp sentence at design-r3.txt:389: "That check was made against main 98bb8cb22f94 with git merge-tree. At rebase time, re-run git merge-tree <parent-head> <old-child-head>, or a trial rebase in a scratch worktree, and review every auto-merged file that main restructured, including src/tron/CMakeLists.txt (the file that gates amx_attn.cpp on TRON_AMX_DISPATCH and that the child extends with its TRON_K_VNNI block), not only self_attention.hpp." Do not bake the eleven-file list into the design; main moves before the rebase.

fairness re-grader (Partly): The core re-measure instruction is now present. design-r3.txt:389: "At port time, remeasure shared files with git diff --name-only and conflicts with git merge-tree against the recorded current main/parent and saved child head. The historical check found an include conflict in common.hpp. It does not predict the final conflict set." That covers re-running git merge-tree at rebase time with the parent head and the saved child head as operands, listing the files changed on both sides, and not treating the old result as final. It also deliberately omits the dated eleven-file list at 2880c3aa9b, which the intent lens said not to bake in. Section 9 row design-r3.txt:523 ("Remeasure shared files and conflicts against the final parent scope at port time", "The old common.hpp conflict is historical evidence only", link #child) matches this body text. Two concrete parts of the corrected recommendation are missing. (1) The commit of the historical measurement. The hash 98bb8cb2 appears at design-r3.txt:148 (section 3 revision table) and :576 (S12 rule-file identity), and neither place ties it to the merge check. (2) The semantic-review rule for auto-merged files still names one file: "Review self_attention.hpp semantically even when Git merges it automatically" (design-r3.txt:389), the same sentence as round 2 (design-wdiff.txt:1268-1300 shows only rewording). The intent lens asked for the general rule "give the auto-merged ones (build files and headers restructured on main) a semantic review before rework"; the motivating case was src/tron/CMakeLists.txt (130 main-side lines from 0128331632, the file that gates amx_attn.cpp on TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, to which the child adds a 16-line TRON_K_VNNI block; r2-findings.md:433-434), which auto-merges and is not covered by the design's sentence. Severity minor, as in round 2: the remeasure instruction prevents the wrong build, and the two gaps affect how carefully the implementer reads the auto-merged result. Suggested one-sentence fix at design-r3.txt:389: "That check was made at main 98bb8cb22f94. Give every auto-merged file that main restructured after the common ancestor, including build files such as src/tron/CMakeLists.txt, a semantic review before rework." Correction: The checker's evidence quote for N30 is complete. One clarification: the design's merge-tree operands are given in prose ("the recorded current main/parent and saved child head"), not as a command line; that is adequate, since the round-2 F15 fairness correction (r2-findings.md:876) asked only that the parent head be the merge target. The F15 point that one merge-tree conflict hunk is a lower bound on rebase stops (a rebase replays the child's 22 commits one at a time, r1-findings.md F15 correction 1) is not in design-r3.txt:389 either; it belongs to F15, not to N30, so it does not change this grade.

Checker assessment: The substance of the corrected recommendation is present and every checkable fact in the body text is right. One concrete part of the recommendation is missing: the name of the required CI check that runs the Haskell tests. Facts checked, all at 30c4ac82cb (the child): - Two overload pairs exist. save_k_helper: operation_ix template form at model.hpp:2952-2959 and descriptor form at :2961-2989. save_k: operation_ix form at :3064-3070 ("size_t n_workers = 1") and descriptor form at :3072-3079. The design's "both existing save_k/save_k_helper overload pairs: the operation-index pair and the descriptor pair" matches. - The worker-0 duties in the shared case match save_k_impl model.hpp:3009-3058: k_store_cut_units (:3013) and opened.fetch_add (:3017) = window setup; the main thread also claims units (:3018-3023) = block claims; the join loop (:3026-3038); mark_k_complete (:3049); credit_gof_save (:3053); upstream_kvs_ready.count_down (:3058). - The helper side matches save_k_helper model.hpp:2967-2988: if constexpr (!k_vnni::layout_on<...>) return; (:2967), if (!k_store_shared<geometry>(q_batch, n_workers)) return; (:2970), the range assert worker_ix >= 1 && worker_ix < n_workers (:2973-2975), wait for the window (:2976-2979), claim loop (:2981-2986), finished.fetch_add (:2987), no completion marks. k_store_shared itself checks layout_on (:2807). So "First preserve the existing layout_on and k_store_shared checks" and the two-case description are right. - The serial case matches: worker 0 calls store_k_block(0, n_items) at :3040 and then the completion loop. - Generator: run() is Method "run" (TronCpp.hs:1169) and holds n_workers in scope (:1217 calls run_main_help(q_batches, 1 + i, n_workers)); saveKv emits "save_k" with [key, n_workers] (:2405-2408). run_main_help is Method "run_main_help" (:1273) with params worker_ix, n_workers (:1283) and concatenates runHelperStatement (:1281), which emits "save_k_helper" with [key, worker_ix, n_workers] (:2337-2340). So "run() passes 0, n_workers" and "run_main_help passes worker_ix, n_workers" describe the merged shape correctly. - Test files: LoopyTronSpec.hs:2801-2818 asserts the main call text "q_batch->outer_batch,k,n_workers);" and the helper text "q_batch->outer_batch,k,worker_ix,n_workers);"; :3225-3232 asserts ",k,n_workers);" and ",k,worker_ix,n_workers);" a second time. t_llama_unit.cpp:2772-2784 is the three-thread SECTION calling save_k_helper from std::thread helpers and save_k with N_WORKERS_3. The design names both files. - "Search all old positional calls, which passed only n_workers": needed, because with save_k(..., worker_ix = 0, n_workers = 1) an old three-argument call save_k(q_batch, ks, N) would compile and bind N to worker_ix (the runtime assert "index below that count" would then fire). The sentence covers this trap. - bin/ingest-cabal exists at 2880c3aa9b and runs cabal "$@" in ingest/ (bin/ingest-cabal:1-5), so "Run bin/ingest-cabal test" runs the Haskell tests locally. - The three residual guesses named by the intent-lens verifier are all answered: (a) the helper entry points are deleted (:420); (b) the main thread passes 0 (:424); (c) the assert becomes "a positive worker count and an index below that count" (:420). What is missing: the lead's recommendation said "Run the ingest tests (required 'Test ingest' check)" and the design-text verifier asked to note that the same tests run in CI in the required Test ingest job's "Run Haskell ingest tests" step. The design names only the local command. "ingest" appears only at design-r3.txt:390 and :424; neither section 8 nor the CI-ownership subsection mentions the ingest check. The step exists at gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:235-238 (nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux."tron-ingest:test:ingest-tests"), and "Test ingest" is in the required list at README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:76-79 (facts-r3.md:75). An implementer should know that a wrong generated call text blocks the child at a required check, not only at a local run. Separately, the fix added evidence row S18 whose two generator links carry swapped labels (see new_defect).

Still needed: Append to design-r3.txt:424 one sentence such as: "The required Test ingest CI job runs the same Haskell tests in its Run Haskell ingest tests step (gcp-nix.yml: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.\"tron-ingest:test:ingest-tests\"), so a wrong generated call text blocks the child at a required check."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked for a section-7 sentence that names the reference form the parent PR body uses for issue #4525 ("Part of #4525", no closing keyword) and says who closes the issue and when (the user, after #4424 is rebased, or earlier if the user splits the issue). Line 120 repeats it and gives the closure rule ("The assignee closes the issue after ... or explicitly splits that work into another issue"), and 499 keeps issue completion out of the parent's definition of done. "Part of" is not one of GitHub's closing keywords (close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved), so the parent's merge leaves #4525 open, which is the behavior the finding wanted. One checkable fact in the fix is wrong: lines 107 and 120 call the issue's remaining work its "child-adaptation checklist". Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:288 "No new packed slice or iterator API. No generic row.set, set_pair, matrix.set, or owner expression constructor/assignment. No runtime shapes, general transpose, or V plane-copy helper. Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged." design-r3.txt:290 "The existing generic expression-slice fallback can accept an lvalue packed view. It captures that view by reference, so the view and owner must outlive the slice. Do not pass a temporary packed view or use the owner overload: that overload creates a temporary view internally. This proposal adds no lifetime guarantee for that existing fallback. Ordinary tensors may still copy from a packed matrix expression. [S15]" design-r3.txt:579 "| S15 | Type and expression boundaries. Pinned round-2 main sources. ... [Owner slice wrapper] [Generic expression slice] ..." whose links are slice.hpp#L38-L42 and slice.hpp#L147-L177 at 2880c3aa9b (design-r3-links.tsv:196-197). Section 9, design-r3.txt:541 "| F08 F34 F37 | Defer unneeded writes, slices, and iterators. Remove unused V plane copying. State generic-slice lifetime limits. [Design section] | K expression is retained as a named compatibility proposal, not a production need. |" ([Design section] goes to #api, which exists).

Checker assessment: The round-2 residual asked for one sentence naming the generic slice path (slice.hpp:147-177), its by-reference capture, the rule not to pass a temporary view or go through the Owner& overload (slice.hpp:38-42), the statement that slice.hpp stays as is with no deleted overload, and the narrowing of the claim that the lifetime questions are removed. The re-grader corrections strengthened one point: the Owner& overload dangles for any owner, lvalue or not, so the text must forbid the owner spelling outright. The new paragraph at :290 does this. "It captures that view by reference" names the hazard. "Do not pass a temporary packed view or use the owner overload: that overload creates a temporary view internally" forbids the owner overload without a temporary-only qualifier, which is the re-grader's corrected wording. The S15 links pin both overloads by line at 2880c3aa9b. "Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged" (:288) rules out any new slice::operator() overload, deleted or not, because those are members declared only in that header. "This proposal adds no lifetime guarantee for that existing fallback" states the choice. The previous revision's inaccurate sentence "This scope decision removes the unneeded odd-boundary slice-write and temporary-slice lifetime questions" (design-revised-text.txt:277) was removed rather than narrowed; grep for "lifetime question" and "odd-boundary" in design-r3.txt finds nothing, so no wrong claim survives. Section 8 (:435-443) has no "How long slices remain valid" row, as round 1 asked. Facts checked against source, h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp@2880c3aa9b (git diff --stat shows the file unchanged from f46e48bab498 to 2880c3aa9b and from 2880c3aa9b to live main 1400fa4481, so the pinned lines hold): - :38-42 template <typename Owner, typename... Offset> requires requires(Owner& owner) { owner.as_view(); } auto operator()(Owner& owner, size_t offset0, Offset... offsets) { return (*this)(owner.as_view(), offset0, offsets...); } forwards the prvalue returned by as_view(). The design's "that overload creates a temporary view internally" is right. - :147-177 operator()(expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in, ...) with auto f = [=, &v_in](size_t i) {...} at :168-169 and the comment "It's critical that v_in be captured by reference here." The design's "captures that view by reference" is right. - The by-value overloads at :53 (view<T,aligned,dma,seq<...>,sseq<...>>) and :90 (const_view<...>) and the const_views overload at :125 cannot bind v_vnni_view, because the design gives it no views<> base (:241) and no pointer conversion (:248). So the expr const& overload is the only viable one for the packed view, and the owner-overload warning is needed for lvalue owners as well; the design's unqualified wording covers that case.

source re-grader (Resolved): The round-2 residual asked for one added statement in Explicitly deferred: the existing generic expression slice accepts an lvalue packed view through its rank-2 expr base and captures it by reference, do not pass a temporary view or the owner (the Owner& overload forwards a temporary view), slice.hpp stays unchanged and no deleted overload is added, and the old claim that the lifetime questions are removed must be narrowed. fairness re-grader (Resolved): The round-2 residual asked for one caveat sentence and the removal of an over-claim. design-r3.txt:290 adds the caveat: "The existing generic expression-slice fallback can accept an lvalue packed view. Resolved N02. TRON_IGNORE_NAN on in every non-Debug build; NaN row build-dependent (round 2, grade Major)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:331 "Packed append truncates fp32 to its upper 16 bits. Generic fp32s_to_bf16s also truncates, but preserves a NaN with only discarded mantissa bits when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent. That correction sets the lowest retained mantissa bit, not necessarily the quiet-NaN bit. All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds. Preserve the behavior selected by the actual macro. [S7][S17]" design-r3.txt:333-334 "| Independent input bits | Packed append | Generic conversion, macro absent | Generic conversion, macro defined |" / "| fp32 0x7F800001 : NaN with upper seven mantissa bits zero | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity | bf16 0x7F81 : NaN | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity |" design-r3.txt:336 "Only the generic conversion changes with the macro. Branch test expectations on #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN. The fp16 input path keeps its existing hardware conversion behavior." design-r3.txt:437 (section 8 Bits row) "Keep packed append expectations separate from generic conversion. Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN , using section 6's bit table. Check Debug and non-Debug builds for the two policies." design-r3.txt:455 "| NaN-preserving Debug check, 16 lanes | cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug | Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target, or build with cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit after Debug configuration. Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo. Checker assessment: The corrected (minor) recommendation asked for two things: one sentence saying when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined, and a note in the section 8 Bits row that generic NaN expectations depend on the macro. Both are in the body, and every checkable fact in them is right. Facts checked: - "All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro": src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-294 target_compile_options(tron PUBLIC "$<$<AND:${CXX_GccOrClang},$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>>:-O3;-DTRON_IGNORE_NAN;-DTRON_IGNORE_FTZ>" "$<$<AND:${CXX_GccOrClang},$<CONFIG:Debug>>:-O0>"), repeated at :314-318 for tron_model_compile_config. CXX_GccOrClang is $<COMPILE_LANG_AND_ID:CXX,AppleClang,Clang,GNU> (CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:74). RIGHT. - "native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds": CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37 (preset native, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo); nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo. RIGHT. - Bit table: h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:93-108 (16-lane) and :57-73 (8-lane), file identical to f46e48ba: with the macro the value is truncated as is; without it, lanes whose exponent field equals 0x7f800000 and whose low 16 bits are nonzero get 0x00010000 ORed in before the shift. 0x7F800001 -> 0x7F81 (macro absent) / 0x7F80 (macro defined). Packed float set_v is _mm512_srli_epi32(..., 16) (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2382) -> 0x7F80. "upper seven mantissa bits zero" is right: fp32 mantissa bits 22-16 of 0x7F800001 are zero. RIGHT. - "Only the generic conversion changes with the macro": git grep TRON_IGNORE_NAN 2880c3aa9b hits bf16.hpp, fp8 headers, emulation/debug.hpp and the CMake files only; kv_cache.hpp has no use. RIGHT. - The #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN test guidance works because the option is PUBLIC on tron and t_llama_unit links tron (t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:190 target_link_libraries("${TEST_NAME}" PRIVATE ${TEST_LIBRARIES}), :586-587 LIBRARIES tron pos_fake). The design does not state PUBLIC; that is F41's residual, not N02's. - Debug row: CMakePresets.json:89/102/114 (asan, tsan, coverage) are Debug. The design does not name those presets or the deb preset (:74, RelWithDebInfo). It supplies its own Debug configuration (-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug on the command line overrides the preset's cache variable). The general rule "all non-Debug" covers the unnamed presets, and no section 8 configuration uses them, so this omission does not change what an implementer builds. - Section 9 row 513 matches the body text.

New defect raised by the checker (minor): Claim: the new Debug configuration row tells the agent to "Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target" (design-r3.txt:455). That command changes the build type only when Make re-runs the CMake configure step, and Make re-runs it only when the gen/config/test stamp is stale. Source: GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:880-881 gen/t_%: gen/config/test $(HEADERS) $(SOURCES) runs only cmake --build gen --target $(notdir $@); the configure recipe cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ... is the rule body of gen/config/test (:538-543) and runs only when a prerequisite is newer than the stamp; gen/.preset_stamp (:299-303) records CMAKE_PRESET only, not BUILD_TYPE. So in a gen/ that was already configured as RelWithDebInfo, make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit keeps the cached RelWithDebInfo and TRON_IGNORE_NAN stays defined; the agent would then test the macro-defined policy while believing it tested the Debug policy. Mitigation already in the design: "Use a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair" (design-r3.txt:449) and "Confirm the macro is absent" (:455), so the risk is low. Also the sentence "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo" (:455) describes the same stamp mechanism incompletely: a later plain make restores RelWithDebInfo only when the stamp is stale. Recommendation: change the row to "Run make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit only in a freshly configured gen/ (delete gen/config/test first); the Make configure recipe re-runs only when that stamp is stale, and gen/.preset_stamp records the preset, not the build type. Confirm the macro is absent in compile_commands.json before running."

source re-grader (Resolved): The design now states when TRON_IGNORE_NAN (the compile-time switch that disables the NaN correction in the SIMD bf16 conversion) is defined and gives exact expected bits per policy. design-r3.txt:331 says all non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds. This is right: src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 and :314-318 add -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN under $<AND:${CXX_GccOrClang},$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>> as a PUBLIC option of tron, CXX_GccOrClang is COMPILE_LANG_AND_ID:CXX,AppleClang,Clang,GNU [CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:74], the native preset is RelWithDebInfo [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37], and the Nix test build passes -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80]. No other CMake file defines the macro for tests (git grep at 2880c3aa9b: only src/tron and src/rinzler CMakeLists plus #ifdef consumers). The bit table at design-r3.txt:333-334 is right: for fp32 0x7F800001 the packed append shifts right 16 bits and stores 0x7F80 (+infinity); the generic fp32s_to_bf16s without the macro ORs 0x00010000 where the exponent field is 0x7F800000 and the low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts, giving 0x7F81 (a NaN); with the macro it shifts only, giving 0x7F80 [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-109, unchanged from f46e48ba]. The section 8 test row at design-r3.txt:437 now selects generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN and asks for both build types, and design-r3.txt:336 repeats the branch rule. The Debug configuration row at design-r3.txt:455 is executable: a -D after --preset overrides the preset cache variable; GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80 sets BUILD_TYPE := RelWithDebInfo, which a command-line make variable overrides, and :541 passes -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) to the configure step; gen/t_% at :880-881 runs cmake --build gen --target. Section 9 row design-r3.txt:513 matches the body. The recommendation's preset names (deb, asan, tsan, coverage) and the word PUBLIC are not spelled out, but the stated rule (all non-Debug builds) covers them, so this is not a missing piece. Correction: Note, no status change: GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:299-305 writes only $(CMAKE_PRESET) into gen/.preset_stamp, and gen/config/test (:538-543) is remade only when a prerequisite changes, so make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit in an already-configured gen/ does not reconfigure and builds the RelWithDebInfo tree. The design's separate-worktree rule (design-r3.txt:447) and the instruction 'Confirm the macro is absent' (design-r3.txt:455) cover this trap, and its second form (configure Debug, then cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit) avoids it. The row could say 'configure Debug first' in one clause.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked for three things. (1) A sentence saying when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined. The design now says: "All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds. Preserve the behavior selected by the actual macro." [design-r3.txt:331]. This is right: src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 adds -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN under $<AND:${CXX_GccOrClang},$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>> as a PUBLIC option of tron, and CXX_GccOrClang is COMPILE_LANG_AND_ID:CXX,AppleClang,Clang,GNU [CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:74]. The native preset is RelWithDebInfo [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37]. The Nix test build is RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80]. (2) Exact bits per path and policy. The bit table gives fp32 0x7F800001 -> packed 0x7F80 (+infinity), generic without macro 0x7F81 (NaN), generic with macro 0x7F80 [design-r3.txt:333-334]. I recomputed this from h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:93-108: without the macro the code masks lanes whose exponent field is 0x7f800000 and whose low 16 bits are nonzero, ORs 0x00010000, then shifts right by 16, so 0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F81; with the macro it only shifts, giving 0x7F80. Packed truncation also gives 0x7F80. The table is right. (3) The section 8 test row must warn about the build dependence. The Bits row now says: "Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN, using section 6's bit table. Check Debug and non-Debug builds for the two policies." [design-r3.txt:437]. A Debug configuration row was added [design-r3.txt:455], and the section 9 row matches the body [design-r3.txt:513]. The recommendation also named the deb preset and the Debug presets asan, tsan and coverage. The design does not name them. It gives a Debug native configuration instead (cmake --preset native ... -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug), which yields the same macro-absent policy, because a command-line -D overrides a preset cache variable. That omission is note-level and changes no implementation step. Correction: Two note-level facts for the Debug row [design-r3.txt:455]. (a) The row offers "make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target". The Make configure stamp tracks only the preset name, not BUILD_TYPE [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:299-303], and gen/config/test reruns cmake only when its prerequisites change [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538-541]. The gen/t_% recipe only runs cmake --build [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:880-881]. So in an already configured gen/ that command keeps RelWithDebInfo without reconfiguring. The design's separate-worktree rule [design-r3.txt:449] and "Confirm the macro is absent" [design-r3.txt:455] cover this. One sentence saying the stamp does not track BUILD_TYPE would make it explicit. (b) The design never says the option is PUBLIC. The #ifdef in test code works only because t_llama_unit links tron [t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:586-592] and inherits the PUBLIC option. The instruction is right; the reason is implicit.

Apply the V owner's lvalue-only as_view(), const conversion, and private packed-pointer rules to K too." design-r3.txt:405-407 (typed store_row / load_row; store_block(writable_k_view, block, mask, rows); typed K token copies and a typed K plane-copy operation; k_vnni_view<const bf16,64,128> by value to qk_vnni_128x4 and the corresponding shape to qk_group). Section 9: design-r3.txt:544 lists C07.

Checker assessment: The round-2 residual asked for one decision: what the index anchors call after the K mapping moves, with one spelling picked (public constexpr k_vnni::index in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, or a static member of k_vnni_view). The re-graders added two precisions: the byte-position checks call the same function, and prefill/poison writes and plane-to-plane copies need a stated form. The decision is made. Line 391 keeps k_vnni::index as "the existing constexpr free function", moves it into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, and keeps its spelling. Source: constexpr size_t index(size_t token, size_t dim) noexcept in namespace tron::k_vnni [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:42, 101-107, 310]. The STATIC_REQUIRE anchors (Catch2's compile-time assertion) call it by that name [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:80 using tron::k_vnni::index;, 81-90]. The byte-position checks call the same name [:120 tron::k_vnni::index(tok, d), :143]. "Keep the function spelling" therefore covers both callers, even though line 391 names only "the independent index checks". Poison and prefill writes. Line 416 chooses 64 typed row saves. This is the first option round-2 N57 offered, and it is bit-exact because scatter_row moves 32-bit lanes without float conversion [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139-146] and line 405 keeps those instructions. It replaces the direct plane writes at t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:107-109, 190-192, 286-288. Plane-to-plane copies. The test copies one plane into another with memcpy [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:193, 216]. Line 401 makes the K owner trivially copyable with the V owner's rules, and line 239 keeps same-type copy defaulted for V, so an owner-to-owner assignment is available. The design does not spell this as a sentence, but it follows directly from the stated traits, and this precision was an addition by the re-grader rather than part of the round-1 ask. The four raw-pointer call kinds in the child test (scatter_row :113, 139, 199, 214, 226, 291; gather_row :129, 232; store_block :201, 228; qk_group :306-309) map onto the typed operations named at design-r3.txt:405-407. Line 416 keeps the ban on the internal friend helper. Line 416 does not force stack allocation, so the heap fixtures at :99, 173-174, 262 may stay. Every checkable fact in the fix is right.
