Resolved F41. NaN divergence between set_v truncation and generic conversion unstated (round 1, grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:331 "Generic fp32s_to_bf16s also truncates, but preserves a NaN with only discarded mantissa bits when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent. That correction sets the lowest retained mantissa bit, not necessarily the quiet-NaN bit. All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds. Preserve the behavior selected by the actual macro." design-r3.txt:334 "| fp32 0x7F800001 : NaN with upper seven mantissa bits zero | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity | bf16 0x7F81 : NaN | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity |" design-r3.txt:336 "Expected bit patterns from the source conversion rules, not measured test results. Only the generic conversion changes with the macro. Branch test expectations on #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN." design-r3.txt:437 "Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN , using section 6's bit table. Check Debug and non-Debug builds for the two policies." design-r3.txt:549 (section 9) "| F41 | Correct the fp32 NaN example and select generic expectations by the actual build macro. [Design section] | No new NaN behavior is requested. Test both policies. |"

Checker assessment: The round-2 residual had three parts plus two re-grader additions. Three parts are now in the body and are factually right; the two additions are missing. Present and verified: 1. Worked example: the table row (design-r3.txt:334) gives 0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 (packed) / 0x7F81 (generic, macro absent) / 0x7F80 (generic, macro defined). Checked against h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:93-108 (OR 0x00010000 where exponent field == 0x7f800000 and low 16 bits != 0, then shift right 16) and kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2382 (_mm512_srli_epi32(..., 16) in the float set_v). "upper seven mantissa bits zero" correctly replaces the loose "no upper mantissa bits" (fp32 mantissa bits 22-16). RIGHT. 2. Build-type sentence: "All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds" (design-r3.txt:331) matches src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-294, CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37 and nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80. The plain direction ("outside Debug both paths truncate identically") is carried by the table's last column and by "Only the generic conversion changes with the macro" (:336). RIGHT. 3. Test-row guidance: design-r3.txt:437 tells the author to branch generic NaN expectations on #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN and to run both build types; the Debug configuration exists at :455. This is the first branch of the residual's either/or. RIGHT. 4. Section 9 row 549 now matches the body (the example exists), which closes the fairness re-grader's point. Missing (the re-grader additions): (a) The design never says the macro is a PUBLIC compile option of the tron target, so a reader may think only library code is affected. Source: src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292 target_compile_options(tron PUBLIC ...); t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:190 links each test PRIVATE to its LIBRARIES, and t_llama_unit lists tron (:586-587). The design's #ifdef guidance works only because of this propagation. (b) The existing precedent t/t_bf16.cpp@2880c3aa9b:97-110 ("bf16 preserves nan", comment "this test may fail on some hardware if IGNORE_NAN is set", NaNs built from inf - inf) is not named, and the advice "use quiet NaNs for expectations shared by both paths; put the signalling case 0x7F800001 only on the packed append path" is absent. Because the design chose the #ifdef branch, (b) is helpful rather than required. Both omissions are low risk: an implementer following :437 and :455 builds the right tests.

Still needed: Add after the sentence at design-r3.txt:331 "All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro ...": "TRON_IGNORE_NAN is a PUBLIC compile option of the tron target [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-295 @2880c3aa9b], so test executables that link tron, including t_llama_unit [t/CMakeLists.txt:586-587], compile with it too; an #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN in test code therefore sees the same value as the library." Optionally add to the Bits row (design-r3.txt:437): "Precedent: t/t_bf16.cpp:97-110 (\"bf16 preserves nan\") avoids the build dependence by using quiet NaNs (inf - inf). Use quiet NaNs for expectations shared by both paths; put the signalling case 0x7F800001 only on the packed append path, which always truncates."

source re-grader (Resolved): Round 1 asked for the exact NaN divergence rule, the fp32 worked example, and a warning that expected bits differ per path and per build type; the round-1 verifiers withdrew the fp16 example. All three parts are now in the body. Rule: design-r3.txt:331 says packed append truncates fp32 to its upper 16 bits, the generic fp32s_to_bf16s also truncates but sets the lowest retained mantissa bit (not necessarily the quiet bit) when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent, and all non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro. This matches bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-109 (OR 0x00010000, which becomes bf16 bit 0 after the 16-bit shift) and src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295. Worked example: design-r3.txt:333-334 gives fp32 0x7F800001 (upper seven mantissa bits, fp32 bits 22-16, zero) -> packed 0x7F80 (+infinity), generic without macro 0x7F81 (NaN), generic with macro 0x7F80; I recomputed all three and they are right. Test guidance: design-r3.txt:336 ('Branch test expectations on #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN') and the section 8 row at design-r3.txt:437 ('Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN, using section 6's bit table. Check Debug and non-Debug builds'). The fp16 example is dropped; design-r3.txt:336 says only that the fp16 input path keeps its existing hardware conversion, which is right (VCVTPH2PS quiets a signalling NaN, so no fp16 NaN becomes infinity on either path). The section 9 row at design-r3.txt:549 ('Correct the fp32 NaN example and select generic expectations by the actual build macro') now describes what the body contains, closing the round-2 fairness point that the earlier row claimed an example that did not exist. Correction: Two optional additions from the round-2 re-graders were not adopted and are not required: (1) the word PUBLIC (that test executables linking tron inherit the macro) is implied by 'all non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro' but not stated; (2) the existing precedent t/t_bf16.cpp@2880c3aa9b:97-99 ('bf16 preserves nan' uses quiet NaNs from inf-inf and 0/0 and its comment warns that IGNORE_NAN can change the result) is not named. The design's #ifdef branch is a valid alternative to that precedent.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The round-2 residual asked for three things. (1) A worked example replacing "an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits". The bit table now reads "fp32 0x7F800001 : NaN with upper seven mantissa bits zero | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity | bf16 0x7F81 : NaN | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity" [design-r3.txt:333-334]. I checked the bits: 0x7F800001 has exponent 0xFF and mantissa 0x000001, so mantissa bits 22 to 16 are zero and the value is a signalling NaN. Truncation to the upper 16 bits gives 0x7F80 (+infinity). fp32s_to_bf16s without the macro ORs 0x00010000 [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:106] and shifts right by 16 [108], giving 0x7F81. With the macro it gives 0x7F80. The sentence "That correction sets the lowest retained mantissa bit, not necessarily the quiet-NaN bit" [design-r3.txt:331] is right (bit 16 of fp32 versus bit 22). (2) A sentence that the macro is defined for every non-Debug build including the RelWithDebInfo Nix test build. Present at design-r3.txt:331, verified against src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 and nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80. (3) A test-row warning that generic NaN bits depend on the build type, with a guard or a restriction. The Bits row chooses the guard: "Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN ... Check Debug and non-Debug builds" [design-r3.txt:437], and a Debug configuration row exists [design-r3.txt:455]. The fairness re-grader's point is also addressed: the section 9 row "Correct the fp32 NaN example" [design-r3.txt:549] now describes a body that contains the example, and the direction is plain because the "macro defined" column equals the packed column. The withdrawn fp16 example stays out: "The fp16 input path keeps its existing hardware conversion behavior" [design-r3.txt:336]. Two optional additions from the round-2 re-graders were not taken: the word PUBLIC (the option's scope) is not stated, and the precedent test "bf16 preserves nan" that uses quiet NaNs only [t/t_bf16.cpp@2880c3aa9b:97-100] is not named. Both were offered as alternatives, not requirements, so they are not residuals.

Resolved N09. Q3 omits reviewer's reason for excluding operator[] (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:97 "| Q3. May packed views expose logical rows through operator[] ? | Yes. The sketch excluded indexing because it suggests a contiguous row. The expression interface requires row indexing. Return a logical row with no public pointer and no views<> base. Keep bounds-checked at() . Apply the same expression-read proposal to the child. | ..." design-r3.txt:240 "A row stores its pair address and parity by value." design-r3.txt:241 "The packed types have no DMA template parameter or static DMA flag. ... Do not inherit views<>, whose leaf rows must be contiguous." design-r3.txt:248 "Owners, views, and rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion. Rows are constructed only by the matrix view." design-r3.txt:245 "matrix[token][dimension] , matrix.at(token, dimension) | Assert bounds using repository assertions."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked the Q3 answer to carry the sketch's reason, the expression base's need for operator[], a rebuttal that says the row exposes no public pointer (not "has no data pointer") and does not rest on dma = false, and the retention of bounds-checked at(). Line 97 has each part. "The sketch excluded indexing because it suggests a contiguous row" matches Ben's sentence "There is no data(), pointer conversion, or operator[] that suggests a contiguous row." [github-review.json, comment 5765866077]. "The expression interface requires row indexing" is right: both expr::operator[] overloads return self()[i], so a derived type must supply operator[] [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:57-65]. "No public pointer" is the narrow claim the source-lens correction asked for; the row keeps a private pair address (240) and the public-surface rule is at 248. "No views<> base" is true: a rank-1 view never inherits views<> [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@f46e48bab498:113-117, comment "views is not a superclass of a rank-1 view"], and the design's matrix view also does not inherit it (241); two of the three verifier-suggested answers used this phrase, so it is accepted. dma = false is no longer used as a contiguity claim anywhere, because 241 removes the DMA flag from the packed types; that follows the views.hpp definition of dma as DMA-safety [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:11-15]. "Keep bounds-checked at()" matches 245. The expr.hpp citation is not inside the cell, but S2 links the expression source (566); the recommendation did not require an inline line number.

source re-grader (Resolved): The recommendation, as corrected by all three lenses, asked Q3 to state the reviewer's reason for excluding operator[], the design's rebuttal, and to avoid using dma = false as a contiguity claim. Q3 now reads: "Yes. The sketch excluded indexing because it suggests a contiguous row. The expression interface requires row indexing. Return a logical row with no public pointer and no views<> base. Keep bounds-checked at(). Apply the same expression-read proposal to the child." [design-r3.txt:97]. Facts checked: Ben's sketch says "There is no data(), pointer conversion, or operator[] that suggests a contiguous row." (github-review.json, comment 5765866077), so the stated reason is right. Resolved N13. bf16_chunk 'different signature silently selects conversion' is wrong (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:247 "| bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept | Use this non-template, non-overloaded signature to extract stored bits directly. A missing override uses the expression base's fp32 conversion fallback. A wrong signature can fail compilation; omitting noexcept does not silently select that fallback. Verify the member-pointer type. Do not claim the fallback corrupts stored bf16 bits. [S15] |" design-r3.txt:440 "| Expression reads: existing tensor/cache cases | Construct a host tensor from the packed matrix view. Check row chunks and exact bf16 copies with independent patterns. Check decltype(&Row::bf16_chunk) against bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept to distinguish the derived override from an inherited fallback. Use an existing hardware-tensor fixture only if it already accepts this input. | Broken expression compatibility or a missing direct-bit override. Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback. |" design-r3.txt:517 (section 9) "| N13 N49 N51 N52 N53 | Correct override/fallback behavior, ... [Design section] | Compile the contracts. ..." (link target #api = section 5). S15 link "[bf16 override detection]" -> h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp#L110-L117 @2880c3aa9b (design-r3-links.tsv).

Checker assessment: Both factual errors named by N13 are gone. The round-2 sentence "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" was replaced (design-wdiff.txt lines 597-603 show the OLD/NEW text). The word "lossy" was removed from the section-8 row (design-wdiff.txt lines 1613-1615). Facts checked in the new text: - "A missing override uses the expression base's fp32 conversion fallback": RIGHT. h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:111-117@2880c3aa9b reads if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) { return self().bf16_chunk(i); } else { return fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)); }. When B declares no bf16_chunk, both pointers name the base member and compare equal. - "A wrong signature can fail compilation": RIGHT and hedged as the verifier asked (a mismatched signature makes the != ill-formed at expr.hpp:112; the round-2 source-lens verifier noted g++ 11.4 and clang 19 differ on the noexcept-only case). - "omitting noexcept does not silently select that fallback": RIGHT per the intent-lens correction (either the override is used or the comparison is a compile error; never silent). - "Do not claim the fallback corrupts stored bf16 bits" and section 8 "bit-exact fallback": RIGHT. h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498 (identical at 2880c3aa9b and 1400fa4481) ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field == 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits != 0, then shifts right 16. After even_part (_mm512_slli_epi32(x, 16), kv_cache.hpp:2005-2007@2880c3aa9b) or odd_part (_mm512_and_epi32(x, hi_16_of_32), :2000-2002) the low 16 bits are zero, so the mask never fires and the original bits return. - The decltype check at :440 is a valid detector: when Row does not declare bf16_chunk, &Row::bf16_chunk has type bf16s (expr<Row,D>::*)(size_t) const noexcept, not bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept, so the comparison distinguishes the inherited fallback. This is the "static_assert" alternative the corrected recommendation allowed ("name the static_assert or the instruction record"). The design places it in the test suite instead of vnni.hpp; that location difference does not change what is detected. - S15's "[bf16 override detection]" link points at expr.hpp#L110-L117 @2880c3aa9b, the right lines. What is missing from the corrected recommendation: the cost clause. The recommendation's replacement text said the fallback "is bit-exact for stored bf16 but adds a shift, NaN check, and narrow per chunk", and the section-8 wording should read "(bit-exact, slower)". Neither :247 nor :440 states that the fallback costs anything (grep of design-r3.txt for "slower", "extra", "round trip" finds only :326, which is about append). Without it, a reader of :440 does not learn why a missing override matters at all. This is one explanatory clause; the actionable guidance (exact signature, decltype check) is correct and complete, so the risk of leaving it out is low.

Still needed: In design-r3.txt:247, after "A missing override uses the expression base's fp32 conversion fallback." add: "That fallback is bit-exact for stored bf16 but adds a shift, a NaN check, and a narrow per chunk [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109]." In design-r3.txt:440 change "Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback." to "Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback; it is slower, not wrong."

source re-grader (Resolved): The two factual errors are gone and every fact in the new text checks out against expr.hpp at 2880c3aa9b. The design row now says: a missing override uses the base's fp32 conversion fallback, a wrong signature can fail compilation, and omitting noexcept does not silently select the fallback [design-r3.txt:247]. That matches the base: expr<B,N>::bf16_chunk compares member-function pointers with if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) and only falls back to fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)) when B declares no bf16_chunk [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:111-116]. The noexcept wording follows the round-2 verifier hedge (either accepted as the override or a compile error, never silent). The word 'lossy' is gone; section 8 now says 'Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback' [design-r3.txt:440], and section 6 says bf16_chunk() preserves stored bits [design-r3.txt:328]. The detector the recommendation asked for is present: 'Check decltype(&Row::bf16_chunk) against bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept to distinguish the derived override from an inherited fallback' [design-r3.txt:440]. That check is sound: when Row does not declare the member, &Row::bf16_chunk names the base member and has type bf16s (expr<Row,D>::*)(size_t) const noexcept, so the types differ. The recommendation placed a static_assert in the header; the design places the check in the section-8 test row next to the STATIC_REQUIRE checks [design-r3.txt:438]. Both are compile-time, so the placement difference is acceptable. The S15 link '[bf16 override detection]' points at expr.hpp#L110-L117 at 2880c3aa9b, and those lines are exactly the bf16_chunk body [design-r3-links.tsv:195; expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:110-117]. Section 9 row 'Correct override/fallback behavior' matches the body change [design-r3.txt:517]. One small gap is graded under F35, not here: the design never says the fallback costs extra instructions (a shift, a NaN check and a narrow per chunk).

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The round-2 sentence "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" is gone [design-wdiff.txt:595-600]. The new contract row reads: use one non-template, non-overloaded bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept; a missing override uses the expression base's fp32 conversion fallback; a wrong signature can fail compilation; omitting noexcept does not silently select that fallback; verify the member-pointer type; do not claim the fallback corrupts stored bf16 bits [design-r3.txt:247]. Each statement matches the source. The base decides with if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:111-117], so only an absent member falls back silently. The noexcept sentence follows the hedged verifier correction (compile-time outcome either way, never a silent fallback). The bit-exact fact is carried by :247 and by "bf16_chunk() preserves stored bits" [design-r3.txt:328]; fp32s_to_bf16s changes bits only when the low 16 bits are nonzero [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-109], and even_part/odd_part leave them zero [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2000-2007]. Section 8 no longer says "lossy"; it says "Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback" and names the detector: compare decltype(&Row::bf16_chunk) (decltype = the C++ operator that yields an expression's type) with bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept [design-r3.txt:440]. That is the static_assert option the recommendation allowed. The test works: a member inherited from the base has type pointer-to-member-of-the-base, so the type comparison separates the derived override from the inherited fallback. The S15 link "bf16 override detection" resolves to expr.hpp#L110-L117 @2880c3aa9b [design-r3-links.tsv:195]. Section 9 row [design-r3.txt:517] has matching body text. Note level, no change required: the recommended clause naming the fallback's cost (one shift, one NaN check, one narrow per chunk) is not in the text; :247 says only "extract stored bits directly". The override is mandatory in the design and the check at :440 enforces it, so no implementation choice depends on that clause. The check lives in the test suite instead of v_vnni.hpp; the recommendation accepted either place.

A directive to the implementer is at least as strong as the requested factual statement, so I do not count it as missing. - One verifier suggested naming the slice<geometry.kv.head_size>()(vs[ix].as_view(), ...) construction at the model call site. New defect raised by the checker (note): Claim: the sentence "Dma preserves the existing contiguous view's DMA flag" [design-r3.txt:257] has nothing to preserve at two of the three migrated call sites, so the implementer must still choose the Dma value there. Evidence: the 16-lane model branch passes a raw pointer &vs[ix][kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size] [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832], and the GOF callback passes a raw bf16* dest [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2656]; only the 8-lane branch has an existing view, vs[ix].as_view() [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2834-2836], and tensor::as_view() carries dma = false [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:71-72, 35]. The packed bodies do not read the flag, so the choice has no behavioral effect. Recommendation: replace the sentence with "Dma is deduced from the caller's view. Where a call site wraps a raw pointer today (the model's 16-lane branch and the GOF scratch), construct the view with dma = false, the value tensor::as_view() carries."

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The recommendation asked for one rule: the packed append_v_row and load_row overloads, and the typed page::set_v/get_v wrappers, accept only aligned = true row views, the moved bodies keep their aligned loads and stores, today's callers satisfy this, and the heterogeneous fixture gains alignas(64). The design text now carries each part. The signature block fixes the alignment flag to true on both sides: const_view<Source, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> src and view<Destination, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> dst [design-r3.txt:255]. The rule is stated in words: "The shown alignment flag is true: preserve the existing aligned load/store contract and use 64-byte-aligned rows at every migrated call site. The flag describes a precondition; wrapping a pointer does not establish alignment. Add alignas(64) to the V fixture in t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp." [design-r3.txt:257]. The bodies are moved, not rewritten: "append_v_row moves today's packed set_v bodies" and "load_row moves today's get_v loops" [design-r3.txt:258-259]. Those bodies use aligned intrinsics (_mm256_load_epi32 at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2300 and :2308, _mm512_load_ps at :2380 and :2389, _mm512_store_ps at :2421 and :2430, _mm256_store_si256 at :2455 and :2463), so "preserve the existing aligned load/store contract" means keep them. The typed wrappers carry the same precondition: page::set_v takes "the aligned source row shown above" and page::get_v accepts "an aligned typed destination" [design-r3.txt:268-269]. Step 3 repeats it for the model call site [design-r3.txt:374]. The get_v caller's scratch is named as aligned [design-r3.txt:269]; that is right: gof.hpp@2880c3aa9b:62-63 documents "caller-owned, 64-byte-aligned scratch" and gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203 declares alignas(64) std::array<bf16, ...> v_scratch. The fixture fact is right: t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:441 declares std::array<float, 256> values; and the file contains no alignas. The view constructor fact is right: view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:124-126 stores the pointer with no alignment check. The design also dropped the claim that the section-8 instruction comparison would flag an aligned-to-unaligned swap, as the verifiers asked; section 8 no longer mentions it [design-r3.txt:483-490]. Section 9 row matches the body [design-r3.txt:519] and links to #api. One small difference from the recommended wording: the design does not state as a fact that today's production set_v source is already 64-byte aligned (model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832 offsets a chunk-aligned buffer by kv_head * head_size with head_size % 32 == 0). It lists "Verify every migrated caller meets the alignment precondition" as remaining work instead [design-r3.txt:519]. The rule is what the implementer needs, and the 8-lane branch kept unchanged at model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2834-2836 already shows the slice<head_size>()(vs[ix].as_view(), offset) construction that yields an aligned = true view (slice.hpp@2880c3aa9b:56-63 asserts the offset), so this is a note, not a missing piece.

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:273 "| page::scaled_v , detail::scaled_v_expr | Use a packed read-only V view in the 16-lane constructor. Use const_view<bf16,true,false,seq<page_size,head_size>,sseq<head_size,1>> in the 8-lane constructor, constructed internally from the block. | Keep scales, live count from page::count() , and scratch separate. The packed bound is (count + 1) / 2 * 2 . The row-major bound is count . Neither uses the view's static row count. |" design-r3.txt:329 "| scaled_v_expr | Keep the live count separate from the storage shape. Keep pair rounding only in the 16-lane packed path; the 8-lane row-major path reads exactly count rows. Preserve supported widths, weight conversion, unrolled loops, and addition order. Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation. |" design-r3.txt:298 "A packed-V weighted sum rounds an odd live-token count up to a complete pair. ... The row-major path reads exactly the live-token count. [S5]" design-r3.txt:213 "The packed scaled_v_expr supports 64, 128, 256, or 512 dimensions. The unchanged 8-lane path requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0." Section 9, design-r3.txt:520 "Type both weighted-sum constructors."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked the row to name the typed input of each build's constructor and to name page::count() as the count source. Both are now in the row at :273. The 16-lane input is "a packed read-only V view"; with :54 ("v_vnni_view accesses a packed V matrix") and :271 (return type v_vnni_view<const bf16,page_size,geometry.head_size>) that phrase maps to exactly one type. The 8-lane input is spelled in full. The count source is page::count(). The wrong reading feared in round 2 (handing the 8-lane constructor the packed view type) is excluded because the 8-lane type is spelled. Facts checked against source (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b, byte-identical through live main 1400fa4481 per facts-r3.md:42-43): - The 8-lane constructor today is scaled_v_expr(const tensor<page_size>& scales, const bf16s* data, const size_t count, tensor<head_size>& scratch) noexcept requires(head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0) (2139-2143). Its loop is for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) over data + i * (head_size / chunk_size) + part * 8 (2157-2159), so it is row-major and reads exactly count rows. The design's "row-major bound is count" and ":213 requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0" are right. - The 16-lane constructor takes the same raw const bf16s* data, requires head_size in {64,128,256,512}, and computes end = (count + 1) / 2 * 2 (2066-2078). The design's packed bound and width list are right. - page::scaled_v<geometry> passes kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[0], count() (2259-2261), so "live count from page::count()" and "constructed internally from the block" describe today's call. page::count() is documented "How many kv entries are live" (1483-1494), which is the source of the design's word "live". - The named 8-lane type is the existing row-major const view: kv_block::k_view() const returns const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<page_size, head_size>> (2214-2219). The defaulted fifth parameter is Stride = row_major<Dim> (views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:26,35), and row_major<seq<page_size,head_size>> expands to sseq<seq_stride<0,S>, seq_stride<1,S>> = sseq<head_size,1> (seq.hpp@2880c3aa9b:383-394). The 8-lane V array is bf16s v[page_size][head_size / chunk_size] (2200-2201), a row-major plane of that shape. So the explicit spelling at :273 is the same type as k_view() with no default relied on, matching the header rule at :234. - Terminology: the corrected recommendation allowed defining "live-token count" either in Words used here or in the row; :273 ties "live count" to page::count(). Words used here (:56) still has only "Valid token row", and :298 uses "live-token count". This is a note-level wording nit, not a gap the corrected recommendation required closing.

source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked the design to name the typed input of the 8-lane scaled_v_expr constructor, to say that the count comes from page::count(), and to define "live-token count" in Words used here or at the constructor row. The row now reads "Use a packed read-only V view in the 16-lane constructor. Use const_view<bf16,true,false,seq<page_size,head_size>,sseq<head_size,1>> in the 8-lane constructor, constructed internally from the block" and "Keep scales, live count from page::count(), and scratch separate. The packed bound is (count + 1) / 2 * 2. The row-major bound is count" [design-r3.txt:273]. Section 6 adds "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" [design-r3.txt:329]. The facts in the fix are right. Today's 8-lane constructor takes const bf16s* data and requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0 [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2139-2143], and the design states that width rule [design-r3.txt:213]. The 8-lane storage is bf16s v[page_size][head_size / chunk_size] [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2201], the same shape as k, whose const k_view() is const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<page_size, head_size>> [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2217]. The default stride row_major<seq<page_size, head_size>> expands to sseq<head_size, 1> [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp@2880c3aa9b:388-394], so the spelled 8-lane type is the existing row-major view type with its stride written out, matching the explicit-stride rule at [design-r3.txt:234]. page::scaled_v already passes count() [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2261], which is page::count() returning offset_bound [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1492]. The 16-lane constructor requires 64, 128, 256 or 512 dimensions and rounds the bound to (count + 1) / 2 * 2 [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2066-2078], as the design says [design-r3.txt:213, 273]. Section 9 says "Type both weighted-sum constructors" [design-r3.txt:520]. Correction: Wording note only, no status change: Words used here still defines only "Valid token row" [design-r3.txt:56], and the design uses "live-token count" [design-r3.txt:298] and "live count" [design-r3.txt:329, 436]. The first use ties "live count" to page::count() [design-r3.txt:273], which meets the recommendation's alternative of defining the term at the constructor row. Adding one Words row "live count: page::count(), the number of live tokens on the page" would remove the remaining gap.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): design-r3.txt:273 names the 8-lane constructor input exactly: "Use const_view<bf16,true,false,seq<page_size,head_size>,sseq<head_size,1>> in the 8-lane constructor, constructed internally from the block", and names the count source: "live count from page::count()". Those are the two pieces the source and intent lenses asked for. The type is right: the 8-lane V array is bf16s v[page_size][head_size / chunk_size] (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2201), the same shape kv_block::k_view() const already returns as const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<page_size, head_size>> (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2215-2219), and row_major<seq<page_size,head_size>> is sseq<head_size,1> (h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp@2880c3aa9b:388-394), so the explicit stride equals the default. The bounds sentence is right (16-lane end = (count + 1) / 2 * 2 at kv_cache.hpp:2078; 8-lane loop i < count at 2139-2175, facts-r2.md). The old raw const bf16s* data constructor (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2139-2143) is replaced by the typed view per design-r3.txt:273, and design-r3.txt:329 "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" closes the raw-pointer reading. The live-count term is defined at its first use in the body (design-r3.txt:273, "live count from page::count()"), which the intent lens accepted as an alternative to a Words row. The 16-lane input is written as "a packed read-only V view" rather than the spelled type, but the design's vocabulary (design-r3.txt:54) and the spelled type at design-r3.txt:271 make it unambiguous; the N24 ambiguity was the 8-lane type, which is now exact. Section 9 row design-r3.txt:520 "Type both weighted-sum constructors" matches the body. Note only: the Words table (design-r3.txt:23-56) still has no row for live-token count, and the text alternates "live count" (273, 329, 436) with "live-token count" (298).

Resolved N25. EAGLE bullet omits uniform-geometry requirement; misread as heterogeneous (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:349 "For uniform geometry, construct one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region. Its bound is the checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t). This matches the existing uniform accessor's indexing across slots." design-r3.txt:351 "EAGLE requires uniform geometry. The uniform retained-arena array already includes its final physical KV slot with the primary geometry. Do not add an EAGLE branch to heterogeneous enumeration. Reclaimable restoration must not reconstruct that retained slot. Do not touch x_data, the separate embedding buffer. [C01] [C09]" design-r3.txt:521 "| N25 M04 | Use existing geometry dispatch and filter by arena. Uniform construction includes EAGLE once. Heterogeneous enumeration has no EAGLE branch. [Design section] | Pinned-compiler construction and allocation/restore checks remain required. |" design-r3.txt:580 S16 "[EAGLE uniform-geometry requirement]" -> kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b#L771-L789 (design-r3-links.tsv:199). Removed text (design-wdiff.txt, OLD segment at old word 4160): "Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked the bullet to say four things and to keep two more. (1) EAGLE (the speculative model's extra cache slot) exists only with uniform geometry. (2) The uniform whole-arena array already covers the extra EAGLE KV slot, which sits in the retained arena. (3) The heterogeneous enumeration never meets an EAGLE slot. (4) Keep the x_data sentence. Verifiers added: place the EAGLE slot as the last primary-geometry slot of the retained arena; say it is constructed once because restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena; keep a qualified caution that for_each_active_slot omits the EAGLE offset; move the bullet after the uniform bullet. Facts checked in the new bullet (design-r3.txt:351), all RIGHT. "EAGLE requires uniform geometry": kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:771 eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0; :788-789 TRON_ASSERT "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage"; :1158-1159 calculate_allocation_sizes returns std::nullopt when support_eagle && !eagle_compatible. "The uniform retained-arena array already includes its final physical KV slot with the primary geometry": arena_sizes :717-719 adds offsets.values[1].total() to result.retained; storage_location :731-734 returns reclaimable = false for offset.i == logical_slot_count with byte_offset = the retained prefix, so the EAGLE slot is the last region of the retained arena; kv_block_at_storage :1328-1329 asserts geometry == layout_t::primary_geometry; the uniform bound of line 349 is retained_kv_bytes_ / sizeof(kv_block_t), and retained_kv_bytes_ = n_pages * unit retained (:1165) includes that slot. "Do not add an EAGLE branch to heterogeneous enumeration": follows from :1158-1159, because a heterogeneous layout with support_eagle never allocates. "Reclaimable restoration must not reconstruct that retained slot": restore_reclaimable_kv_storage :968 calls allocate_kv_group(true, reclaimable_kv_bytes_) only, and line 349 constructs only the just-allocated arena. "Do not touch x_data, the separate embedding buffer": x_data :1131 is a separate unique_dma buffer allocated at :1106-1113. Section-9 row 521 links #lifetime and matches the body text. Three deviations from the corrected recommendation, judged acceptable. (a) The bullet was not moved; it still follows the heterogeneous bullet (350). It now opens with "EAGLE requires uniform geometry" and forbids an EAGLE branch in heterogeneous enumeration, so the misreading N25 described cannot happen. (b) The qualified caution about for_each_active_slot omitting the EAGLE offset was deleted. Its condition was "if the implementer uses a per-offset loop for uniform layouts too". Line 349 prescribes one whole-arena array for uniform geometry, and line 350 names for_each_active_slot only for heterogeneous geometry, so the guarded path is excluded by the design. (c) The clause "it contains no KV blocks" after x_data was dropped; "separate embedding buffer" still carries the meaning. That clause is recorded under C01's residual, where the two-buffer distinction was the original point.

source re-grader (Resolved): The EAGLE bullet was rewritten and every fact in it checks against kv_cache.hpp at 2880c3aa9b (byte-identical at live main 1400fa4481 per facts-r3.md:42-43). (1) "EAGLE requires uniform geometry" [design-r3.txt:351]: eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0 [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:771]; TRON_ASSERT "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage" [:788-789]; calculate_allocation_sizes returns std::nullopt for support_eagle without it [:1158-1159]. (2) "The uniform retained-arena array already includes its final physical KV slot with the primary geometry" [design-r3.txt:351]: storage_location returns reclaimable = false and the retained prefix for offset.i == logical_slot_count [:727-735]; arena_sizes appends one slot's bytes (offsets.values[1].total()) to result.retained [:717-719], so the slot sits at the end of the retained arena; kv_block_at_storage asserts geometry == layout_t::primary_geometry for that offset [:1326-1329]. The uniform rule at design-r3.txt:349 (one array, bound = checked arena bytes / sizeof(kv_block_t)) therefore covers it. (3) "Do not add an EAGLE branch to heterogeneous enumeration" [design-r3.txt:351] states the fact the finding asked for. (4) "Reclaimable restoration must not reconstruct that retained slot" matches restore_reclaimable_kv_storage, which calls allocate_kv_group only for the reclaimable arena [:968]; design-r3.txt:348 says both allocation paths run the construction helper there. (5) x_data is a separate buffer [:1131]. The misleading sentence "Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot" was deleted [design-wdiff.txt:1082-1084]. Two deviations from the letter of the corrected recommendation are acceptable. The bullet stays after the heterogeneous bullet (design-r3.txt:350) instead of after the uniform bullet (:349); the explicit sentence in (3) removes the misreading the move was meant to prevent. The source-lens qualified caution ("if the implementer uses a per-offset loop for uniform layouts too ...") was dropped rather than kept; the design prescribes one whole-arena array for uniform geometry [design-r3.txt:349], so the caution's precondition does not arise in the design as written. Section 9 row "Uniform construction includes EAGLE once. Heterogeneous enumeration has no EAGLE branch." [design-r3.txt:521] matches the body. Sources row S16 links the requirement at kv_cache.hpp#L771-L789 [design-r3-links.tsv:199]. Checker quotes confirmed at design-r3.txt:349, 351, 521, 580. Correction: Optional (note, no change required): the bullet says "constructed once" only by implication. One clause would make it explicit: "Restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena (kv_cache.hpp:968), so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, in the constructor."

fairness re-grader (Resolved): Severity: none remaining (note only). The corrected recommendation asked for four statements, one verifier addition, and a bullet move. All statements are in the body. (1) EAGLE exists only with uniform geometry: design-r3.txt:351 says "EAGLE requires uniform geometry." The code agrees: kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:771 defines eagle_compatible as layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0, :788-789 asserts it, and :1158-1159 makes calculate_allocation_sizes return std::nullopt otherwise. The design links the first two sites through S16 "[EAGLE uniform-geometry requirement]" -> kv_cache.hpp#L771-L789 (design-r3.txt:580; design-r3-links.tsv:199). (2) The uniform whole-arena array already covers the EAGLE slot, and the slot is in the retained arena: design-r3.txt:351 says "The uniform retained-arena array already includes its final physical KV slot with the primary geometry." The code agrees: storage_location returns reclaimable = false with the retained prefix offset for offset.i == logical_slot_count (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:730-734), arena_sizes adds one slot to result.retained (:717-719), and kv_block_at_storage asserts primary geometry at the EAGLE offset (:1326-1329). (3) The heterogeneous enumeration never meets an EAGLE slot: design-r3.txt:351 says "Do not add an EAGLE branch to heterogeneous enumeration." (4) x_data stays untouched: design-r3.txt:351 says "Do not touch x_data, the separate embedding buffer." (5) Verifier addition, constructed once in the constructor: design-r3.txt:351 says "Reclaimable restoration must not reconstruct that retained slot"; design-r3.txt:348 says both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use the construction path; design-r3.txt:350 says restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart retained objects. The code agrees: restore_reclaimable_kv_storage calls allocate_kv_group(true, ...) only (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:968). Section 9 row design-r3.txt:521 matches this body text. Three deviations remain, none of which defeats the recommendation's purpose. (i) The bullet was not moved. It still follows the heterogeneous bullet (design-r3.txt:350 then :351). The misreading that motivated the move (the bullet read as part of the heterogeneous enumeration) is now excluded by the explicit sentence "Do not add an EAGLE branch to heterogeneous enumeration." (ii) The source-lens verifier asked to keep the caution that for_each_active_slot omits the EAGLE offset, qualified for a per-offset loop over uniform layouts. The design deleted the sentence instead (design-wdiff.txt:1082-1084). This is acceptable: design-r3.txt:349 prescribes one whole-arena array for uniform geometry, so the per-offset loop that the caution guarded against is not an option the design allows. (iii) The clause "it contains no KV blocks" after x_data was dropped (design-wdiff.txt:1083-1084). The words "embedding buffer" carry the same meaning. Correction: Precision to the checker's evidence: the removed text was not only the caution sentence. The same word-diff segment (design-wdiff.txt:1082-1084) also removed "EAGLE" before "embedding buffer" and the clause "; it contains no KV blocks". The checker's quotes also omit design-r3.txt:348 and :350, which together with :351 carry the verifier's added requirement that the EAGLE slot is constructed only in the constructor.

Resolved N27. token_ix_needed mislabeled 'partner-readiness rule' (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:319 "Keep adjust_grains_for_partners, the scheduler's pair-preserving work partition, in model.hpp. Keep token_ix_needed, the page-readiness rule, in common.hpp. Its existing comment is accurate and needs no edit. Update only the partner-scheduling comments that name the moved V operation. [C02]" design-r3.txt:374 "| 3. Model save | h/tron/models/model.hpp | Wrap aligned source rows in the packed branch. Keep the existing 8-lane branch, partner scheduling, completion, and notifications. Update the changed operation's comments. Leave common.hpp 's page-readiness rule unchanged. |" design-r3.txt:363 "Cross-reference it from amx_attn_iface.hpp:224-227, self_attention.hpp:31-35, and model.hpp:209-213,2816-2820." design-r3.txt:522 (section 9) "| N27 N28 | Name page readiness correctly, leave its accurate comment unchanged, and list exact changed comment sites. [Design section] | Relocate line references on fetched main. |" (the [Design section] link resolves to #contracts, section 6).

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked for three things: rename the rule to "page-readiness rule", state that the token_ix_needed comment stays unchanged, and limit the comment update to the adjust_grains_for_partners comment in model.hpp. The body does all three. Facts checked. (1) The rename is right: common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1024-1036 is token_ix_needed; its comment at 1025-1028 says "scaled_v reads the entire page, including masked-out entries, and V writes share interleaved storage. Wait for every producer of a page that any query sees"; the body scans every visible range of one page. The rule is page-granular, so "page-readiness rule" is the accurate label. (2) "Its existing comment is accurate and needs no edit" holds under the design: page::set_v keeps its name (design-r3.txt:268), scaled_v_expr keeps pair rounding and whole-page reads (design-r3.txt:329), and the interleaved layout is unchanged (design-r3.txt:208). (3) "the partner-scheduling comments that name the moved V operation" identifies model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:209-213, whose text reads "because page.set_v interleaves them in the same SIMD values"; design-r3.txt:363 names that site by line. (4) The step-3 Files column at design-r3.txt:374 lists only h/tron/models/model.hpp; the round-2 entry "comments in h/tron/models/common.hpp" is gone (design-wdiff.txt:1147 OLD vs :1154 NEW), which is the firm fix the round-2 fairness re-grader asked for. (5) The round-2 sentence "Update their explanatory comments" was replaced (design-wdiff.txt:991-997). (6) common.hpp and model.hpp are unchanged between 2880c3aa9b and live main 1400fa4481 (facts-r3.md:40-41), so the cited lines are valid on a fresh fetch. Not included: the recommendation's optional parenthetical explaining the rule ("it waits for every producer of a page that any query sees ..."). The verifier correction asked only for the rename, so I do not count that as a gap. One small internal tension between lines 319 and 363 is reported as a new defect below.

New defect raised by the checker (minor): Claim: design-r3.txt:319 restricts the model.hpp comment edits to "the partner-scheduling comments that name the moved V operation", but design-r3.txt:363 asks to cross-reference the relocated layout documentation from "model.hpp:209-213,2816-2820". Only the first of those two comments names the operation. Source: model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:209-213 reads "because page.set_v interleaves them in the same SIMD values"; model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2816-2820 reads "Take care: we can't just split the items across threads, because we're interleaving the even-offset and odd-offset tokens of any given page in the same SIMD values" and names no function. So an implementer following line 319 literally skips the 2816-2820 edit that line 363 requires. A second small ambiguity: "the moved V operation" is not a defined phrase; design-r3.txt:258 says append_v_row moves the set_v bodies, while design-r3.txt:268 keeps the name page::set_v, so the reader must infer that the phrase means set_v. Recommendation: replace the last sentence of line 319 with "Update only the two partner-scheduling comments in model.hpp (209-213 and 2816-2820 at 2880c3aa9b): add a cross-reference to the v_vnni.hpp layout documentation, and in 209-213 optionally say that page::set_v forwards to append_v_row, which does the pair interleaving." Low risk: line 363 already lists both sites explicitly.

source re-grader (Resolved): The mislabel is gone. The design now says "Keep token_ix_needed, the page-readiness rule, in common.hpp. Its existing comment is accurate and needs no edit." [design-r3.txt:319; word change OLD partner-readiness -> NEW page-readiness at design-wdiff.txt:991-993]. The label is right: the function scans every visible range of the page that holds the token and has no pair logic [h/tron/models/common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1024-1038]. The "comment is accurate" claim is right: the comment gives two reasons, scaled_v reads the entire page and V writes share interleaved storage [common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1025-1028]. Both reasons hold under the design, which keeps whole-page reads in the 16-lane weighted sum [design-r3.txt:322] and keeps the interleaved layout [design-r3.txt:205-206]. The open-ended "Update their explanatory comments" is replaced by "Update only the partner-scheduling comments that name the moved V operation" [design-r3.txt:319], and the exact sites are named: model.hpp:209-213 and 2816-2820 [design-r3.txt:363]. Both ranges are the partner comments at 2880c3aa9b: "Fix grains not to split even/odd token pairs ... because page.set_v interleaves them" [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:209-213] and "Take care: we can't just split the items across threads ... interleaving the even-offset and odd-offset tokens" [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2816-2820]. Step 3 now lists only model.hpp in its Files column and says "Leave common.hpp 's page-readiness rule unchanged" [design-r3.txt:374], which is the firm form the round-2 fairness verifier asked for. The section-9 row matches the body change and links to #contracts [design-r3.txt:522; design HTML row hrefs]. Every checkable fact in the fix is right. Severity of what remains: note. Correction: Two notes, no change required. (1) "the moved V operation" [design-r3.txt:319] is loose wording. page::set_v keeps its name [design-r3.txt:268]; only its body moves into append_v_row [design-r3.txt:258]. The one partner comment that names an operation is model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:211 (page.set_v); model.hpp:2816-2820 names none but is still listed at design-r3.txt:363 as a cross-reference site. A tighter sentence: "Update the model.hpp:209-213 comment that names page.set_v to say set_v forwards to append_v_row, which does the pair interleaving; add a cross-reference at 2816-2820." (2) The recommendation's explanatory clause for the page-readiness rule ("it waits for every producer of a page that any query sees ...") is not in the design. The bare name plus "in common.hpp" is enough to locate the function, so this is not a missing piece. The checker's quotes at design-r3.txt:319, 374, 363 and 522 exist as cited.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked for three things: call token_ix_needed the page-readiness rule, state that its comment stays unchanged, and limit the comment update to the adjust_grains_for_partners comment. The design does all three. Section 6 now reads "Keep token_ix_needed, the page-readiness rule, in common.hpp. Its existing comment is accurate and needs no edit. Update only the partner-scheduling comments that name the moved V operation." [design-r3.txt:319]. Step 3 lists only h/tron/models/model.hpp in its Files column and says "Leave common.hpp 's page-readiness rule unchanged." [design-r3.txt:374]. Resolved N29. Shared-file count is ten, not nine (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: The round-2 sentence "Both PRs edit nine of the same files. [F15]" is gone: grep for "nine", "same files" and "ten of the same" in design-r3.txt returns nothing. design-r3.txt:389 "- At port time, remeasure shared files with git diff --name-only and conflicts with git merge-tree against the recorded current main/parent and saved child head. ... The final parent file list above is the scope to compare." Section 9, design-r3.txt:523 "| N29 N30 | Remove the fragile historical overlap count. Remeasure shared files and conflicts against the final parent scope at port time. [Design section] | The old common.hpp conflict is historical evidence only. |" ([Design section] goes to #child, which exists) and :544 "Recompute overlaps/conflicts and perform child validation. Do not use the old file count."

Checker assessment: N29 was a factual error: the count said nine while the round-2 parent list shared ten files with the child. The recommendation offered one fix, replacing the number with "ten" plus the list. The design took a different fix: it removed the count and tells the implementer to remeasure the shared-file set with git diff --name-only against the final parent list (:389). The error is gone, and the replacement instruction is correct and durable. The removal is the better fix, and I checked why. The round-3 parent step table (:372-377) lists kv_cache_fwd.hpp (new), v_vnni.hpp (new), kv_cache.hpp, model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, amx_attn_iface.hpp, amx_attn.cpp, full.hpp, t_llama_unit.cpp, t_amx_numerics.cpp, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp and heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp. common.hpp left the parent list in this revision (:319 "Keep token_ix_needed, the page-readiness rule, in common.hpp. Its existing comment is accurate and needs no edit."; :374 "Leave common.hpp 's page-readiness rule unchanged."). The child changes 25 files (git diff --name-only c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb). The intersection with the round-3 parent list is nine files: kv_cache.hpp, model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, amx_attn_iface.hpp, amx_attn.cpp, full.hpp, t_llama_unit.cpp, t_amx_numerics.cpp, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp. So the recommended literal text "ten of the same files" would itself be wrong against this revision. A count written into the page goes stale whenever the parent scope moves, which is what the N30 intent-lens correction warned about for dated lists. Removing the number and pointing at the final parent list as the scope to compare resolves the finding without introducing a new stale fact. The section-9 row (:523) matches the body change (:389); this is not a table-only claim.

source re-grader (Resolved): The finding was a factual error: the round-2 text said "Both PRs edit nine of the same files" when the round-2 parent list shared ten files with the child. That sentence is gone. Grep of design-r3.txt for "nine", "same files" and "ten of the same" returns no hit. In its place the design says "At port time, remeasure shared files with git diff --name-only ... The final parent file list above is the scope to compare" [design-r3.txt:389], and section 9 says "Remove the fragile historical overlap count" [design-r3.txt:523] and "Do not use the old file count" [design-r3.txt:544]. The design chose removal plus a remeasure instruction instead of the recommended corrected number. That choice is sound and is the one the N30 intent-lens correction asked for (no dated lists baked into the design). Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:410: "K saves differ from V saves. A K token owns one 4-byte lane containing two consecutive dimensions in each of 64 cache lines. Sixteen tokens share every line. Checker assessment: The round-2 sentence "A K token owns separate 4-byte lanes in a shared cache line" is replaced by the recommended wording. The word diff confirms the replacement at this spot (design-wdiff.txt:1451-1454). Every fact in the new sentence checks out against the child source. - One 4-byte lane holds two consecutive dimensions of one token: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:46-47 ("The two values of one dimension pair share one 32-bit lane") and :15-17. - One 64-byte line holds that pair for 16 tokens, so sixteen tokens share every line: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:16-17 and :49-51 (BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 64 bytes / (2 * sizeof(bf16))). - A 128-dimension token owns 64 such lanes in 64 different lines: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:135-137 ("Only this token's 64 pair slots are written") and h/tron/gof.hpp@30c4ac82cb:69-70 ("a token's 128 values sit in 64 lines"). - Lane scatter: scatter_row = 4 x _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 with DWORD_BYTES_4 scale, k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139-146. Full-block stores write whole lines (:206-209) without a read-merge-rewrite, so "Never read, merge, and rewrite the whole 64-byte line" stays true. - Disjoint token lanes across workers: h/tron/models/common.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1060-1061 ("Their writers touch disjoint token lanes"). Resolved N32. set_k_row/get_k_row/set_k_block parameter types unspecified (round 2, grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:405 "| page::set_k_row , page::get_k_row | Use const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for save and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for load. The boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties. Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions. These K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement. Wrap scratch without copying. Call typed store_row / load_row . |" design-r3.txt:406 "| page::set_k_block | Keep the name. Call store_block(writable_k_view, block, mask, rows) . Preserve const bf16* const rows[BLOCK_TOKENS_16] for 16 independent native source rows, with null entries for absent lanes. The destination plane carries the layout type. These source-row pointers do not expose packed storage. |" design-r3.txt:408 "| hardware::page_info K callback | Add the child's scratch parameter. The caller owns 64-byte-aligned scratch. Consume each returned row before that buffer is reused for the next token. [S14] |" Section 9, design-r3.txt:514 "specify row/block argument families".

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked the design to state the parameter type per accessor and give the reason. Both are done. set_k_row and get_k_row take tron's contiguous row view family (const_view for the source, view for the destination), the same family the parent uses for set_v/get_v at design-r3.txt:255. set_k_block keeps 16 raw const bf16* entries. Each choice carries a reason: the view flags preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties and no copy is needed [design-r3.txt:405]; the pointer array is kept because absent lanes are null and the destination plane, not the source rows, carries the layout type [design-r3.txt:406]. Facts checked: - Template parameter order is view<T, aligned, dma, Dim, Stride> [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:22-28]. The rank-1 specialization is view<T, aligned, dma, seq<d0>, sseq<s0>> [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:115-116]. The design's spelled types const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> follow that order. - The child's parameters are const bf16* row and bf16* row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1701-1702, :1737-1738]. Conversion to bf16 happens before the call: view<bf16, true, false, seq<geometry.kv.head_size>>{conv[i]}.set(kout) [h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2922-2924, :2936-2938]. So fixing the element type to bf16 matches the child. - kout is already a view with a .data member [model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2918-2920]. The GOF callback passes caller-owned scratch dest to get_k_row [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655]. "Wrap scratch without copying" applies to these sites. - scatter_row loads the source row with _mm512_loadu_si512 (an unaligned load) [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:142] and gather_row stores with _mm512_storeu_si512 (an unaligned store) [:226]. store_block loads with loadu [:201]. So "These K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement" is right, and "Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions" names real instructions (_mm512_i32scatter_epi32 at :143, _mm512_i32gather_epi32 at :224). - set_k_block takes const bf16* const rows[k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16] [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1723-1728]. The caller zero-initializes const bf16* rows[K_STORE_BLOCK_16] = {}; so absent lanes are null [model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2929]. "null entries for absent lanes" is right. - Ben's sketch uses std::span<const bf16, Dims> for the K row (github-review.json, comment 5765866077). The design states its deliberate alternative and why, which the recommendation allowed. One observation that is not part of N32 and not a new error: the child's set_k_row/get_k_row also serve the native (row-major) layout through memcpy via k_at(i_page).data [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1707-1709, :1745-1747]. The design row says "Call typed store_row / load_row" without saying what the native branch does with the view parameter. The round-2 text had the same sentence, so this is pre-existing and outside the corrected recommendation. An implementer can keep the memcpy from the view's data or use the native row view's set().

source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked the design to pick one parameter rule per accessor and say why. For set_k_row and get_k_row the design picks the existing rank-1 view family: const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for save and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for load, and gives the reason: the boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties, the K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement, and scratch is wrapped without copying [design-r3.txt:405]. For set_k_block it keeps 'const bf16* const rows[BLOCK_TOKENS_16]' and gives the reason: 16 independent native source rows with null entries for absent lanes, and the pointers do not expose packed storage [design-r3.txt:406]. Every checkable fact is right. The child's set_k_row and get_k_row take const bf16* / bf16* today [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1702, 1738]. set_k_block takes 'const bf16* const rows[k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16]' [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1723-1728]. The 'no stronger alignment requirement' claim holds: scatter_row loads the row with _mm512_loadu_si512, gather_row stores with _mm512_storeu_si512, and store_block loads rows[t] with _mm512_loadu_si512, so no aligned-row precondition exists for K [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139, 200, 244]. 'Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions' matches _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 and _mm512_i32gather_epi32 [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:140-141, 242-243]. Wrapping without copying is possible: the child already wraps conv[0] as view<bf16, true, false, seq<head_size>> [model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2922-2924] and passes the GOF scratch 'dest' to get_k_row [full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655]. The rank-1 view has valid() [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:126-141], so both options were legal and the design chose one. Ben's sketch used std::span<const bf16, Dims> / std::span<bf16, Dims> for the K row [github-review.json, comment 5765866077]; the design's choice of the repository's own view family is a stated alternative with a reason, which the recommendation allowed. The checker's quotes exist at lines 405, 406, 408 and 514.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked the design to state the row parameter type for set_k_row and get_k_row, and to pick one option for set_k_block with a reason. Both are done. The set_k_row/get_k_row row now says: use const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for save and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for load [design-r3.txt:405]. That is the same contiguous row family the parent uses for V rows [design-r3.txt:255]. The row states the deliberate difference and its reason: the boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties, and "These K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement" [design-r3.txt:405]. The child's instructions support that choice: scatter_row and store_block load the source row with _mm512_loadu_si512, an unaligned load [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:142, 201], and gather_row writes the row with _mm512_storeu_si512, an unaligned store [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:227]. "Wrap scratch without copying" and "Call typed store_row / load_row" cover kout, conv[i] and the callback scratch [design-r3.txt:405, 408]. The bf16-only element type matches the child, which converts non-bf16 rows into an alignas(64) bf16 conv buffer before calling set_k_row or set_k_block [model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2883, 2918-2938]. For set_k_block the design picks the pointer option and gives two reasons: "Preserve const bf16* const rows[BLOCK_TOKENS_16] for 16 independent native source rows, with null entries for absent lanes" and "These source-row pointers do not expose packed storage" [design-r3.txt:406]. BLOCK_TOKENS_16 is the child's constant [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:51], and the child's set_k_block already has that parameter [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1723-1728].

The design picks (a): class definitions complete, only the operation bodies guarded at 16 lanes (:414), and it names TRON_K_VNNI=OFF for the 8-lane child check (:414, :461). Facts checked at the child head 30c4ac82cb. The fake qk_vnni_128x4 is defined at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:196-199 inside the fake namespace :170-205, and the only #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH in the file starts at :207, so the fake is compiled in every build. h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:27 includes tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp without a condition, and :35-40 #errors only when TRON_K_VNNI is defined with TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16, so the 8-lane build with TRON_K_VNNI off still compiles the header. In h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp the operations scatter_row (:138-146), store_block (:193-216) and gather_row (:220-228) are non-template functions marked TRON(inline), which expands to inline __attribute__((always_inline)) (h/common/attributes.hpp:78), and they use _mm512 intrinsics under no TRON_CHUNK_SIZE guard; qk_group (:246-248) is a template; the file's only conditional is #ifdef TRON_K_VNNI around layout_on (:91-97). The names store_row/load_row at :405 are the proposed typed operation names, parallel to the V names; :405 says the existing gather/scatter instructions are preserved, so the mapping to the child's scatter_row/gather_row is clear.

The lead-level fact that no child reader uses expr on K stays true at 30c4ac82cb (dense and partial QK take the whole plane, staging uses get_k_row, copies use gather_row/scatter_row; facts-r2/facts-r3), and the design now says so at :412 ("Production staging, copies, and scores continue to use bulk row operations or whole-plane arguments") and in the child accessor table at :404-407. - Consumer: "an ordinary host tensor constructed from a packed-K view in the existing layout suite" (:412). The layout suite is t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp, named at :390 and :416; it exists at 30c4ac82cb (git ls-tree) and is registered unconditionally as a fake-labelled test at t/CMakeLists.txt@30c4ac82cb:618. So "eight 4-byte values across eight cache lines" is right for the 16-lane chunk. gather_row itself is 4 gathers of 16 dwords (k_vnni.hpp:218-221), consistent with the design's bulk load_row. - Conditional on Q3: :412 last sentence matches the Q3 "If rejected" column at :97 ("Remove matrix and row expression inheritance from both families"), so K and V are dropped together as the intent-lens verifier asked. - Required-CI limitation: the required Nix build sets neither TRON_K_VNNI nor TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (no match in nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@30c4ac82cb; facts-r3.md:76 for the AMX flag), and the design states that K-expression coverage in required CI is a child obligation (:414, :467, :524). That is an honest limit, not a residual, because the recommendation did not ask the design to solve required-CI coverage here. The requirement at :391 is no longer a bare "its row expression": :412 gives its purpose, consumer, cost, and exit condition. No fact in the fix is wrong.

source re-grader (Resolved): The design now states the purpose, the consumer, the cost, and the fallback, as the corrected recommendation asked. Purpose: "serves the reviewer's uniform-expression requirement in Q3" [design-r3.txt:412], with Q3 applying the expression-read proposal to the child [design-r3.txt:97]. Design text checked: design-r3.txt:479 "Before a campaign on delphi-3bda, source ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh and call campaign_guard_acquire. Section 9, design-r3.txt:526 "| N37 N38 | List all guard refusal conditions and platform-specific bench limits. No benchmark records were refreshed. |"

Checker assessment: The recommendation asked the design to list every campaign_guard_acquire refusal condition, state the --allow-serving rule, say the flock reserves the machine only among this user's sessions, and say that ci_took_dut returns busy for the CI lease, another active user, or a blackout window and that the run must stop in any of those cases. Lines 479-480 do all of this. I checked each clause against ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh (the current file; the round-2 verifiers cited the same line numbers). campaign_guard_acquire (lines 146-179) refuses, in order: ci_lease_busy (147, "GUARD: System CI holds the DUT (lease busy)"), other_user_active (148, "another person is actively using the DUT"), blackout_active (149), a held flock on /var/tmp/jhan/3bda-campaign.lock (150-156, "campaign flock held by another session"), a running runtron (162-168, pgrep ... -x 'runtron(\.[a-z0-9]+)?', "runtron already running"), and rinzler_active unless the first argument is --allow-serving (172-177, "pass --allow-serving only if your script stops and restores it"). The design's six conditions map one to one onto these six checks, and its --allow-serving sentence matches the script's message. "The lock coordinates this user's campaigns; it does not reserve the host against CI" matches the authority order (lines 6-12: the lease is authoritative; the flock is the cross-session campaign lock). ci_took_dut at line 316 is ci_lease_busy || other_user_active || blackout_active; line 480 names exactly these three and says to stop on any. The lease rule matches lines 6-8 and the ci_lease_busy test at lines 25-44 (state == 'busy' and time.time() < exp + grace, grace defaults to 0 s, and ci_took_dut passes no grace argument). The lease path /run/lock/systems-test-ci.lease matches lines 6 and 28. "Clock windows are advisory" matches lines 13-15. rinzler_active checks rinzler@0 through rinzler@3 (lines 181-183); the design does not need that detail. The sentence "recheck ci_took_dut, the guard for CI, another active user, or a configured blackout" reads as an appositive that defines ci_took_dut; it is not misleading. No factual slip found.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The recommendation asked for the full refusal list of campaign_guard_acquire (the shell function in lib-guard.sh that a campaign calls before launching on delphi-3bda), the meaning of its lock, the --allow-serving rule, and the full meaning of ci_took_dut (the shell function that reports whether the host is contended). Design text checked: design-r3.txt:459 "The native preset probes the build host and can disable AVX-512 despite -DAVX512=ON. Look for Disabling AVX512 in configure output. Section 9 row: design-r3.txt:527 "N39 N40 N41 N60 | Check actual AVX-512 selection, separate Make caches, ..."

Checker assessment: The recommendation asked for one sentence with three parts: confirm the configure log has no "Disabling AVX512" warning; on a host without AVX-512 configure with BUILD_NATIVE=OFF (preset cross-avx512) for the 16-lane rows; those binaries run only on an AVX-512 host. The source-lens correction added a fourth part: say that the AMX-on row fails loudly, so the log check matters for the AMX-off row. All four parts are in design-r3.txt:459, and :452 adds a check of the actual TRON_AVX512_ENABLED definition. Facts checked at 2880c3aa9b. CMakeLists.txt:38 option(BUILD_NATIVE "Probe this host before enabling AVX512" ON); :95-117 runs lscpu and, when a required feature is missing, set(AVX512 OFF) and message(WARNING "Disabling AVX512: ${FEATURE} not supported") (:112-113). CMakePresets.json:40-48 defines preset cross-avx512, inheriting native, with BUILD_NATIVE OFF (:45) and AVX512 ON (:46). h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:30-36 has #if defined(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) && TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16 followed by #error "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH requires TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 ...", and src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:219-224 and :329-332 define TRON_AMX_DISPATCH independently of AVX512, so the AMX-on row does fail at compile time when the probe turns AVX512 off. TRON_AVX512_ENABLED is defined only inside if(AVX512) at src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:269-272 and :319-324, so it is the right definition to check. The S17 link range CMakePresets.json#L31-L49 covers both presets (native :30-39, cross-avx512 :40-48); the one-line offset at the start is harmless. Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation (all three verifier lenses) asked for: (1) a method to locate the inlined bodies by source line or by the enclosing non-inlined callers, without telling the agent to look for set_v< or append_v< as symbols; (2) a statement that the baseline t_llama_unit has no fp16 set_v body, with the harness-or-record alternative; and it dropped the optimization-level demand. All three are in the body. Facts checked: - "RelWithDebInfo build type": CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37 for preset native. RIGHT. - "The build adds -O3; do not assume the preset's nominal -O2 is the effective final setting": src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-294 adds -O3 PUBLIC on tron for every non-Debug GCC/Clang build; t_llama_unit links tron (t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:190, :586-587), and per-target options follow CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO on the compile line, so -O3 is the effective level. RIGHT, and more accurate than the verifiers' "(-O2 -g)". - "gen/t_llama_unit": CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:66 set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}); preset native binaryDir is ${sourceDir}/gen (CMakePresets.json:34). RIGHT. (Note only: the S17 link "[Binary output directory]" points at CMakeLists.txt#L67, one line after the set() at :66; that link belongs to N60/S17, not N40.) - objdump -d -l --no-show-raw-insn -C: -l is --line-numbers and needs the -g that RelWithDebInfo carries. Consistent with the design-text lens correction. - "Forced-inline helpers may have no separate symbol": set_v (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1621-1673) and append_v (:1872) are TRON(inline); h/common/attributes.hpp@2880c3aa9b:77-78 defines tron_inline as inline __attribute__((always_inline)). RIGHT. allocate_kv_group (:1199) and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage (:962-963) carry no forced-inline attribute, so "surviving allocation/restore instantiations" is the right hedge. - "The baseline suite does not instantiate fp16 append": git grep fp16 2880c3aa9b -- t/t_llama_unit.cpp hits only :1081 (a scale constant); every set_v call in that file (:142, :796, :1554, :1723, :1923, :2533-2802) passes bf16 or float buffers; no fp16 set_v caller exists in h/, src/ or t/ at 2880c3aa9b. RIGHT. - The harness-or-record alternative (:487) matches the correction's either/or, and the text names no set_v< / append_v< symbols to search for. - Section 9 row 527 matches the body.

source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation kept two points: name a method to locate the inlined bodies in the optimized t_llama_unit binaries, and state that the baseline binary has no fp16 append body. Both are in the body. design-r3.txt:486 runs objdump -d -l --no-show-raw-insn -C on both gen/t_llama_unit binaries and locates the enclosing Catch test functions through source lines, plus surviving allocation/restore instantiations, and warns that forced-inline helpers may have no separate symbol. This is right: -l (--line-numbers) is valid with -d and uses the -g debug data that RelWithDebInfo carries; the test binary lands in gen/ because CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:66 sets CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY to the binary dir and the native preset's binaryDir is gen [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:34]; set_v is TRON(inline) [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2327], which expands to always_inline [h/common/attributes.hpp@2880c3aa9b:78], so it has no symbol of its own. design-r3.txt:487 states the baseline suite does not instantiate fp16 append, asks for a matched temporary harness against both trees or an explicit 'Insufficient data: no baseline fp16 body' record, and forbids presenting an absent symbol as a comparison. This is right: t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b mentions fp16 only at :1081 (a float scale constant), its set_v callers (:1723, :1923, :2533-2802) pass bf16 or float buffers, and the fp16 set_v overload exists unchanged at baseline [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2325-2330], so a harness can instantiate it in both trees. The new sentence at design-r3.txt:485 ('The build adds -O3; do not assume the preset's nominal -O2 is the effective final setting') is right: src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:293 adds -O3 for every non-Debug build as a PUBLIC option, target compile options follow CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO (-O2 -g -DNDEBUG) on the compile line, and the last -O flag wins for GCC and Clang; no CMake file overrides CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO. compile_commands.json exists because base-ninja sets CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS 1 [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:22]. Section 9 row design-r3.txt:527 matches the body. Correction: Note only: design-r3.txt:486 says 'surviving allocation/restore instantiations' without naming book::allocate_kv_group and book::restore_reclaimable_kv_storage in that bullet; section 6 (design-r3.txt:343, the arena construction bullets) names both, so the implementer has the names. The [S17] link text 'Binary output directory' points at CMakeLists.txt#L67 while the set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ...) line is :66 (line 67 is the include of cmake/PortableBuildTree.cmake); off by one line.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation kept two points and dropped the optimization-level demand. (1) A method to locate inlined bodies without hunting for set_v< or append_v< symbols. The design now says: "Run objdump -d -l --no-show-raw-insn -C on both gen/t_llama_unit binaries. Locate the enclosing Catch test functions through source lines ... Locate surviving allocation/restore instantiations. Forced-inline helpers may have no separate symbol." [design-r3.txt:486].
