The optional optimization statement is also right: "The build adds -O3; do not assume the preset's nominal -O2 is the effective final setting" [design-r3.txt:485] follows from the PUBLIC -O3 option [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:293] and from the absence of any CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO override (none in CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt or t/CMakeLists.txt at 2880c3aa9b), so CMake's default -O2 -g -DNDEBUG is the nominal value. compile_commands.json exists because CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS is on [CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:635; CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:22]. Section 9 matches the body [design-r3.txt:527]. Resolved N12. scaled_v_expr width list attached to the wrong (8-lane) path (round 2, grade Note)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:213 "The new V storage type requires a positive even number of rows. Its column count must be positive and divisible by chunk_size, the selected SIMD width. This satisfies the sketch's positive-dimension rule. The 16-lane packed set_v still requires widths divisible by 32 dimensions. The packed scaled_v_expr supports 64, 128, 256, or 512 dimensions. The unchanged 8-lane path requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0. There is no new 8-lane V-save wrapper. Type constraints do not expand kernel support." design-r3.txt:283 "Type constraints are positive even rows and positive columns divisible by chunk_size. Keep stricter operation constraints, including the packed append width." design-r3.txt:329 "| scaled_v_expr | ... Preserve supported widths, weight conversion, unrolled loops, and addition order. ... |" design-r3.txt:513 (section 9) "| N02 N12 | ... Attach each width constraint to the correct weighted-sum path. [Design section] | ... |"

Checker assessment: The round-2 verifiers re-graded N12 to a note: the defect was the semicolon that let a reader take the 16-lane width list as an 8-lane rule, plus the missing 8-lane rule, and the fix was optional. The new paragraph removes the semicolon and attaches each rule to its path. Facts checked at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b: - "The 16-lane packed set_v still requires widths divisible by 32 dimensions": set_v declarations :1622-1631 and :1645-1659 all carry head_size % 32 == 0 (also get_v :1634-1641, :1663-1673). RIGHT. - "The packed scaled_v_expr supports 64, 128, 256, or 512 dimensions": the 16-lane constructor :2066-2071 requires(head_size == 64 || head_size == 128 || head_size == 256 || head_size == 512) inside #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 (:1995). RIGHT, and now attached to the packed path. - "The unchanged 8-lane path requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0": the AVX2 constructor :2139-2143 requires(head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0) under #else (:2138). RIGHT. The 8-lane v()/v_ptr() accessors :1677-1724 carry only the geometry checks, so the sentence is true only of the scaled_v_expr constructor; the subject is implicit, but the sentence follows the scaled_v_expr sentence and no 8-lane change is specified (design-r3.txt:270, 282), so it cannot lead an implementer to add a constraint. - Class-level rule :1989 requires(head_size % chunk_size == 0) is matched by the new type's "columns divisible by chunk_size" (design-r3.txt:213, 283). - The phrase with no requires-clause referent ("8-lane forwarding wrapper retains its existing contiguous-row constraints") is gone; "There is no new 8-lane V-save wrapper" replaces it. Two optional items from the per-build list were not adopted: get_v is not named beside set_v for the % 32 rule, and the 8-lane rule is not spelled out as head_size % 64 == 0. Both are derivable, and the corrected recommendation called the list optional, so they are not residuals.

source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected defect (lead note) was a missing 8-lane rule and a misleading sentence order that attached the 16-lane width list to the 8-lane path. design-r3.txt:213 now reads: 'The 16-lane packed set_v still requires widths divisible by 32 dimensions. The packed scaled_v_expr supports 64, 128, 256, or 512 dimensions. The unchanged 8-lane path requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0.' Each fact is right at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b (identical at live main 1400fa4481): set_v requires head_size % 32 == 0 [:1622-1632], the 16-lane scaled_v_expr constructor requires head_size == 64 || 128 || 256 || 512 [:2070-2071, inside #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 at :1995], the AVX2 constructor requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0 [:2143]. The type constraint 'positive columns divisible by chunk_size' (design-r3.txt:213, :283) matches the class-level requires(head_size % chunk_size == 0) [:1989]. The semicolon that let a reader take the list as the 8-lane rule is gone (design-wdiff.txt:449-450 shows the inserted sentence). Section 6 row design-r3.txt:329 keeps 'Preserve supported widths', and design-r3.txt:283 keeps stricter operation constraints, so no shared static_assert can narrow 8-lane support. Section 9 row design-r3.txt:513 ('Attach each width constraint to the correct weighted-sum path') matches the body. Correction: Two optional parts of the per-build list were not adopted; both are note-level. (1) get_v shares set_v's head_size % 32 == 0 rule [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1634-1641, :1661-1673] and design-r3.txt:213 names only set_v. (2) 'The unchanged 8-lane path' at design-r3.txt:213 should say 'the 8-lane scaled_v_expr constructor', because the 8-lane v() and v_ptr() accessors carry only the geometry check [:1674-1724] and no width rule; the preceding sentence makes the intended subject clear, so an implementer is unlikely to misread it. The paragraph still has no file:line pointers.

fairness re-grader (Partly): Severity note. The corrected recommendation asked for a per-build list: set_v and get_v need head_size % 32 == 0 (16-lane), the 16-lane scaled_v_expr constructor needs head_size in {64, 128, 256, 512}, the 8-lane scaled_v_expr constructor needs head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0 (that is head_size % 64 == 0), and both builds share head_size % chunk_size == 0. The design now says: "The 16-lane packed set_v still requires widths divisible by 32 dimensions. The packed scaled_v_expr supports 64, 128, 256, or 512 dimensions. The unchanged 8-lane path requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0. There is no new 8-lane V-save wrapper. Type constraints do not expand kernel support." [design-r3.txt:213]. What is now right: the four-value list is attached to the packed (16-lane) scaled_v_expr, which matches kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2070-2071 inside the #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 branch [1995]; the 8-lane rule head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0 matches the AVX2 constructor [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2143]; the semicolon is gone; the column rule "divisible by chunk_size" [design-r3.txt:213, 283] mirrors the class-level requires [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1989]; the closing sentence is kept. Two concrete parts are missing. (1) get_v is not named beside set_v. get_v carries the same head_size % 32 == 0 requires-clause [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1634-1641 and 1663-1672]. The design mentions get_v only in section 5 [design-r3.txt:269] and section 8 [design-r3.txt:439] without a width rule. (2) The 8-lane sentence names "the unchanged 8-lane path" instead of the 8-lane scaled_v_expr constructor. Only that constructor carries the rule [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2143]; the 8-lane v() and v_ptr() accessors carry only the geometry check [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1677-1724], and the 8-lane save uses the row view's .set(). Section 9 says "correct weighted-sum path" [design-r3.txt:513], so the intent is clear there, but the body sentence does not say weighted sum. Risk is low: design-r3.txt:283 ("Keep stricter operation constraints") and :329 ("Preserve supported widths") already forbid narrowing any operation, and every declared geometry head size is a multiple of 64 dimensions. Correction: Suggested body fix for design-r3.txt:213: replace the fourth sentence with "The unchanged 8-lane scaled_v_expr constructor requires head_size / chunk_size % 8 == 0, that is head_size % 64 == 0 [kv_cache.hpp:2143]." and add "get_v shares set_v's head_size % 32 == 0 rule [kv_cache.hpp:1634-1672]." Design text checked: design-r3.txt:241 "- The packed types have no DMA template parameter or static DMA flag. No proposed consumer requires one. Dma preserves the existing contiguous view's DMA flag. ..." (the Dma template argument of the ordinary source/destination views in append_v_row/load_row, not a flag on the packed types). design-r3.txt:517 (section 9) "... omit an unused DMA flag ...". Checker assessment: The finding said the sentence "Set dma = false" named nothing that exists and gave an imprecise reason. The design now states explicitly that the packed types carry neither a dma template parameter nor a static dma member, and gives the correct reason. The referent problem is gone. Facts checked in :241: - "No proposed consumer requires one": RIGHT. git grep -E '::dma\b' at 2880c3aa9b over h/ and src/ finds exactly one reader, h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:415-416 (Activation::dma, Result::dma inside launch_matmul_for). That alias is instantiated only for matmul operand owner types; no consumer in the design passes a packed view or row there. A future generic reader of X::dma would fail to compile loudly, never silently. - "An arbitrary logical row is not a contiguous DMA input": RIGHT. h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:11-15@2880c3aa9b: the dma parameter means DMA-safe memory, and "Logically, being DMA-safe requires contiguity, namely that the last stride is 1". A pair-interleaved row has stride 2 in bf16 elements. - "The backing arena can still be DMA-safe memory": RIGHT. h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1199-1208@2880c3aa9b allocate_kv_group calls hardware::try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<uint8_t[]>(bytes, std::align_val_t(storage_alignment)). - "Do not inherit views<>, whose leaf rows must be contiguous": RIGHT. views.hpp:47-51@2880c3aa9b "For now we require the leaf view to have stride 1". - views.hpp, tensor.hpp, itensor.hpp are byte-identical at f46e48ba, 2880c3aa9b and 1400fa4481. Relation to the corrected recommendation: the original recommendation and the design-text-lens correction said the types "may expose" static constexpr bool dma = false for consistency with tensor.hpp:35, :254 and itensor.hpp:26 (all three verified at 2880c3aa9b; dmatensor.hpp:38 and :173 define = true). The intent-lens correction said "Expose" it. The design chose the third path the original recommendation allowed: no flag, with the stated reason that nothing reads it. This is a convention preference, not a correctness issue, and every fact in the design's sentence is right. The round-3 sentence also restores the meaning round 1 accepted ("unsuitable for direct row DMA"), which the round-2 verifier noted the previous revision had dropped. Consistency: :257's "Dma" is the template argument of the ordinary contiguous source/destination views (const_view<Source, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>>), which does exist on view/const_view (5-parameter template, facts-r2.md). Offsets> requires(d0 != DYN_SIZE && sizeof...(ds) == 1) auto operator()(expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in, ...). The design's view inherits expr<view_type,R,D> (:240), so it binds. The lambda indexes v_in[i + offset0] and wraps the row in slice_expr<Row&&, d1> (slice.hpp:170-174), which needs the row to satisfy expression (expr.hpp:141-143 requires size_; the rank-1 base defines static constexpr const size_t size_ = N at expr.hpp:88) and to provide chunk/bf16_chunk/fp16_chunk (expr.hpp:710-722; fp16_chunk comes from the base at :121-127). - "It captures that view by reference": RIGHT. slice.hpp:168-169 "// It's critical that v_in be captured by reference here. auto f = [=, &v_in](size_t i) {". - "Do not ... use the owner overload: that overload creates a temporary view internally": RIGHT. slice.hpp:38-42 template <typename Owner, typename... Offset> requires requires(Owner& owner) { owner.as_view(); } auto operator()(Owner& owner, size_t offset0, Offset... offsets) { return (*this)(owner.as_view(), offset0, offsets...); }. For a v_vnni_tensor the as_view() prvalue is not a view<>/const_view<> or const_views<>, so only the expr const& overload is viable, and the temporary bound to v_in dies at the end of that return statement while the lambda still holds &v_in. - "Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged" (:288) is the design's explicit choice of "leave the path as is", which implies no deleted overload is added; "This proposal adds no lifetime guarantee for that existing fallback" says the same from the caller's side. - The sentence that could be misread as "no slice path exists" was removed rather than narrowed. Removal satisfies the finding's purpose. Not stated: the generic path's offset1 % 64 == 0 and d1 % 64 == 0 rules (slice.hpp:158-161). The design-text-lens correction put them in its suggested sentence; the intent-lens correction said the sentence "could mention" them. No caller at main or in the child slices a cache plane (round-1 F08 evidence), so omitting the rule changes nothing an implementer builds. I treat it as optional and do not carry it as a residual.

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:391 "Define k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, and k_vnni_row for the proposed logical expression reads in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. Move mapping constants, k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, and the existing constexpr free function k_vnni::index there. Keep the function spelling for the independent index checks." design-r3.txt:416 "Adapt t_k_vnni_layout to actual aligned owners. Fill poison with 64 typed row saves. Copy the trivially copyable owner's bytes to a test buffer for physical-layout comparisons. Preserve independent index anchors and avoid the internal friend helpers." design-r3.txt:401 "The owner has one aligned array, no self-pointer, and trivial construction/copy/destruction. ... a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions." design-r3.txt:405 "Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions. ... Call typed store_row / load_row." Section 9: design-r3.txt:514 "N03 N32 N56 N57 N58 N59 | ... name index/poison paths."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation asked for one sentence with two parts: how the test fills poison (64 typed store_row calls or memcpy into the owner), and where k_vnni::index lives (constexpr free function, or its new home). Both parts are now in the body. Poison fill. Line 416 says "Fill poison with 64 typed row saves". That is the first option the recommendation offered. It is valid: each token owns disjoint slots [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:28-29 "Token i owns column (i % 16) of token block (i / 16) in every panel"], and 64 tokens x 128 dimensions = 8,192 elements = the whole plane [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:81-82 static_assert N_PANELS_16 * PANEL_ELEMS_512 == PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]. The poison bits survive a typed row save: scatter_row moves 32-bit lanes with _mm512_loadu_si512 and _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 and does no float conversion [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139-146], and line 405 keeps those instructions. So both POISON_0XA5A5 and the NaN poison 0x7FC1 [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:51, 257] are stored bit-exactly. The current direct plane writes at t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:107-109, 190-192, 286-288 are what this replaces. Index location. Line 391 says k_vnni::index is "the existing constexpr free function", moves it to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, and keeps its spelling. Source: constexpr size_t index(size_t token, size_t dim) noexcept in namespace tron::k_vnni [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:42, 101-107, 310]. The anchor cases (STATIC_REQUIRE = Catch2's compile-time assertion) call it by that spelling [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:80 using tron::k_vnni::index;, 81-90], as do the byte-position checks [:120, :143]. So they compile unchanged. Size fact. Line 401 states a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions. Source: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:22 "64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB". This is the size the memcmp against a same-size reference buffer [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:202, 229] needs, so the verifier's premise correction is also satisfied. Every checkable fact in the fix is right.

Resolved N58. Header split does not say where layout_on is defined (round 2, grade Note)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:391 "Move mapping constants, k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, and the existing constexpr free function k_vnni::index there [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp]." design-r3.txt:392 "The cache includes the K tensor header. h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header and retains software score arithmetic. self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly for qk_group. Neither tensor header includes an attention kernel header." Section 9: design-r3.txt:514 "... fix header ownership ..."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation (intent lens) had three sentences: (1) layout_on and the layout constants move to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp with the index mapping; (2) kv_cache.hpp includes only that header; (3) self_attention.hpp and amx_attn.cpp include h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp for qk_group. (1) is met by line 391. Today layout_on is defined in the kernel header [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:91-97, under #ifdef TRON_K_VNNI with a false fallback], the constants at :44-75, and index at :101-107. The design moves all three to the tensor header. (2) is met in substance by line 392 "The cache includes the K tensor header". kv_cache.hpp today includes the kernel header [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:27] and uses k_vnni::layout_on in 13 places [:1619, 1625, 1631, 1640, 1651, 1658, 1664, 1674, 1687, 1704, 1721, 1740, 2099]. With layout_on in the tensor header, the cache's requires-clauses compile from that include. The word "only" is absent, but the next sentence (self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly) implies the cache no longer provides the kernel header transitively. (3) is met for self_attention.hpp by line 392. Source: self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1-28 has no k_vnni include, and uses k_vnni::qk_group at :1636, k_vnni::layout_on at :1365, 1436, 1574, and k_vnni::PAGE_TOKENS_64 at :1633. The design's direct include supplies qk_group; layout_on and the constants arrive through the kernel header's include of the tensor header. amx_attn.cpp is not mentioned, which is harmless: it already includes the kernel header [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@30c4ac82cb:14]. No include cycle: the child's kernel header includes only standard and common/ headers [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:32-40], and line 392 forbids a tensor header from including a kernel header. The ambiguity the finding named (which header defines layout_on) is gone. One new omission was introduced by the rewrite; see new_defect.

New defect raised by the checker (minor): Claim: the round-3 rewrite of the header-split bullets dropped the sentence that placed the K storage operations in the tensor header, so the design no longer says which header defines store_row, load_row, store_block, the K token copy, and the K plane copy. Design quote: design-r3.txt:391 lists what moves to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp: the three types, "mapping constants, k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, and the existing constexpr free function k_vnni::index". design-r3.txt:392 says the kernel header "retains software score arithmetic". The typed operations are named only as callees: design-r3.txt:405 "Call typed store_row / load_row", :406 "Call store_block(writable_k_view, block, mask, rows)", :407 "Use typed K token copies and a typed K plane-copy operation". No sentence names their header. The round-2 text had it: "This header contains the K mapping and storage operations without including attention kernels" [design-wdiff.txt OLD segment at line 1332; round-2 design text]. Source evidence: kv_cache.hpp calls these operations today [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1705 scatter_row, 1729 store_block, 1741 gather_row, 2111-2113 gather_row + scatter_row], so the cache must see their definitions. If an implementer leaves them in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp, the cache must keep including the score reader, and "The cache includes the K tensor header" (design-r3.txt:392) is not sufficient. Why minor: the parent's parallel header v_vnni.hpp holds append, load, and token copy [design-r3.txt:258, 372], and "The parent uses the parallel filename v_vnni.hpp" [design-r3.txt:391] makes the intended reading likely. Recommendation: in design-r3.txt:391 add: "This header also defines the typed K storage operations store_row, load_row, store_block, the K token copy, and the K plane copy, so the cache needs no include of the kernel header."

source re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation asked the design to say: layout_on and the layout constants move to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp with the index mapping; kv_cache.hpp includes only that header; self_attention.hpp and amx_attn.cpp include h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp for qk_group. The design now says this, and the facts hold. Design text: "Move mapping constants, k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, and the existing constexpr free function k_vnni::index there [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp]" [design-r3.txt:391]. "The cache includes the K tensor header. h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header and retains software score arithmetic. self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly for qk_group. Neither tensor header includes an attention kernel header" [design-r3.txt:392]. Source check. Today kv_cache.hpp includes the kernel header [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:27] and uses layout_on (:1619-1674, :1687, :1704, :1721, :1740, :2099), BLOCK_TOKENS_16 (:1727-1728), scatter_row (:1705, :2113), gather_row (:1741, :2111) and store_block (:1729). After the move, layout_on and the constants live in the tensor header, and the raw scatter/gather/store_block calls become the typed store_row / load_row / store_block calls [design-r3.txt:405-406], so the tensor header is all kv_cache.hpp needs. self_attention.hpp has no direct include of the kernel header today [self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:21-28] and calls k_vnni::qk_group at :1636, so the new direct include is required and correct. amx_attn.cpp already includes the kernel header [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@30c4ac82cb:14] and uses only constants (:214-223), which it still reaches through the kernel header's include of the tensor header. The design's silence about amx_attn.cpp therefore costs nothing. No include cycle arises: the kernel header includes only standard and common/ headers today [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:32-40], and the design fixes the direction kernel -> tensor. One wording gap, low risk: the design does not say that kv_cache.hpp drops its #include "tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp" (the recommendation's word "only"). The drop is implied by "self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly". A stale include still compiles, so an implementer cannot build the wrong thing. Section 9 "fix header ownership" [design-r3.txt:514] matches the body change. Correction: Optional wording at design-r3.txt:392: "The cache includes only the K tensor header and drops its include of h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp." No factual correction to the checker's evidence.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): Corrected recommendation (intent and design-text lenses): layout_on and the layout constants move to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp with the index mapping; kv_cache.hpp includes only that header; self_attention.hpp and amx_attn.cpp include h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp for qk_group and the panel constants (amx_attn.cpp already does). The design now names the header for layout_on: "Move mapping constants, k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, and the existing constexpr free function k_vnni::index there [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp]" [design-r3.txt:391]. It states the include graph: "The cache includes the K tensor header. h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header and retains software score arithmetic. self_attention.hpp includes the kernel header directly for qk_group. Neither tensor header includes an attention kernel header." [design-r3.txt:392]. The facts hold. self_attention.hpp has no k_vnni include of its own [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:3-28] and uses k_vnni::layout_on (:1365, :1436, :1574), k_vnni::PAGE_TOKENS_64 (:1633) and k_vnni::qk_group (:1636) through kv_cache.hpp's include [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:27], so the direct include is the right instruction. amx_attn.cpp already includes the kernel header [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@30c4ac82cb:14], so no text is needed for it. The ambiguity the finding raised (which header defines layout_on) is gone. Two minor notes, no change required. (1) The word "only" is not written; the graph at 392 lists no cache-to-kernel edge, which implies kv_cache.hpp drops #include "tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp" (kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:27); keeping it would still compile, and make iwyu-check is optional for the parent [design-r3.txt:477]. (2) "mapping constants" leaves the kernel-only constants (FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF, LANES_16, BF16_BITS_16, HIGH_HALF_0XFFFF0000, MAX_KV_MUL_16 at h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:67-75) to the implementer; self_attention.hpp needs only layout_on and PAGE_TOKENS_64 from the tensor header, so either split compiles. The section-9 row "fix header ownership" [design-r3.txt:514] has matching body text.

Resolved N60. cmake preset flags vs make targets: cache caveats unstated (round 2, grade Note)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design-r3.txt:449 "Use a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair, with the normal gen/ build directory in each. Record compiler version, build type, flags, and generated compile definitions. Presets can accept a different -B directory, but repository Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it. Confirm the cached feature values after invoking them. [S17]" design-r3.txt:455 "Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target, or build with cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit after Debug configuration. Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo." design-r3.txt:477 "Run targeted suites, then make format, make lint, make build-test, and make test-host in the normal 16-lane AMX-off configuration." S17 link: design-r3-links.tsv:216 [Make test configuration] GNUmakefile#L538-L543 at 2880c3aa9b. Section 9 row: design-r3.txt:527 "... separate Make caches ..."

Checker assessment: The corrected recommendation (design-text lens, kept as a note) asked for one sentence under the table: the Make targets re-run cmake --preset over gen/ without the AVX512 and TRON_AMX_DISPATCH values, the required checks run in whichever configuration gen/ last held, they should run in the 16-lane AMX-off configuration, and configurations are switched by re-running the row's cmake line or by one worktree per configuration. The source-lens correction asked the design not to claim that three build directories are impossible, because cmake -B overrides the preset's binaryDir, but to say that the Make targets hardcode gen/. The design does all of this: one worktree per configuration (design-r3.txt:449); Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it (:449); cached feature values confirmed after invoking them (:449); presets accept a -B directory (:449); required checks in the 16-lane AMX-off configuration (:477). The Debug row (:455) also warns that plain Make defaults restore RelWithDebInfo. Facts checked at GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b. BUILD_TYPE := RelWithDebInfo (:80) is a plain Make variable, so make BUILD_TYPE=Debug overrides it. build-test depends on gen/config/test and runs cmake --build gen (:351-352). The gen/config/test recipe runs rm -rf gen/config then cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ... with no AVX512 or TRON_AMX_DISPATCH argument (:538-541). test-host depends on build-test-host (:905-906), which builds into gen (:369-370, :360-365). CMAKE_PRESET is native or cross-avx512 by /proc/cpuinfo (:227-231). CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:34 sets the native binaryDir to ${sourceDir}/gen. "may reconfigure" is the right hedge: the stamp gen/config/test re-runs cmake only when a prerequisite listed at :538 is newer, so a hand configure in gen/ is not always overwritten, and the design's instruction to confirm the cached values covers both cases.

source re-grader (Resolved): The design carries the corrected recommendation. It prescribes one worktree per baseline/head and configuration pair with the normal gen/ directory, says presets accept a different -B directory but repository Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it, and tells the implementer to confirm the cached feature values after invoking them [design-r3.txt:449]. The required checks (make format, make lint, make build-test, make test-host) run in the normal 16-lane AMX-off configuration, which is the configuration the design-text lens asked for [design-r3.txt:477]. The Debug row's Make usage is right [design-r3.txt:455]: BUILD_TYPE := RelWithDebInfo is a plain makefile assignment, so a command-line make BUILD_TYPE=Debug overrides it [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80]; the gen/config/test stamp rule re-runs cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) with no AVX512 or TRON_AMX_DISPATCH argument [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538-543, the S17 link range]; the per-test rule gen/t_%: gen/config/test runs cmake --build gen --target <name> and t_%: gen/t_% runs the binary [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:880-888]; build-test and test-host also depend on that stamp and use gen [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:351-353, 905-906]. The stamp's prerequisites do not include BUILD_TYPE, so a reconfigure happens only when a prerequisite is newer; the design's hedged wording ("may reconfigure", "can restore RelWithDebInfo") matches that. The native preset fixes binaryDir to gen [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:31-35] and the -B override statement follows the source-lens correction. The recommendation's literal sentence that AVX512 and TRON_AMX_DISPATCH persist only through gen/CMakeCache.txt is not quoted, but "Confirm the cached feature values after invoking them" states the same requirement in operational form. The checker's quotes exist at lines 449, 455, 477 and 527.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): The corrected recommendation (a note) asked the design to say that the hand-passed AVX512 and TRON_AMX_DISPATCH values survive the Make targets only through the CMake cache, that the Make targets reconfigure gen/ with their own flag list, that the required checks should run in the 16-lane AMX-off configuration, and that configurations are switched by a full reconfigure or by one worktree per configuration. The source lens added that -B overrides the preset's binaryDir while the Make targets hardcode gen/. The design now covers each point. It uses a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair with the normal gen/ directory in each [design-r3.txt:449]. It says presets can accept a different -B directory, but repository Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it, and tells the agent to confirm the cached feature values after invoking them [design-r3.txt:449]. It runs make format, make lint, make build-test, and make test-host in the normal 16-lane AMX-off configuration [design-r3.txt:477]. It says plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo after a Debug configuration [design-r3.txt:455]. Facts hold. build-test and test-host hardcode gen [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:351-352, 905-906]. The gen/config/test recipe re-runs 'cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ...' with no AVX512 or TRON_AMX_DISPATCH flag [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538-543], so the hand values persist only as cache entries. BUILD_TYPE defaults to RelWithDebInfo [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80]. The native preset pins binaryDir to gen [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:34]. Two notes, no change required. The design does not name gen/CMakeCache.txt; 'Confirm the cached feature values' gives the same instruction. 'A separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair' means up to 8 worktrees (2 revisions times 4 configurations); that is heavier than the source lens's alternative of a full reconfigure in gen/, but it is one of the options that lens allowed.

Major G01. scaled_v_expr is not named as a permitted user of detail::v_vnni_access, and its file home was dropped

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds: the design no longer says where detail::scaled_v_expr obtains the packed V address, and its helper rule does not say whether that class may use the friend. Every checkable fact is right. (1) detail::scaled_v_expr is cache code: kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1987-1990 opens namespace detail and the struct, :1992 stores const bf16s* const data, and the constructor at :2066-2069 takes a raw const bf16s* data. (2) The 16-lane body loads whole 64-byte pair tiles with _mm512_load_si512 and feeds them to _mm512_dpbf16_ps (:2019-2034, :2087-2090, :2102-2109; eight tiles per pair at head_size 128). page::scaled_v passes kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[0] at :2260-2261. (3) design-r3.txt:273 gives the 16-lane constructor "a packed read-only V view"; :248 says views expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion; :249 permits detail::v_vnni_access "only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels" and says "Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers"; :329 says "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" and names no mechanism. (4) The v_vnni.hpp operation list at :254 and step 1 at :371 names only append, load, and token copy; no weighted-sum operation is listed. Step 2 at :373 keeps "typed weighted-sum inputs" in kv_cache.hpp. (5) design-wdiff.txt @old 4447 shows the round-2 sentence "Keep typed scaled_v_expr here unless a real include dependency requires a separate header" in the deleted OLD segment with no NEW counterpart; grep of r2-findings.md finds no round-2 recommendation asking for that deletion (N24 only cited the sentence as evidence). (6) :39 defines a kernel as "a specific computation", which does not classify scaled_v_expr either way. (7) Reading through row.chunk (:245, one token's fp32 chunk extracted from the 64-byte pair chunk) would load each pair tile twice and replace the dpbf16 with extraction plus fp32 multiply-add, so it would change the instruction stream that :329 ("unrolled loops, and addition order") and the section-8 objdump comparison at :486 aim to preserve. Severity: minor, not major. Both admissible readings (friend use from kv_cache.hpp, or moving the body to v_vnni.hpp) preserve behavior, and the harmful third reading (row.chunk) is caught by the design's own instruction comparison at :486, which names weighted sums. The fix is one sentence. Major is defensible only if the DoD sentence at :496 must be mechanically checkable without an implementer's judgment call.
    Correction: Narrow the title and kind. Replace "two access rules conflict" with "the helper rule at :249 does not say whether scaled_v_expr counts as a V-specific kernel, and :329 names no mechanism"; the rules conflict only under the reading that scaled_v_expr is a "cache caller". Change kind from contradiction to ambiguity. Fix one citation: namespace detail opens at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1987, so cite :1987-1993 (not :1988-1993). Add the provenance fact: no round-2 finding asked to delete the placement sentence, so its removal (design-wdiff.txt @old 4447) is an unrequested loss of specificity relative to the round-2 text (evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:353). Keep the recommendation. Option A is the one consistent with step 2 (:373 keeps typed weighted-sum inputs in kv_cache.hpp) and with the deleted round-2 sentence, so present it as the default: add to :273 and :373 "detail::scaled_v_expr stays in kv_cache.hpp; its 16-lane constructor takes v_vnni_view<const bf16, page_size, head_size>, obtains the pair-tile base once through detail::v_vnni_access, and keeps today's _mm512_load_si512 / _mm512_dpbf16_ps loops (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2078-2119)", and amend :249 to name scaled_v_expr as the one kv_cache.hpp user of the helper. Drop the sentence "The definition-of-done sentence at :496 cannot be checked until that decision is written"; it can be checked once the implementer records which reading was used, so say instead "the DoD at :496 needs the classification of scaled_v_expr written down to be checkable without a judgment call."
  • design-text lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The finding holds in a narrowed form. The design keeps detail::scaled_v_expr in kv_cache.hpp by implication only: step 2, whose file is h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, says "Apply the accessor table, typed weighted-sum inputs, and explicit fill exception" [design-r3.txt:373], step 1 lists v_vnni.hpp's contents as "owner, view, row expression, append, load, and token copy" with no weighted sum [design-r3.txt:372], and section 5 names only append_v_row, load_row and copy_token as bodies that move into v_vnni.hpp [design-r3.txt:255-259]. So the finding's option (b), moving the weighted-sum body into v_vnni.hpp, is not an open reading of the text; that half of the finding is refuted. What the design does not say is how scaled_v_expr, staying in kv_cache.hpp, obtains the pair-tile address. Owners, views and rows expose no public pointer route [design-r3.txt:248]. The helper detail::v_vnni_access is allowed "only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels", and the same row says "Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers" [design-r3.txt:249]. Line 329 says "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" without naming the helper [design-r3.txt:329]; that sentence is not new, round 2 had it too [evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:316]. The design never classifies scaled_v_expr as a "V-specific kernel" or as a "cache caller", and the round-3 edit deleted the one sentence that placed it explicitly ("Keep typed scaled_v_expr here unless a real include dependency requires a separate header") [design-wdiff.txt segment @old 4447 / new 5912]. An implementer following the letter of "Cache callers ... do not use these helpers" could conclude that a struct defined in kv_cache.hpp may not call the helper, which leaves no compliant way to load whole 64-byte tiles as today's constructor does [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2066-2109: reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) then _mm512_load_si512(tile + k) into _mm512_dpbf16_ps]. Severity is minor, not major: the Words table defines a kernel as anything that "performs a specific computation" [design-r3.txt:39], line 329 requires preserving "unrolled loops, and addition order", and section 8 compares the weighted-sum instruction stream against the baseline [design-r3.txt:486-488], so an implementer reasoning by elimination lands on the friend helper, and a wrong choice (row.chunk reads) would be caught by that comparison rather than merged. The claim that the definition-of-done sentence at :496 "cannot be checked" is overstated: once scaled_v_expr is named a layout-specific kernel, "Packed physical indexing stays inside tensor operations and layout-specific kernels" [design-r3.txt:496] is checkable.
    Correction: Narrow the title to "scaled_v_expr is not named as a permitted user of detail::v_vnni_access". Drop "two access rules conflict": the rules at design-r3.txt:249 and :329 conflict only if scaled_v_expr is a cache caller, and the design leaves that classification unstated rather than contradicting itself. Drop option (b) from the claim: the design already places the weighted sum in kv_cache.hpp through step 2 ("typed weighted-sum inputs" in the kv_cache.hpp row, design-r3.txt:373), step 1 (v_vnni.hpp contents list no weighted sum, :372) and section 5 (only append_v_row, load_row, copy_token move, :255-259). Line 329 says the address is obtained "only inside the typed implementation" [design-r3.txt:329]. These are compatible when scaled_v_expr is the V-specific kernel that holds the typed implementation. The Words table defines a kernel as code that "performs a specific computation" [design-r3.txt:39], which scaled_v_expr does. Ben's sketch prescribes exactly this reading: "Physical-address access stays in a small internal helper used by SIMD and AMX implementations" and "kernels extract the pointer once and retain the existing instruction sequence" [github-review.json comments[3] body, lines 152 and 209]. The 16-lane weighted sum is a SIMD implementation. (2) "An implementer cannot tell whether (a) or (b)" is overstated. The remaining text points to option (a). Step 2, whose file is kv_cache.hpp, says "Apply the accessor table, typed weighted-sum inputs, and explicit fill exception" [design-r3.txt:373]. Section 9 says "Type both weighted-sum constructors" [design-r3.txt:520]. Section 5 and step 1 list only owner, view, row expression, append_v_row, load_row and copy_token as the v_vnni.hpp operations [design-r3.txt:253-259, :371], so no weighted-sum operation is planned there. Reading through row.chunk is already ruled out: line 329 requires "unrolled loops, and addition order" to be preserved, and the section 8 objdump comparison names "weighted sums" as a compared region [design-r3.txt:486]. A public tile route is ruled out by line 248 [design-r3.txt:248]. (3) "The definition-of-done sentence at :496 cannot be checked" is wrong. Under (a) the friend use sits inside a layout-specific kernel; under (b) it sits inside a tensor operation. Both satisfy "Packed physical indexing stays inside tensor operations and layout-specific kernels" [design-r3.txt:496]. Consequence for jhan's goal: none for merge or rebase. Either placement gives the same behavior and the same instruction stream. Ben's sketch sanctions kernel-side friend use. The child does not touch scaled_v_expr, v_data, v_base or weights_times_v: a grep of git diff c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp for those names returns nothing, although that diff changes 277 lines in those two files. What survives is one missing clause. The design never names scaled_v_expr as a user of detail::v_vnni_access, and it removed the sentence that fixed its file. An implementer who reads "Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers" [design-r3.txt:249] strictly, and sees that scaled_v_expr is defined in kv_cache.hpp, must infer from :373 and :486 that it is a kernel. One sentence removes that inference. The risk if the sentence is not added is low, so the severity is minor, not major.

Delete the sub-claims "two access rules conflict" and "the definition-of-done sentence at :496 cannot be checked". Replace "An implementer cannot tell whether (a) or (b)" with "The remaining text points to (a): step 2 places typed weighted-sum inputs under kv_cache.hpp [design-r3.txt:373], section 9 says 'Type both weighted-sum constructors' [:520], and the v_vnni.hpp operation list has no weighted sum [:253-259, :371]; the design should say so in one sentence." Minor G04. D5 says 'reuse the existing view alias'; the alias is new in this design

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. Row D5 says "Reuse the existing view alias" [design-r3.txt:99; HTML design-new-tensor-type.html line 95, no markup lost]. No alias named native_k_view or const_native_k_view exists in the repository: git grep over h, src and t finds no match at 2880c3aa9b (round-2 main) or 30c4ac82cb (the child), and a whole-tree grep at live main 1400fa4481 also finds none. The design itself introduces both aliases inside the new header h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp [design-r3.txt:232]. What does exist is the view type: kv_block::k_view() returns view<bf16, true, false, seq<page_size, head_size>> and, on a const block, const_view<...> [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2207-2219]. The design's explicit-stride alias names that same type, because seq = std::integer_sequence<size_t, ...> [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp@2880c3aa9b:22], sseq = std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, ...> [:25], and row_major<seq<R, C>> = sseq<C, 1> via the row-major seq_stride [:377-394]. Section 2's bullet uses the correct wording "the existing read-only matrix view" [design-r3.txt:76], so D5 contradicts it. The row is new in round 3: the word diff shows the D5 row only on the NEW side of the segment REPLACE @old 1384 / new 1918 [design-wdiff.txt:313-315], and the round-2 design text has no D5 row. Minor G09. Type constraints must be body static_asserts, not requires-clauses

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design states type constraints for the new owners and views but never says how to express them. design-r3.txt contains no "static_assert" at all. The word "requires" appears only in English prose (:213, :353) or for test probes (:438 "dependent requires concepts", :530). The constraints themselves are stated at :213, :240 ("Restrict T to bf16 or const bf16"), :283 ("positive even rows and positive columns divisible by chunk_size") and :401 ("Require 64-byte alignment ... and a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions"), each without a mechanism. Leg 1 (forward-declaration conflict) is confirmed. design-r3.txt:232 forward-declares v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row with unconstrained template-heads. design-r3.txt:234 says "Include only the standard headers needed for sizes and integer sequences." chunk_size is defined only in h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:86 (static const size_t chunk_size = TRON_CHUNK_SIZE;), and that header includes <immintrin.h> at :6, so kv_cache_fwd.hpp cannot name it. I compiled a test with g++ 11.4.0 and -std=c++20: an unconstrained forward declaration followed by a definition with requires(Rows > 0 && Rows % 2 == 0 && Cols > 0 && Cols % chunk_size == 0) fails with "error: redeclaration 'template<...> class v_vnni_tensor' with different constraints". The requires-clause is the local convention, not just the "natural C++20 form": kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:538-540 forward-declares scaled_v_expr as template <size_t page_size, size_t head_size> requires(head_size % chunk_size == 0) struct scaled_v_expr; and repeats the same clause at the definition (:1988-1990). That pattern only works because kv_cache.hpp can name chunk_size. An implementer following the codebase precedent would hit the error. Leg 2 (std::conditional_t) is confirmed as a language fact but is narrower than stated. design-r3.txt:399 names k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size> inside kv_block for every head size. k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:93 makes layout_on true only for HEAD_SIZE_128. Declared geometries include head sizes 64, 128 and 256 (t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:62-64; t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:836-838). With g++ 11.4.0 -std=c++20, kv_block<64, 64> fails to instantiate when k_vnni_tensor has requires(Cols == 128) ("template constraint failure ... constraints not satisfied"), although layout_on<64> is false. The same program compiles when the check is a static_assert in the class body, because the unselected specialization is never completed. It also compiles when the requires-clause is Ben's sketch constraint (Rows % 16 == 0, Cols % 32 == 0), and the design's own V constraints at :283 pass for every declared geometry (64, 128 and 256 are divisible by 16 and by 8; 64 tokens is even). So leg 2 bites only if the implementer turns the :401 owner size (64 tokens by 128 dimensions) into a class constraint. The design gives no K owner type constraint other than that size, so the misreading is possible. The reviewer-sketch reference is right: comment 5765866077 in evidence/github-review.json has static_assert(Tokens > 0 && Tokens % 2 == 0) in v_vnni_layout and static_assert(std::same_as<std::remove_const_t<T>, bf16>) in vnni_view; its vnni_tensor and vnni_view class templates carry no requires-clause. Severity minor is right. The failure is a compile error that stops the implementer at once, not a wrong build, and the fix is one or two sentences of design text.

Alias templates cannot be forward-declared. Say "three class forward declarations". 2. Replace the unverified clang diagnostic with the one measured here: g++ 11.4.0, -std=c++20, "error: redeclaration 'template<long unsigned int Rows, long unsigned int Cols> class v_vnni_tensor' with different constraints". However, the constraints the design itself states (even rows, columns divisible by chunk_size) and the sketch's K checks (Tokens % 16, Dims % 32) pass for every declared geometry: page_size 64 is even, and 64, 128 and 256 are all divisible by 16 and by 32. That is a plausible choice, because the design moves the child's mapping constants unchanged [design-r3.txt:389] and those constants hard-code 64 tokens by 128 dimensions (TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = PAGE_TOKENS_64 / 16, DIM_STEPS_4 = HEAD_SIZE_128 / 32, N_PANELS_16) [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:52-61], and the design asks for "a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions" [design-r3.txt:401]. The reviewer's sketch does use static_asserts inside the class bodies: k_vnni_layout (Tokens % 16, Dims % 32), v_vnni_layout (Tokens % 2, Dims > 0) and vnni_view (same_as<remove_const_t<T>, bf16>) [evidence/github-review.json, comment 5765866077]. The repo has precedent on both sides: kv_cache.hpp forward-declares scaled_v_expr with its requires(head_size % chunk_size == 0) repeated [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:539-540], which is possible there only because that header includes the intrinsics, and kv_block uses a body static_assert(sizeof(k) == sizeof(v)) [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2205]. The design does not pick a side, so the ambiguity is real for an implementer. Severity minor is right. Both failure modes are immediate compile errors, so nobody builds the wrong thing. But the implementer must then choose between breaking the intrinsics-free header rule and moving to static_asserts, and one sentence in the design removes that choice.

Minor G12. bf16_chunk override and decltype test protect a test-only path; the decltype check belongs in the header, not the suite

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Every checkable fact of the finding holds at the pinned sources. (1) The design names the section-8 host-tensor check as the only V expression consumer and says production V paths keep using bulk operations [design-r3.txt:242]. (2) The design mandates the override signature and concedes the fallback does not corrupt stored bits [design-r3.txt:247, :440 "Bit patterns alone cannot detect the bit-exact fallback"]. (3) The fallback is bit-exact: expr<B,N>::bf16_chunk returns fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)) when no override exists [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:111-117@2880c3aa9b]; fp32s_to_bf16s changes bits only where the exponent field equals 0x7f800000 and the low 16 bits are nonzero, or is a plain shift under TRON_IGNORE_NAN [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-108@2880c3aa9b]; the design's chunk(i) reuses even_part (shift left 16) and odd_part (mask high 16) [design-r3.txt:251; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2000-2007@2880c3aa9b], so the low 16 bits are always zero. (4) No production consumer exists: kv_cache.hpp on main contains no bf16_chunk (main's scaled_v_expr does not override it), and the only callers of bf16_chunk in the tree are h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:276,296,316,329,359, permuted.hpp:53 (its own override) and expr.hpp:715-716 (a forwarding wrapper) [git grep bf16_chunk 2880c3aa9b]. (5) The decltype sentence is new in round 3 and sits inside the "Behavior checks for the implementing agent" table [design-r3.txt:440; design-wdiff.txt INSERT @old 5487 / new 7529]. (6) N13 asked for a static_assert in the V header or the instruction record as the detection [batches/B08.md N13 RECOMMENDATION and design-text verifier correction]; the design placed a decltype check in the test suite instead, and its instruction-comparison list names even/odd V append, packed token copy, weighted sums and allocation/restore but not the bf16 read path [design-r3.txt:486-488], so neither of N13's two detectors is present. (7) The repository rule exists as cited [AGENTS.md:35-38@2880c3aa9b]. One wording slip: the rule does not flatly "forbid" structural assertions; it requires an identifiable consumer, compatibility requirement, or failure mode, and the design names none on a production path. Severity minor is right: no wrong values result either way, but an implementing agent following :440 would add a structural test assertion a reviewer applying AGENTS.md may reject, and the design text should choose between dropping the override and moving the check into the header.

The fallback is bit-exact: expr::bf16_chunk calls fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) when no override exists [expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:111-117]; fp32s_to_bf16s changes bits only where the exponent field is saturated and the low 16 bits are nonzero [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-109]; even_part shifts left by 16 and odd_part masks the high 16 bits, so the low 16 bits are zero [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2000-2007]. The ordinary contiguous bf16 view has no bf16_chunk override at main either: the only definitions are in dmatensor.hpp:367, permuted.hpp:53 and expr.hpp:111/322/715 (git grep at 2880c3aa9b over h/, src/, t/). So a row that relies on the fallback follows the existing view convention. On the check's location: the round-2 N13 recommendation asked for a static_assert in the header and asked section 8 to name that static_assert or the instruction record as the detection [r2-findings.md N13 RECOMMENDATION]. The design writes 'Verify the member-pointer type' with no location [design-r3.txt:247] and lists the decltype check as evidence produced in the 'existing tensor/cache cases' row of the behavior-check table [design-r3.txt:440]. The decltype sentence is new in round 3 [design-wdiff.txt:1600]. An implementer cannot tell whether the check is a header static_assert or a suite STATIC_REQUIRE. The design also dropped N13's cost statement ('adds a shift, NaN check, and narrow per chunk'), so the text gives no benefit for the mandated override. Two corrections. First, 'which the repository's test rules forbid' is too strong. AGENTS.md requires that a structure assertion have an identifiable consumer, user-visible behavior, compatibility requirement, or failure mode that makes it important to preserve [AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:35-38]. The design names a failure mode ('a missing direct-bit override') but its own text removes the consequence (bit-exact fallback), so the justification is weak rather than absent. A header static_assert is not a test and is outside the test policy. Second, the design followed round 2: N13 asked for the override plus a member-pointer check, and N52 said to keep the row's bf16_chunk body [r2-findings.md N52 lead claim]. So this is a new simplicity finding on the round-3 text, not an unresolved or regressed N13. Severity minor: the design text should state a rationale and a location, and the risk of leaving it is a few dead lines and a possible reviewer objection to a structural STATIC_REQUIRE. The decltype check itself is technically right: an inherited member has type bf16s (expr<Row,D>::*)(size_t) const noexcept, so std::is_same against bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept distinguishes the two cases.

The central fact holds. book::fill_random draws every element from std::normal_distribution<>(0.0, 1.0) and fill_storage_slot casts each double to bf16 [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1054-1065 (comment "Fill all kv_block data with random values ... bypasses the zero-init V slot invariant"; :1059 std::normal_distribution<> dis(0.0, 1.0);), :1365-1374 (:1373 data[i] = static_cast<bf16>(distribution(gen));)]. Every written value is finite. No NaN and no sentinel bit pattern is written. The child leaves the function unchanged [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1125-1131, 1433]. The design's new row says "Keep its poison-fill behavior and existing lifecycle-test callers" [design-r3.txt:274; HTML line 226 has no definition or title attribute on the phrase]. That row is new in round 3 [design-wdiff.txt:882-883, INSERT @old 3183 / new 4305]. The round-2 text used "poison" only at design-revised-text.txt:285, :395, :473, none about fill_random. The NaN poison in the existing t_llama_unit tests is written through page::set_v with a quiet_NaN source row, not through fill_random [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1919-1925, :2701-2705, :2788-2792]. The finding's design_quote and section citations (:262, :274, :441) match the text. The round-3 text now assigns only the three types, the mapping constants, layout_on and index to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [design-r3.txt:391]. 3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claims hold against the primary source at 2880c3aa9b (byte-identical kv_cache.hpp at live main 1400fa4481 per facts-r3.md:42-43). (1) for_each_active_slot enumerates descriptor indices, not physical offsets: for_each_slot_impl expands std::index_sequence<n_slots> and passes kv_slot_specs[slots].geometry (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1236-1240); for_each_active_slot keeps only slot < logical_slot_count() (:1243-1249). The lambda receives a slot index; the caller forms the storage offset itself, as fill_random does with kv_storage_offset(slot) (:1060-1061). The design's phrase 'dispatches the physical slot' (design-r3.txt:350) is therefore loose, and its filter 'storage_location(offset, ...)' uses an 'offset' the bullet never forms. (2) 'logical alias' is undefined: it occurs once in the design (design-r3.txt:350); the Words table defines 'slot' only (design-r3.txt:32), not logical slot, physical slot, or alias; every other 'alias' in the design means a type alias or pointer aliasing (design-r3.txt:99, 267, 518, 529). (3) No alias can occur in the heterogeneous enumeration: make_kv_slot_offsets assigns each slot one prefix in one arena (:651-670); storage_location reads offsets.values[offset.i] and slot_specs[offset.i] (:727-735); heterogeneous_kv_cache is built on fixed_kv_layout with allow_layer_prefix = false (heterogeneous_kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:36-37, kv_cache.hpp:745). The shift is consumed only by the kv_block accessor that requires(layout_t::uniform_geometry) (:1277-1300) via kv_blocks_alias (:1222-1227); kv_block_at_storage<geometry> (:1309-1335) does not read it. The one many-to-one relation in the code is operations sharing a slot (Note [KV slot retention], :113-115 'Several operations can consume one slot'), and a per-slot loop visits such a slot once, so no deduplication is needed under that reading either. (4) The sentence is carried over: design-revised-text.txt:332 has 'Do not construct the same region again for a logical alias.' verbatim; design-wdiff.txt:1071 shows it as OLD context; grep of r1-findings.md and r2-findings.md for 'logical alias' and 'same region again' finds nothing, and the round-2 M04/N25 texts and corrections (r2-findings.md '### M04', '### N25') never mention it. Severity minor: the effect for logical slots is unchanged (offset.i == slot for every logical slot, :906-907, :1060-1061), and the next bullet (design-r3.txt:351) already states the only real duplicate-construction hazard, so an implementer builds the right thing but may waste effort on a case that cannot occur.

Its three central claims check out against the design text and the source at 2880c3aa9b (byte-identical to live main 1400fa4481 for kv_cache.hpp, facts-r3.md:42-43). (1) The helper visits logical slot indices, not physical slots. for_each_active_slot iterates every index of kv_slot_specs and keeps only slot < logical_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1243-1249]. logical_slot_count is documented as "The number of logical K/V slots described by this cache's active layout" [:918-921]. The caller forms the storage offset itself: fill_random passes kv_storage_offset(slot) [:1060-1061], and the heterogeneous kv_block<geometry> accessor passes kv_storage_offset(slot.i) [:1355]. The design bullet instead says the helper "dispatches the physical slot" [design-r3.txt:350]. The round-2 M04 recommendation the design adopted said "for each active logical slot" (r2-findings.md, M04 RECOMMENDATION), so the wording drifted from logical to physical during the fix. (2) "logical alias" is undefined. The word "alias" appears in the design only at design-r3.txt:99, 262, 267, 284, 350, 516, 518, 529; every other use is about the native-K view alias or C++ aliasing. The Words table [design-r3.txt:28-60] does not define "logical alias", "physical slot" or "storage offset". The bullet also uses the variable offset in "storage_location(offset, logical_slot_count())" [design-r3.txt:350] without saying how offset is formed from the lambda's slot; the design never mentions kv_storage_offset (grep of design-r3.txt: 0 hits). (3) No two enumerated slot indices share one physical region. kv_slot_spec carries only geometry and retention, no alias or shared-storage field [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:154-159]. make_kv_slot_offsets computes one prefix per slot [:654-670]; storage_location returns offsets.values[offset.i] [:727-735]; slot_base adds arena + n_pages * byte_offset [:1188]. The only mechanism that maps a logical slot to a different physical slot is storage_view_offset_, written by set_storage_view/reset_storage_view [:892-902], and it exists only for EAGLE, which requires uniform geometry [:771, :788-789, :1158-1159]. So the heterogeneous enumeration cannot meet an alias, and the caution "Do not construct the same region again for a logical alias" [design-r3.txt:350] warns against a case that cannot occur there. (4) Provenance is right: the sentence is OLD context in the word diff [design-wdiff.txt:1071], it is present verbatim in the round-2 text [claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:332], and 'logical alias' has 0 hits in r1-findings.md and r2-findings.md. Effect on an implementer: low. For the enumerated slots the logical index and the storage offset have the same numeric value, so kv_storage_offset(slot) is the natural step and gives the right region. The residual risks are the ones the finding names: hunting for a physical-offset loop the helper does not provide, or adding a deduplication set for an impossible case. Section 9 row "N25 M04" [design-r3.txt:521] and the EAGLE bullet [design-r3.txt:351] do not cure the wording. Minor is the right severity; the design should change the two sentences, but nothing wrong gets built if it does not.
    Correction: Three narrowings; the verdict and the recommended replacement text stand. (a) Narrow "cannot occur in a fixed layout". Sharing does exist in fixed layouts, one level above slots: the design's own Words table says "A slot is a cache region used by one layer or shared by several layers" [design-r3.txt:32], and Note [KV slot retention] says "Several operations can consume one slot" [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:113-116]. That is a layer-to-slot or operation-to-slot mapping. for_each_active_slot iterates slot indices [:1243-1249], not layers or operations, so it visits each slot once. Restate the claim as: "no two slot indices of the enumeration map to one physical region, and layer-to-slot sharing happens above the slot index, so it cannot cause double construction in a slot-indexed loop." (b) Fix the storage_view_offset_ citation. It is not "used only inside the uniform kv_block accessor". It is also read by refresh_kv_blocks_alias [:1224, :1227], which sets kv_blocks_alias, and kv_blocks_alias is read by the uniform_reclaimability branch of the uniform accessor [:1285-1288]. The substantive point survives: kv_block_at_storage [:1311-1336], the path the heterogeneous construction and fill_storage_slot [:1366-1373] use, calls slot_base(offset) directly and never consults storage_view_offset_. (c) Add one fact to the evidence: the round-2 M04 recommendation (which section 9 row "N25 M04" [design-r3.txt:521] claims to have applied) said "for each active logical slot, as fill_random does"; the design's "dispatches the physical slot" is a departure from that corrected text, so this is a small slip introduced by the round-2 fix, not an error inherited unchanged. Recommended text (unchanged in substance, one citation added): "Reuse book::for_each_active_slot, which calls the lambda once per active logical slot index with that slot's compile-time geometry (kv_cache.hpp:1243-1249). Form the storage offset as kv_storage_offset(slot), as fill_random does (:1060-1061). Filter on layout_t::storage_location(kv_storage_offset(slot), logical_slot_count()).reclaimable. A fixed layout maps each slot index to one distinct physical region (make_kv_slot_offsets :654-670), so no deduplication is needed." Delete "Do not construct the same region again for a logical alias." The EAGLE bullet [design-r3.txt:351] already carries the only real double-construction caution and needs no change.

M04's corrected recommendation said "for each active logical slot"; the design wrote "physical slot" instead. Intent lens: this does not make the parent PR unbuildable or unacceptable to Ben. The bullet's operative instructions (filter by storage_location(...).reclaimable, construct n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at slot_base, no EAGLE branch) are right. The cost is implementer time spent looking for an alias mechanism that does not exist, or a needless deduplication set. That is a wording change the design should make, low risk if it does not: minor, not note, because the design elsewhere uses "physical KV slot" for the EAGLE slot [design-r3.txt:351], so the same bullet now uses "physical slot" in two incompatible senses.

Minor G21. Adding reinterpret_cast to the rg completion search makes it unusable

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central facts hold. (1) The round-3 pattern contains reinterpret_cast and is run over h, src and t [design-r3.txt:382]. The design says the second run "checks for obsolete calls and comments" [design-r3.txt:380]. (2) The round-2 pattern had none of fill_storage_slot, fill_random or reinterpret_cast [design-revised-text.txt:360; design-wdiff.txt REPLACE @old 4685 / new 6118]. (3) git grep -c reinterpret_cast 2880c3aa9b -- h src t sums to 979 matching lines in 74 files, exactly as the finding states. (4) No sentence of the design states a cast rule that this alternative would enforce. The word "cast" appears only at design-r3.txt:262, 344, 352, 355, 382 and 393, and none of those lines says what the implementer should look for among reinterpret_cast hits. The section-9 row for M02/M07 [design-r3.txt:529] does not mention the search. So the purpose of the added alternative is unstated, and the recommendation to scope it and say what it is for is sound. One detail of the finding is wrong (see correction): the other alternatives do not match "a few dozen lines". Severity minor is right. An implementer still reaches the right sites; the cost is a 1491-line list instead of a 514-line list, and an unexplained alternative.
    Correction: Narrow two statements and refine the recommendation. (a) Replace "The other alternatives match a few dozen lines" with measured numbers at 2880c3aa9b over h, src and t: without reinterpret_cast the pattern matches 514 lines in 74 files (get_v 136 lines, of which 122 are get_vocab_size, get_value, get_vocabulary_data and similar substrings, not get_v calls; set_v 112; v_base 82; v_data 79; scaled_v 70; fill_random 12; append_v 10; qk_rowmajor_128x4 9; weights_times_v_128x4 7; fill_storage_slot 3). With reinterpret_cast the whole pattern matches 1491 lines in 124 files. So reinterpret_cast supplies 979 of 1491 lines (66 percent) and adds 50 files that no other alternative touches, such as t/t_hwattention.cpp (17 lines) and t/t_mwaitx.cpp (12 lines). (b) Replace "stops being a completion test" with "was never a zero-hit test and now triples in size". The pattern keeps fill_random and fill_storage_slot, which the design says to preserve [design-r3.txt:262, 274], so a non-empty result is expected even after a correct migration. The defect is that the design does not say what the implementer should look for among the reinterpret_cast hits. (c) Refine the scoped command with the expected residue. Minor G22. The t_amx_numerics PV case cannot keep its hand-packed std::vector V page; no permitted typed route is named

2 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds: the design gives the PV numerics case no named route for its V page. Verified facts. (1) The test builds its V page by hand: std::vector<tron::bf16> v_page filled with v_page[(pair * HEAD_SIZE_128 + d) * 2 + j] [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:197-211], passes v_page.data() to weights_times_v_128x4 [:226-227], and its reference reads v_page with the same pair formula [:238-239]. (2) The design's typed kernel takes v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> by value [design-r3.txt:277]. (3) Owners, views and rows expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member or pointer conversion [:248]; tests do not use detail::v_vnni_access [:249]; the owner has no expression constructor or assignment [:288]. So the hand-packed vector cannot be passed or wrapped. (4) The permitted routes that remain are real but unnamed: the owner is trivially default-constructible with as_view() & [:238-239], writable element access exists [:245], append_v_row exists [:252-253], and a trivially copyable owner accepts memcpy. The design chooses among these only for the child's t_k_vnni_layout ("Fill poison with 64 typed row saves. Copy the trivially copyable owner's bytes to a test buffer") [:416]. (5) The design names t_amx_numerics.cpp once, in step 6 [:377]; the round-2 step 6 said only "source-row fixtures" [design-revised-text.txt:357]. Section 8 has no row about the PV fixture; its "16 lanes, AMX code on" row only says real numerical results need AMX hardware [:449-453]. Section 9's N22 row covers the K plane wrap only [:518], and its N15 row covers alignment only [:519]. (6) Not a re-raise: neither r1-findings.md nor r2-findings.md mentions v_page or the PV fixture lines; N22's verifier corrections name only in->k [r2-findings.md, N22]. (7) The recommendation's facts check out: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions x 2 bytes = 16,384 bytes; today's bf16 set_v body zero-extends and shifts stored bits with no numeric conversion, using aligned loads [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2295-2318], so "the bf16 input path keeps exact bits" is right; an explicit const_native_k_view wrap stays legal [:267]. Severity minor as filed: any of the three routes yields a working test, so an implementer would not build the wrong production code, but the design text should choose one.
    Correction: Three narrowings. (a) Reword the reading of step 6: "explicit aligned row wrappers" [design-r3.txt:377] is not K-only. "Explicit ... wrap" is the N22 language for the K plane, and "aligned row wrappers" is the N15 language for append_v_row source rows. The phrase therefore hints at the append_v_row route for V, but step 6 never says that the PV case must replace its hand-packed std::vector page with an owner, which fill route to use, or what happens to the test's own interleave formula and its pair-formula reference. Replace "which fits the K array ... but not V" with "which names a K plane wrap and V source-row wraps but does not say that the PV case's std::vector page itself must move into an owner". (b) Soften the :352 citation: "Do not construct in an accessor or cast an existing SIMD array object into the new owner" [:352] is an arena-construction rule about kv_block's SIMD array; a memcpy of bytes into a trivially copyable owner is not a cast, so the design text leaves the memcpy route unaddressed rather than forbidden. The finding's advice "Do not memcpy the hand-packed buffer into the owner" stands as a recommendation, not as an existing design rule. (c) Fix two line ranges: the hand-packed fill starts at the comment on :197 (cite :197-211, not :198-211), and the reference read is :238-239 (not :236-239). Optional addition to the recommendation: the reference loop can read the logical float array v through bf16_rne (vv = bf16_to_float(bf16_rne(v[t * HEAD_SIZE_128 + d]))), which needs no layout formula at all; the byte-copy comparison is then the only place the pair formula survives.
  • design-text lens: refuted (high confidence, severity note). The first half of the finding is confirmed. The typed kernel takes v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> by value [design-r3.txt:277]. Owners, views and rows have no public raw-pointer constructor [design-r3.txt:248]. Tests do not use detail::v_vnni_access [design-r3.txt:249]. So the PV case can no longer pass v_page.data() [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203-227]. The second half, "no permitted typed route is named", is false. The design names the fixture route in section 6: "Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append" [design-r3.txt:317]. The table row above it defines that write: no read of other elements, other elements unchanged [design-r3.txt:313]. Section 5 makes the route usable from a test: the owner is one 64-byte-aligned bf16 array with trivial default construction [design-r3.txt:240], as_view() exists for lvalue owners [design-r3.txt:241], writable matrix[token][dimension] changes only that element [design-r3.txt:245], and append_v_row is a public operation taking an aligned bf16 source row [design-r3.txt:252-257]. An implementer reading sections 5 and 6 therefore builds a v_vnni_tensor<64,128> (16,384 bytes), fills it by element writes or 64 append_v_row calls, and passes owner.as_view(). That is not an ambiguity that leads to a wrong build. Three parts of the finding are also inaccurate. (1) It cites design-r3.txt:352 as forbidding a cast of existing storage into the owner; that sentence is an arena-construction rule about the kv_block SIMD array, not a rule about test buffers. (2) "Do not memcpy the hand-packed buffer into the owner" is the finder's rule, not the design's; the design is silent on copying bytes into a trivially copyable owner, and that route is the one that would keep the test's present independence from production packing code. (3) "fill it with 64 append_v_row calls" is one of two permitted routes; the design's own fixture sentence points at element mutation [design-r3.txt:317]. What remains true is small. Step 6 lists t/t_amx_numerics.cpp but names only "explicit aligned row wrappers" [design-r3.txt:377], which is the K route [design-r3.txt:267]; it does not say the PV page becomes an owner. The design also does not carry its t_k_vnni_layout pattern (typed fill, then copy the owner's bytes out for the physical-layout comparison) [design-r3.txt:416] to the V numerics case, so it does not say whether the test's independent interleave formula [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:207, :239] survives as a layout check. That is a note, not a defect that changes what gets built.
    Correction: Narrow to a note on step 6 [design-r3.txt:377]: "The PV case of t/t_amx_numerics.cpp [2880c3aa9b:203-227] replaces its std::vector<bf16> page with a v_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> owner (16,384 bytes, 64-byte aligned, default-constructed). Fill it through the public typed operations, either element writes [design-r3.txt:317] or append_v_row from 64-byte-aligned bf16 rows [design-r3.txt:252-257], and pass owner.as_view() to weights_times_v_128x4. Keep the case's independent physical-layout formula [2880c3aa9b:207, :239] as a check by copying the owner's bytes to a test buffer, as section 7 prescribes for t_k_vnni_layout [design-r3.txt:416]. The QK case keeps its raw K array through an explicit const_native_k_view wrap [design-r3.txt:267]." Drop the citation of design-r3.txt:352 (an arena rule, not a test rule) and drop "Do not memcpy the hand-packed buffer into the owner" (not a design rule; the design is silent on it). Relates to N22 (K wrap) and N15 (aligned rows); neither asked for this V-test text.
  • intent lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. Consequence for jhan's goal: the implementing agent hits a compile error at t_amx_numerics.cpp:226 and has to pick a route the design does not name; step 6's wording points at a route that does not exist for V. (2) In the recommendation, replace "Do not memcpy the hand-packed buffer into the owner" with "State whether a memcpy of hand-packed bytes into the trivially copyable owner is allowed in tests. Prefer the append_v_row route, which keeps the pair formula inside the type, and keep any independent formula check on bytes copied OUT of the owner, as :416 prescribes for t_k_vnni_layout." A memcpy into a trivially copyable owner is legal C++, so the design should choose, not the finder. (3) Keep the rest: the evidence lines are right (v_page fill at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203-211, kernel call :226-227, reference read :239), the owner size 64 x 128 x 2 bytes = 16,384 bytes is right, and an alignas(64) owner works as a local or through std::make_unique (C++17 aligned new).
