Minor G25. Successful Slice case logs: location, runner, 10-run pruning and fallback are not stated

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design makes the Slice log files the proof of case execution and tells the implementer to preserve or link them [design-r3.txt:469], but no sentence of the design says where they are, that they are short-lived on the runner, which runner, where the store paths come from, or what to do when the runner cannot be reached. A grep of design-r3.txt for logs-, runner, hostname, retention, oldest, handoff and "Select test reuse" hits only line 469. The S19 link "[Captured test logs and command headers]" points at bin/slice#L3159-L3187 as code, not as a statement [design-r3-links.tsv:232]. The cited source facts are right: LOGS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / f"logs-{HOSTNAME}" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:81, HOSTNAME at :72], RETENTION = 10 [:114], the prune loop [:2766-2768], run_dir [:2770], per-test log path run_dir / f"{name}.log" [:3148] with stdout and stderr redirected into it [:3174-3187], emit_failures echoes tails only for failed tests [:2992-3016], the upload step runs only on failure with path logs-*/run-* [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:581-588], runner labels [:535], tron-test-host = exec bin/slice run --filter=host [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-35; gcp-nix.yml:571-573], Catch2 lines per section [t/testlog.cpp@2880c3aa9b:17-25], SKILL.md names only the local logs-$(hostname)/latest/ location [.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:78], README.ci.md has no logs- text (git grep: no match). Two details are off and one mechanism is incomplete: (1) log_f = open(...) is at :3174, not :3172. (2) The "Logs: <run_dir>" line [:4181] is printed right after allocate_run_dir() [:4180], before any test runs, and a passing job log also shows one status line per test (status, tag, test name, instance, duration [:2924], printed as plain text when stderr is not a TTY [:6168, :6188-6191]) plus a final "N passed, M skipped, K failed" line [:4545-4550]. Case names appear in the console only for failed tests [:2929-2934]. So "no per-case output" is right; "only a final Logs: line" is not. (3) The dominant deletion mechanism on the CI runner is not Slice retention. The Test host job's checkout step [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:540-542] uses actions/checkout@de0fac2e (v6) with no clean: input, and that action's default is clean: true = "git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD before fetching" (action.yml at that commit, lines 57-59, read with gh api). logs-*/ is gitignored [.gitignore@2880c3aa9b:68] and -x removes ignored paths, so the run directory is deleted at the next job that checks out on that runner. Slice's 10-run limit [doc/slice.md@2880c3aa9b:246 "One log per test, retention 10"] applies only if the directory survives that long. This shortens the window the finding describes and strengthens its conclusion. Severity minor is right: the design already names the evidence and the failure-only upload, so an implementer who cannot find the logs must report missing evidence rather than build the wrong thing, but the text should say how and when to collect it.
    Correction: Narrow the claim in three places and fix two citations. All these files are unchanged at live main 1400fa4481 (git diff --stat 2880c3aa9b 1400fa4481 on bin/slice, doc/slice.md, the skill, t/testlog.cpp, README.ci.md, gcp-nix.yml is empty). Live confirmation from an executed, passing Test host job (run 35458087510, job 105939764467, 2026-09-19, runner andoria-09-0): the job log holds 0 lines containing "Catch2" and 89 per-test result lines; the two suites appear as "passed t_llama_unit inst 1,8 4.3s" (log line 344) and "passed t_heterogeneous_scheduler inst 7,8 0.9s" (line 369); the run directory is printed as "Logs: /opt/positron/runners/andoria-09-0/_work/tron/tron/logs-andoria-09/run-0000" (line 313). A second executed job (105818071267, runner delphi-3af6-0) shows the same pattern (0 Catch2 lines, 76 per-test lines, run-0000). So the per-case Catch2 lines exist only in the per-test log files on the runner, which is the finding's central claim. Two parts of the finding need correction. First, the job log is not "only a final Logs: line": it carries one result line per test binary, and the Logs: line is printed before the tests run (bin/slice:4181 precedes the run loop; live log line 313 precedes lines 344 and 369). The job log therefore proves that the test binary ran and passed, but not which Catch2 cases ran. Second, the recommended source for the store paths is not the simplest one: the Test host job's own "Restore exact Nix test runtime" step prints both paths as "Preparing test runtime: <test-runtime store path>; environment=<environment store path>" [bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:133-136; live job 105939764467 log line 159]. One fact the finding understates: the 10-run retention is not the shortest lifetime. The checkout step of every Test host job runs git clean -ffdx in the runner workspace [live job 105939764467 log line 48; job 105818071267 log line 60; actions/checkout default clean]. That command removes every untracked path, including logs-<host>/. Both observed jobs allocated run-0000, consistent with no earlier run directory surviving. So the logs must be copied before the next gcp-nix job checks out on that runner's workspace, which can be minutes, not after 10 runs. Severity stays minor: the design already says the logs are not uploaded and must be preserved or linked, so an implementer who cannot find them would report a gap rather than record a false claim. The design text should still change, because the requirement as written cannot be met without facts the design does not give.

  • intent lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design names the per-case Catch2 lines in the Slice logs-*/run-* files as the proof of which cases executed and tells the implementer to preserve or link them [design-r3.txt:469]. That line is the only place the design mentions those files. The words "runner", "hostname", "latest", "retention" and "Set up job" appear nowhere in the design (grep of design-r3.txt). The design therefore gives no location, no retrieval window, no runner identification and no fallback. The sources the finding cites are right: LOGS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / f"logs-{HOSTNAME}" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:81]; RETENTION = 10 [:114]; pruning of the oldest run directories while 10 or more exist [:2766-2768]; run_dir = LOGS_DIR / f"run-{next_num:04d}" [:2770]; the test's stdout and stderr go to the per-test log file, not the console [:3173-3186]; the console gets only "Logs: <run_dir>" [:4181], a final "N passed, M skipped, K failed" count line [:4546-4549], failed names [:4553] and failure tails [:2992-3016]. The Test host job runs on [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512] [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:535], runs tron-test-host [:571-573] = exec bin/slice run --filter=host [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-35], and uploads logs-*/run-* only on failure [:581-588]. The run-tron-tests skill names only the local logs-$(hostname)/latest/ path [SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:78]; README.ci.md has no logs- retrieval text (grep, no match). Intent: AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 makes execution verification mandatory before committing a test, and the design converted that into a concrete evidence demand in response to N36 [design-r3.txt:469, :498, :525]. As written the demand cannot be followed after the fact, so an implementing agent either stalls or records the green check alone. This does not block merge or Ben's acceptance, so minor, not major. Two parts of the finding need narrowing (see correction): the loss mechanism in CI is the next job's checkout clean, not the 10-run pruning, and the job log carries a count summary line in addition to the Logs line.
    Correction: 1. Loss mechanism: in CI the binding limit is not Slice's 10-run pruning. Every job on the fpga test runners uses actions/checkout@v6 with no clean: input [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:444-457, :535-542, :602-607]. That action's clean input defaults to true and runs git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD before fetching [actions/checkout action.yml at de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd, lines 57-59, read via gh api]. git clean -ffdx removes untracked and ignored directories, so logs-<hostname>/ under the checkout is deleted by the next job that checks out in the same runner workspace (Wait for lab cache, Test host, or Test FPGA on that runner). Reword: "the directory survives only until the next job checks out in that runner workspace; Slice's own 10-run retention [bin/slice:114, 2766-2768] applies to local checkouts." Insufficient data: whether the runners are configured ephemeral cannot be read from the repository; either way the window is at most one job. 2. Job-log content: a passing run's GitHub job log shows the "Logs: <run_dir>" line [bin/slice:4181] and a final "N passed, M skipped, 0 failed, makespan" count line [:4546-4549]; it shows no test names and no per-case Catch2 lines. Replace "only a final Logs line" with that. 3. Store paths: they are readable closer than the Build Tron job. The Test host job's step "Restore exact Nix test runtime" carries TRON_BUILD_STORE_PATH and TEST_ENVIRONMENT_STORE_PATH as step env from needs.tron-build.outputs [gcp-nix.yml:549-556], which the job log prints in the step header, and the uploaded artifact tron-test-runtime (test-runtime.json) carries the receipt [:508-514]. 4. Soften "the false-evidence case N36 warned about": the N36 verifier correction established that a green Test host with an executed (not skipped) Test host step is execution evidence at the test-binary level; what is missing without the Slice log is only the case-level proof the design itself demands. 5. Shorter recommended design text for design-r3.txt:469 (replace the last two sentences): "A successful run uploads nothing. Its job log shows Slice's Logs: <checkout>/logs-<runner hostname>/run-NNNN line and a pass count, no case names. The per-case Catch2 lines exist only in that directory on the self-hosted runner, and the next job's checkout removes it. Read the runner name from the job's Set up job step, copy the t_llama_unit and t_heterogeneous_scheduler logs from that run directory right after the run, and attach or link them in the PR. If the runner is not reachable, record the run URL, attempt number, the executed Test host step, and the store paths from the Restore exact Nix test runtime step, then add a local run of the same binaries and filter with its Catch2 lines, labeled local execution, not CI execution. Uploading successful logs is a separate CI decision for the user and CI owners."

No code path compares a record against the test's current cost. The --check help text says "verify CTest manifest entries are present in the benchmarks JSON" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:6435-6438]. The live rollup of PR 4479 (merged 2026-09-22 06:28 UTC) lists all 13 README names as individual checks (Lint, CI machinery tests, Fresh Cabal plan, Prepare Tron build inputs, Build ingest, Test ingest, Build model traces, Generate model plugins, Wait for lab cache, Build Tron, Test host, Test FPGA, Test). (2) Lint: design-r3.txt:477 already commands make format and make lint, and the CI Lint check blocks merge on its own. (4) Labels: design-r3.txt:156 and :395 already state "Add Skip benchmarks to both PRs. Do not add Run CI without explicit user direction. These are repository rules." [AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:14-18]. The fourth omission has a small real consequence. The repository rule requires a refresh after materially changing a test [t/AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:23-26]. An implementer can therefore declare the parent done with neither a refreshed record nor a recorded deferral. That is a text gap worth one sentence, low risk if left: minor. Minor G49. AMX-on row asks for 'evidence that the kernel ran' without naming a method

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The AMX-on row says "Real numerical results require compatible AMX hardware and evidence that the kernel ran" and names no artifact [design-r3.txt:453]. The rule two lines above excludes "hardware-unavailable early returns" from feature execution [design-r3.txt:445]. The only execution evidence the design names is the "Catch2 starting" / "Catch2 passed" lines in the Slice run logs [design-r3.txt:469]. Those lines cannot separate an executed AMX case from a skipped one. Reason: both AMX precision cases begin with if (!tron::amx_attn_h128g4::available()) { WARN("AMX unavailable on this host - QK precision check skipped"); return; } (QK) and the PV counterpart [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:145-147, 189-191]. WARN adds no failed assertion, so the listener still logs "Catch2 passed" for that test case [t/testlog.cpp@2880c3aa9b:21-25; Catch2 reports the test-case body as its root section - Catch2 behavior, not verified in-repo]. The child adds a third such early return for the VNNI QK identity check [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@30c4ac82cb:199-201; the design's own S13 link "AMX availability check" points there, design-r3.txt:577]. available() is declared as true only when CPU, OS and per-process permission allow AMX and TRON_AMX_DISABLE is not "1" [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:167-170]; the getenv check is in detect_and_request [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@2880c3aa9b:58-62], cached once by available() [:76-86]. So a WARN-free log on an AMX host plus a WARN-bearing control log with TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 is a real, source-backed distinguishing artifact. Slice writes the test binary's stdout and stderr into logs-<hostname>/run-NNNN/<name>.log [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:81, 2770, 3174-3187], so the WARN text lands in the file the design already tells the implementer to preserve. Not a re-raise: round-2 N36 covered the CI lane's RUN_TESTS skip, not the hardware early return [r2-findings.md:487-497]; none of the 16 rejected candidates covers it. The phrase existed in round 2 as "proof that the kernel ran" and only "proof" changed to "evidence" [design-wdiff.txt:1765-1769], so this is a residual omission in unchanged text, not a regression. Severity minor rather than note: the design's two statements (:445 rule, :469 evidence method) combine to a false positive for exactly this row, and one sentence fixes it. Risk if unfixed is low because hardware runs are confined to delphi-3bda [design-r3.txt:476], which has AMX. One detail of the finding is wrong and must be corrected (see correction): t_amx_dispatch_dtype never touches hardware.
    Correction: Narrow the recommendation to t_amx_numerics only. t_amx_dispatch_dtype defines its own fake bool available() noexcept { return true; } and fake kernels, and its header says "no AMX instruction is linked or executed; available() is the fake too" [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:4-8, 166-170]. It therefore never prints the "AMX unavailable" WARN, and TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 has no effect on it. The design row already covers it correctly as "Execute applicable fake dispatch cases" [design-r3.txt:453]. Fix citations: the TRON_AMX_DISABLE read is in detect_and_request [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@2880c3aa9b:58-62], not in available() itself [:76-86]; the child's WARN sites are :146-148 (QK), :199-201 (VNNI QK) and :247-249 (PV) at 30c4ac82cb. Reworded recommendation: after "evidence that the kernel ran" add: "Evidence is the Slice run log (logs-<host>/run-NNNN/t_amx_numerics.log) from delphi-3bda in which the cases 'AMX QK does not digress from the AVX dotter' and 'AMX PV stays inside the AVX weight-rounding envelope' show Catch2 passed and no 'AMX unavailable on this host' WARN line, plus a control run of the same binary with TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 whose log shows those WARN lines. 'Catch2 passed' alone is not enough: the tests WARN and return when available() is false, and that still passes. t_amx_dispatch_dtype uses fake kernels and is not hardware evidence." The parent row can reuse the runtime TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 control the design already prescribes for the child [design-r3.txt:443]. Also add the WARN-line rule as a sentence under :469 so the CI-evidence paragraph and the :445 rule agree.

(2) Name the artifact precisely: the Slice run log logs-<host>/run-NNNN/t_amx_numerics.log, which holds the test process's stdout and stderr [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:2770, 3148, 3174, 3182-3187], must contain "Catch2 passed" for "AMX QK does not digress from the AVX dotter" and "AMX PV stays inside the AVX weight-rounding envelope" (plus the child's "VNNI QK identity" case) and must contain no line with "AMX unavailable on this host". If used, set the variable in the environment before the process starts, because available() reads it once at the first call and caches the result [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@2880c3aa9b:76-80]. Suggested row text after "evidence that the kernel ran": "Evidence is the Slice run log of t_amx_numerics from delphi-3bda with Catch2 passed lines for the AMX precision cases and no 'AMX unavailable on this host' line [S13 AMX availability check, S19 Case execution records]; a Catch2 passed line alone does not prove execution, because the availability early return also ends with zero failed assertions." Also fix S13: it labels the early return "Child:" [design-r3.txt:577], but the same early returns exist on main [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:145-147, 189-191], so the row applies to the parent as well.

Minor H01. Local gate list omits make lint-notes, which the required Lint job runs

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design's local check list is "make format, make lint, make build-test, and make test-host" and the design names lint-notes nowhere (design-r3.txt:477; grep of design-r3.txt for "lint" hits only lines 48, 362, 477, 527, 584, none of which names lint-notes). The lint recipe runs diff --check, the cassert grep, clang-format, cargo fmt, lint-ci-pins and lint-agent-guidance, and never calls lint-notes; lint-notes is a separate phony target (GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:204, 675-685, 693-731). The required "Lint" job (README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:76-79) runs bash bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh (.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:43-56), whose default check_ref is .#checks.x86_64-linux.lint-toolchain (bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh@2880c3aa9b:7). That check is defined at flake.nix@2880c3aa9b:2087 with nativeBuildInputs = lintRuntimeDeps (lintToolchainDeps ++ [ lintNotes ], flake.nix:1571) and its body ends with bin/ci/check-lock-freshness.sh then make lint-notes (flake.nix:2231, 2233). The design edits Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] (design-r3.txt:362); at 2880c3aa9b that name has exactly one definition (kv_cache.hpp:2055) and eight See Note references (kv_cache.hpp:1056, 1886, 1905, 2197, 2298, 2337, 2378; t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2650), as the finding states. bin/lint-notes@2880c3aa9b:132-139 recognizes a definition only when a ~~~ rule sits under the Note [ line, and :278-286 exits nonzero on any reference to an undefined Note, so a renamed or un-underlined heading fails the check. The repo's scoped guide for h/src/t changes lists only the targeted test, make build-test and make test-host (.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:55-56), so "Follow the current scoped guides" (design-r3.txt:477) does not supply lint-notes either. No earlier round raised lint-notes (grep of r1-findings.md, r2-findings.md, facts-r1.md, facts-r2.md: zero hits), so this is new. Severity stays minor: CI catches the slip, at the cost of one failed required job and a rerun. Two details of the finding are off and one mitigation is missing; see the correction.
    Correction: Three corrections and one added mitigation. (1) Drop the sentence "The checker also needs the .#lint dev shell or GHC; the plain dev shell prints an error." The plain nix develop shell inherits the ingest Haskell shell (flake.nix@2880c3aa9b:544 inputsFrom = [ targetIngestFlake.devShells.default ], cabal tool at :329), and README.md@2880c3aa9b:237-247 documents nix develop as providing the pinned GHC and Cabal for make lint-notes. In that shell the recipe takes the bin/lint-notes (Cabal script) branch (GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:678-679); the error text (:681-683) prints only when neither tron-lint-notes nor GHC+Cabal is on PATH, i.e. outside both shells. The .#lint shell (flake.nix:1618-1625, packages = lintRuntimeDeps ++ [ lefthookDev ]) adds the precompiled tron-lint-notes. Reword the recommendation's parenthetical to: "(the .#lint shell supplies the precompiled checker; the default shell runs the bin/lint-notes script through its GHC and Cabal)". (2) Fix the citation "GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:675-683" to ":675-685" (the recipe's fi is at 685). (3) Replace "cross-references from four other files" with "cross-references at four sites in three files (amx_attn_iface.hpp, self_attention.hpp, model.hpp twice)" per design-r3.txt:363. Added mitigation, to narrow "passes make lint locally and fails the required check": lefthook.yml@2880c3aa9b:214-238 defines a pre-commit lint-notes command with globs h//*.{hpp,h,i}, src//*.cpp, t/**/*.cpp that runs make lint-notes, and the default dev shell registers that hook when CI is unset (flake.nix@2880c3aa9b:1611-1616 installNixHooks, appended to the default shell hook at :1851). So a commit made from the dev shell with hooks active does run lint-notes; the gap is the design's explicit checklist, commits made with hooks bypassed, and the hook's silent "Skipping: lint-notes checker or GHC/Cabal not found" path outside Nix (lefthook.yml:235). Also make the second recommendation conditional: the design does not require the relocated v_vnni.hpp documentation to be a Note, so say "If the relocated documentation is written as a Note, give the heading the ~~~ underline (bin/lint-notes@2880c3aa9b:132-139) and write each cross-reference as See Note [Name]; keep the name Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] unchanged, since eight comments reference it." Mechanism nit for the finding text: a heading without ~~~ is not parsed as a definition, so the checker reports the eight references as "Reference to undefined" (bin/lint-notes:283-284) rather than as a malformed definition (:115-116 covers only a missing ] or a name under 5 characters); the check fails either way.
  • design-text lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. The design's local gate list names make format, make lint, make build-test and make test-host, and nothing else [design-r3.txt:477]. The design never mentions lint-notes, the Note convention, lefthook, or the command the required Lint job runs (grep of design-r3.txt for "lint-notes", "See Note", "~~~", "lefthook", "hook": no hits). Its S20 "[Lint target]" link points at the lint target only [design-r3-links.tsv:233 = GNUmakefile#L693-L706]. Note G14. 8-lane class-completeness rule serves only dead fake code; moving the fakes under TRON_AMX_DISPATCH removes it

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central claim holds. Every source fact checked out at 2880c3aa9b (identical to live main for these files). Fakes are dead code with the option off. The fake kernel definitions sit at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:166-190 and the probe at :47-164. The file's own #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH starts at :192; the #else branch at :210-213 is a SUCCEED-only skip case. The test is registered without any if() in t/CMakeLists.txt:596 (no TRON_AMX_DISPATCH condition anywhere in t/CMakeLists.txt:540-620). The real kernels compile only inside if(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:219-224]. Every use of amx_attn_h128g4 in self_attention.hpp is inside an #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH block: :259-267, :281-290, :1429-1464, :1531-1538, :1571-1701 (pack at :1586, qk_rowmajor_128x4 at :1654, weights_times_v_128x4 at :1680), :1748-1771. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp is wrapped at :22 / :260 / :266. No other file references the namespace (git grep over the whole tree). So with the option off, nothing calls the fakes. The option cannot be on at 8 lanes. self_attention.hpp:30-36 is #if defined(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) && TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16 followed by #error. The finding's line range 30-36 is right (facts-r3 says 31-37, which is off by one). No other 8-lane client needs complete packed classes. The 8-lane cache keeps a row-major V array [kv_cache.hpp:2195-2201]; the 8-lane save branch uses v<>().set [model.hpp:2830-2836]; the 8-lane hardware unpack uses v_ptr [full.hpp:2651-2665]. Note G27. Debug row: 'make BUILD_TYPE=Debug <test>' does not reconfigure an existing gen/, and 'Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo' holds for one path only

2 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central mechanism holds at the pinned commit. BUILD_TYPE is a plain := assignment [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80], so a command-line BUILD_TYPE=Debug overrides it. The only place BUILD_TYPE reaches CMake is the three configure recipes (cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ...) [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:532, 541, 553]. The test configure recipe is the stamp rule gen/config/test. Its prerequisites are $(CMAKELISTS) (CMakeLists.txt, t/CMakeLists.txt, src/**/CMakeLists.txt; line 200), config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, the FUSE stamp (tracks ENABLE_FUSE_STATS only; 289-290), the preset stamp (tracks CMAKE_PRESET only; 299-303) and the plugin-bundle stamps [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538]. BUILD_TYPE appears nowhere else in the file (lines 80, 81, 310, 532, 541, 553 only). So when gen/config/test exists and is up to date, make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit runs only cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit and then gen/t_llama_unit with no arguments [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:880-888]; the cached RelWithDebInfo stays, and TRON_IGNORE_NAN stays defined for every non-Debug GCC/Clang build [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295, 314-318]. The reverse path also holds: the hand cmake line creates no gen/config stamp (no CMake file writes gen/config; only the recipe does at 542-543), so the first make build-test, make test-host or make t_llama_unit in a hand-configured Debug worktree re-runs cmake with the default -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:351, 367, 880, 541]. In a Make-configured Debug worktree a later plain make keeps Debug. The design row says "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo" without saying which path [design-r3.txt:455]. The native preset fixes binaryDir gen and CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:34, 37]. GNUmakefile, CMakePresets.json and both CMakeLists.txt files are byte-identical between 2880c3aa9b and live main 1400fa4481 (git diff --stat empty). The Debug row is new in round 3 [design-wdiff.txt:1776, NEW segment; the round-2 text has no BUILD_TYPE=Debug]. Severity minor, borderline note: the design already prescribes a separate worktree per configuration and says to record the build type and generated compile definitions [design-r3.txt:449] and to "Confirm the macro is absent" [:455], so an agent following the text would catch the wrong policy. One sentence removes the ambiguity.
    Correction: Narrow "an existing gen/" in the title and claim to "a gen/ that a Make target already configured (gen/config/test present and up to date)". A gen/ configured only by the row's hand cmake line has no stamp, so make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit there DOES re-run cmake with Debug [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538-543]. On the design's prescribed path (fresh worktree per configuration, design-r3.txt:449) the row's make BUILD_TYPE=Debug instruction is therefore correct; the defect is (1) the unqualified sentence "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo" [design-r3.txt:455], which is true only after a hand configure and false after a Make configure, and (2) the unstated hazard of reusing a Make-configured RelWithDebInfo gen/. Replace "silently undoes" with "re-runs cmake with RelWithDebInfo; the only sign is the ordinary configure output" (the recipe prints cmake's stdout; no warning names the change). In the recommendation, replace "absent from compile_commands.json for the binary you run" with "absent from the compile lines of the test's translation units in gen/compile_commands.json (CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS is on in the base-ninja preset [CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:22])", and extend "a CMakeLists.txt, models.yaml or preset input changed" to also name t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, ENABLE_FUSE_STATS and the plugin-bundle stamps [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538]. Suggested one-sentence design fix for the row: "Make re-runs cmake only when gen/config/test is missing or one of its listed inputs changed; it does not track BUILD_TYPE.   • design-text lens: refuted (high confidence, severity note). The finding's build-system facts are right, but the design already says what the finding says it lacks, so the ambiguity is not there for an implementer who follows the page. Facts confirmed. BUILD_TYPE is used only as the default (GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80-81), in a debug print (:310) and in the three configure recipes (:532, :541, :553). The gen/config/test rule depends on $(CMAKELISTS), config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh and four stamps (:538-543). None of those tracks BUILD_TYPE. gen/t_% runs cmake --build gen --target (:880-881). t_% runs gen/$@ with no arguments (:886-887). So make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit in a gen/ that already holds an up-to-date gen/config/test stamp does not reconfigure. A hand-configured gen/ has no gen/config/test stamp, so the first plain make target reconfigures with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo. Why the finding does not hold against the design text. (1) The failure scenario needs an existing RelWithDebInfo gen/. The design forbids that scenario: "Use a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair, with the normal gen/ build directory in each" [design-r3.txt:449]. The Debug check is a row of the configuration table [design-r3.txt:455], so it gets its own worktree with a fresh gen/. In a fresh worktree both options of the row give Debug: make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit configures with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug because the stamp is missing, and cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit after the row's cmake line keeps the hand configuration. (2) The design already warns that Make may reconfigure gen/: "repository Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it. Confirm the cached feature values after invoking them" [design-r3.txt:449], and "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo" [design-r3.txt:455]. The word "can" is accurate for both paths the finding separates. A Make-configured Debug tree also reconfigures to RelWithDebInfo once any configure input changes (a CMakeLists.txt, config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, or a stamp) [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538-543]. So the finding's own sentence "In a Make-configured Debug worktree a later plain make keeps Debug" is only conditionally true, and the design's hedged sentence is the safer statement. (3) The design already requires the check that detects a wrong build type: "Confirm the macro is absent" [design-r3.txt:455] and "Record compiler version, build type, flags, and generated compile definitions" [design-r3.txt:449]. The Bits-and-conversions row selects NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN [design-r3.txt:437], so the test passes under either policy, and the macro check is what proves which policy ran. The design says to do that check. The finding itself says the risk is low for these reasons. What survives is a note-level wording point, not an ambiguity that changes what gets built: the t_% Make target runs the whole binary with no Catch2 filter [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:886-887], so "Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target" [design-r3.txt:455] cannot run a subset of cases by itself. The agent must run gen/t_llama_unit with a case-name argument after building. Also the design does not name where to confirm the build type and the macro. Neither point misleads an implementer into building the wrong thing. Related dispositions: N60's corrected recommendation asked for the cache-variable persistence caveat and the one-worktree-per-configuration rule; the design carries both at design-r3.txt:449 and section 9 row N39 N40 N41 N60 [design-r3.txt:527]. N02's corrected recommendation asked for the #ifdef guard and the Debug/non-Debug statement; the design carries both at design-r3.txt:331 and :437 and row N02 N12 [design-r3.txt:513]. G27 adds no new omission against those recommendations.

Note G38. Packed accessor names follow different patterns: page::v_view versus page::k_packed

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The central claim holds. The design names the parent's packed V accessor page::v_view<geometry>(slot, head) and says it returns v_vnni_view<const bf16,page_size,geometry.head_size> [design-r3.txt:271]. The design names the child's packed K accessor page::k_packed<geometry>(slot, head) and says const access returns k_vnni_view<const bf16,page_size,geometry.head_size> [design-r3.txt:404]. The two accessors return the same shape family under different suffixes ("_view" and "_packed"). The existing native pair page::k / kv_block::k_view keeps its names [design-r3.txt:267]. In main, page::k returns kv_block(...).k_view() [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1550-1569] and kv_block::k_view is defined at [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2208, 2215]. The child's raw accessor is const bf16* k_vnni_plane(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head) const noexcept and it returns reinterpret_cast<const bf16*>(kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).k) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1689, 1692]. Neither main nor the child defines a v_view or k_packed today (grep at 2880c3aa9b and 30c4ac82cb: 0 hits). The design states no rationale for using two suffixes: the only naming words in both tables are "Keep the name" [design-r3.txt:269, 272, 406]. The design does state that K should follow V's owner rules [design-r3.txt:401], so the pair is meant to be symmetric. Severity stays note: both names are written out, so an implementer builds the right thing either way, and the round-2 intent verifier graded the analogous v_tensor naming point as "Note (no change required; a rename is optional)" [r2-findings.md:330]. Four details of the finding are off and need the correction below: the origin of the v_view name, the origin of the k_packed name, the "section 8" pointer, and the "cannot infer" wording.
    Correction: Narrow and re-anchor the finding as follows. (1) The name page::v_view is not codex's own choice. Round-2 findings N18 and N23 both recommended it: N18 said "Rename to page::v_view<geometry>(slot, kv_head) (or v_plane)" [r2-findings.md:327] and N23 said "Add page::v_view<geometry>(slot, kv_head) const under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 only, returning v_vnni_view<const bf16, page_size, geometry.head_size>" [r2-findings.md:358]. The design's section 9 records the adoption: "Return a read-only packed v_view only at 16 lanes" [design-r3.txt:520]. A recommendation to rename v_view to v_packed therefore reverses the round-2 name recommendation, and the finding must say so. (2) The name page::k_packed is new in this revision (round-2 text only said "page::k_vnni_plane Remove the raw-pointer accessor. Its replacement returns k_vnni_view<const bf16,64,128>" [evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:377]; the word diff shows the NEW segment "with page::k_packed(slot, head)" [design-wdiff.txt:1384]). It matches the reviewer's sketch exactly: Ben's comment shows auto k_packed(kv_slot_id slot, size_t head) const noexcept { return kv_block<geometry>(slot, head).k.as_view(); } and the usage example qk_vnni_128x4(page.v_packed(...), ...); // Compile error [evidence/github-review.json, Ben's sketch comment: k_packed 2 hits, v_packed 1 hit, v_view 0 hits, k_view 0 hits]. So the reviewer's own vocabulary uses "_packed" for both accessors. This is the strongest reason to prefer v_packed / k_packed, and the finding should cite it instead of style alone. (3) Replace "cannot infer the K name from section 5" with "the two accessors use different suffixes for the same kind of return value, and the design gives no reason". Both names are stated explicitly [design-r3.txt:271, :404], so no inference is needed. (4) Replace "update lines 271, 404 and section 8" with "update lines 271, 404 and the section 9 disposition row at line 520". Section 8 [design-r3.txt:429-504] does not mention v_view or k_packed; the only other mention is the N16-N24 row [design-r3.txt:520]. (5) Optional supporting point: the parent merges before the child [design-r3.txt:124 "Add the tensor interface to main first"], so a v_view name frozen in main would need a second rename PR if the pair is later made consistent. Decide the shared suffix before the parent PR is opened. Keep the "page::k_vnni_view would clash with the type name" remark as a reason to avoid that option (a member named k_vnni_view inside page would hide the namespace-scope class template of the same name within page's scope); it is not central. The child accessor path in the evidence should read h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1689, not kv_cache.hpp alone.

A row-to-row converting constructor is not construction by the matrix view, so the literal reading forbids it. design-r3.txt:438 then tells the test author to "Accept writable-to-read-only conversion" and to check "reverse const conversion" without naming views or rows. The design added the "only producer" half of N20 and dropped the friend half without recording a choice; section 9 says only "Restrict row construction" (design-r3.txt:518). Ben's sketch (comment 5765866077, body lines 73-77 and 90-91) has the converting constructor and template <typename, typename> friend class vnni_view; for views, exactly as the finding states. Severity minor rather than note: the finding itself asks for a one-clause text change, the N20 corrected recommendation explicitly requested this item, and N20's disposition is therefore "partly", not "resolved". Risk is low: an implementer who reads :248 literally builds rows without conversion, which breaks nothing, and a test that tries a row conversion fails to compile visibly rather than silently. Note remains defensible if the lead weights the absence of a consumer more heavily.

That pointer is v_scratch.data() + h * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE, where v_scratch is alignas(64) std::array<bf16, ...> on the stack of gof::populate [src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203, :213]. (3) All 15 test call sites pass raw pointers or .data() of arrays and tensors [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:107, 1723, 1923, 2038, 2533-2539, 2568-2569, 2690, 2705, 2721, 2761, 2792, 2802, 2824; t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:443-444]. So the ambiguity is real at the GOF callback and the raw-array test fixtures, and it has no behavioral effect: note. Refuted parts. (a) "Nothing to preserve at the model 16-lane site" is wrong. vs[ix] is a buffer object with an as_view() member; the model already requires it [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1382-1383, attention_buffer_width uses [token_job_id(0)].as_view()]. The 8-lane branch of the same function uses that view two lines below the raw pointer [model.hpp:2834-2836]. So an existing contiguous view with a DMA flag exists at the model site, and slice keeps both the aligned and the dma flag [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp@2880c3aa9b:76-78] and even accepts the owner directly [slice.hpp:40-42]. (b) "tensor::as_view() carries dma = false" describes only the host executor. The buffer element type is the executor's btensor_t [h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp@2880c3aa9b:195; h/tron/models/common.hpp:87]. The production executors tp1, tp2, tp4 and perm_* use hardware::btensor [common.hpp:79, :94-99], which is dmatensor<bf16, ...> [h/tron/hardware/btensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:21]; its as_view() returns view<bf16, true, true, seq<N>, sseq<1>>, dma = true [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:173, :223-228]. Only host binds tensor (dma = false) [common.hpp:100; tensor.hpp:35, :71-75]; host_fp16 binds dmatensor<fp16> [htensor.hpp:8]. This is why set_v has bf16, fp16 and float overloads [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1621-1641]. The design sentence therefore has a concrete meaning at the model site: derive the source from vs[ix].as_view() and let Dma follow the buffer type. (c) The finding's recommendation "construct the view with dma = false" at the model site would label a DMA-allocated buffer "definitely not DMA-safe" [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:11-21 defines the flag semantics] under tp1/tp2/tp4. Harmless to the packed bodies, but the opposite of the design's stated rule. (d) "Two of the three migrated call sites" and "only the 8-lane branch has an existing view" miscount.   • design-text lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The finding holds for one of the two sites it names, and only as a harmless omission. What the design says. The row-write rule declares Dma as a deduced template parameter of the ordinary contiguous view: "const_view<Source, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> src" and "view<Destination, true, Dma, seq<D>, sseq<1>> dst" [design-r3.txt:255]. The sentence "Dma preserves the existing contiguous view's DMA flag" [design-r3.txt:257] describes that deduction. "The existing contiguous view" names tron's pre-existing view type, the same thing line 259 calls "the ordinary contiguous destination view" [design-r3.txt:259]. The child section repeats the rule for K: "The boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties" [design-r3.txt:405]. Round-2 N15 asked for exactly this form, with a lowercase, free "dma" parameter [r2-findings.md, N15 RECOMMENDATION and both verifier corrections]. So the sentence does not presume a view object at the call site. It leaves the flag to whatever view the caller builds. Model site: the finding's "nothing to preserve" is wrong. The 16-lane branch passes a raw pointer today [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832]. But the buffer it points into has its own contiguous view: attention_buffer_width is defined through vs[token_job_id(0)].as_view() [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1382-1383], and the 8-lane branch three lines below already wraps with slice<...>()(vs[ix].as_view(), offset) [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2834-2836]. Every tron owner type carries dma = false [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:35, :71, :75, :254; h/tron/tensor/itensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:26], and slice returns a view with the same aligned and dma arguments [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp@2880c3aa9b:53, :76]. The design's step 3 "Wrap aligned source rows in the packed branch" [design-r3.txt:374] plus that precedent gives the implementer a view whose flag is preserved without any choice. GOF site: the finding is right. The callback receives a raw bf16* dest [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2656]. That pointer is into a stack array, alignas(64) std::array<bf16, ...> v_scratch [src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203, :213; h/tron/gof.hpp@2880c3aa9b:62-66]. No view exists there. The design says only "Wrap existing caller-owned scratch in the ordinary contiguous destination view" [design-r3.txt:259], "wraps its aligned scratch" [design-r3.txt:269] and "Update callback scratch wrapping" [design-r3.txt:439]. It never names the Dma argument for that wrap. views.hpp defines dma = true as "definitely DMA-safe" memory [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:11-19]. A stack array is not that, so false is the only honest value, and the design does not say so. Effect: none on behavior. The dma parameter is consumed only by the matmul launchers and the views concept checks [tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:358-380, :415-416; views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:146-150]. The moved get_v loops write through the pointer and never read the flag. Either template argument compiles and runs identically. An implementer cannot build the wrong thing. Severity note, as the finding itself proposes.

Note G42. Uniform-array rule: the 'existing uniform accessor' justification holds only for uniform reclaimability

2 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The central claim holds. The design's third sentence of the uniform bullet says the one-array rule "matches the existing uniform accessor's indexing across slots" [design-r3.txt:349]. That accessor requires layout_t::uniform_geometry [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1277]. Its cross-slot indexing exists only in the if constexpr (layout_t::uniform_reclaimability) branch, which casts kv_blocks_alias to kv_block_t* and indexes blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1284-1289]. The else branch computes slot_base(kv_storage_offset(physical_slot)) per slot and indexes blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] inside that slot [1290-1299]. uniform_geometry and uniform_reclaimability are separate predicates: one compares geometries, the other compares retention.reclaimable() [594-609, 681-683]. reclaimable() is true only for sliding_window retention [141-143]. The test fixture uniform_mixed_retention_cache has three geometry_64 slots with full_history, sliding_window(128), sliding_window(64) [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:171-175, 184-185], so uniform_geometry is true and uniform_reclaimability is false, and the test case at 602-603 ("uniform-geometry mixed retention addresses both arenas") frees the reclaimable arena, reads slot 0 from the retained arena, restores, and rewrites slots 1 and 2 [604-621]. kv_blocks_alias is one slot's base: refresh_kv_blocks_alias sets it to slot_base(storage_view_offset_) [1222-1228], where storage_view_offset_ is 0 by default [1129] or the EAGLE slot after set_storage_view [892-898]. The rule itself is right per arena: make_kv_slot_offsets packs each slot's n_kv_heads * block_bytes contiguously into its retention arena [650-671], slot_base returns arena + n_pages * byte_offset [1188-1196], and block_bytes is the same for every slot under uniform geometry. The sentence is byte-identical to the round-2 text [evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:331]; the word diff contains no change to it. The round-2 N25 design-text verifier recorded the two-branch nuance as an evidence precision only [r2-findings.md, N25 verifier correction (2)]. Severity note is right: the operative sentences ("one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region", bound = arena bytes / sizeof(kv_block_t)) are correct for both branches, and the helper's placement inside allocate_kv_group, which the constructor calls once per arena [1101-1102] and restore calls once for the reclaimable arena [968], already makes the rule per-arena. Only the justification sentence is loose.
    Correction: Three details need narrowing. (1) The design text does not name kv_blocks_alias anywhere [grep of design-r3.txt: no hit]. The risk is indirect: an implementer who follows "the existing uniform accessor" to kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1284-1289 finds kv_blocks_alias as the base pointer. Reword "should not point the implementer at kv_blocks_alias" to "should not send the implementer to an accessor branch whose base pointer is kv_blocks_alias". (2) "refreshed only after allocation" is too narrow. refresh_kv_blocks_alias runs after allocate_kv_group returns in the constructor [1114] and in restore [971], and also on set_storage_view [897], reset_storage_view [902] and free_reclaimable_kv_storage [953]. The relevant fact is that inside allocate_kv_group [1199-1208], where design-r3.txt:348 places the construction helper, the alias is still nullptr (constructor, member default at 1128) or stale (restore, after the free at 953 refreshed it against a missing arena). (3) "Apply this to each arena separately" is already implied by "the just-allocated arena's" [design-r3.txt:349] plus the helper's placement in allocate_kv_group, which runs once per arena [1101, 1102, 968]. The recommendation should say it makes the implied scope explicit. Suggested replacement for the third sentence: "The existing uniform accessor indexes one array across slots only when layout_t::uniform_reclaimability holds (kv_cache.hpp:1284-1289); with mixed retention it addresses each slot through slot_base (1290-1299). The one-array rule still holds for each arena, because every slot of a uniform-geometry layout has the same kv_block_t and the slots of one arena are packed contiguously (650-671, 1188-1196). Use the arena pointer allocate_kv_group has just installed (retained_data or reclaimable_data), not kv_blocks_alias, which is one slot's base and is refreshed after allocate_kv_group returns (1114, 971, 1222-1228). A uniform-geometry layout with mixed retention has both arenas (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:602-603)." Also add the uniform-geometry mixed-retention case to the section 8 storage row, which names "mixed geometry" and "release/restore" but not that case [design-r3.txt:441].

(3) The justification sentence remains true in substance for the else branch. slot_base returns arena + n_pages * byte_offset [:1188-1197], and byte_offset is the sum of the preceding same-arena slots' bytes [:659-661]. An implementer following the S8 block-access link (f46e48ba L1274-L1334, identical to 2880c3aa9b) sees both branches and can derive the equivalence, but the design does not state it. The finding itself says the rule is right for that layout and rates the item a note.

Note G46. Deduction trap for typed K row arguments not restated for the child's callers

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The central fact holds. The rank-1 view is a final struct that derives only from expr<view<...>, d0> [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:116-117]. The rank-1 const_view is a separate final template [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:361-362]. Its writable-to-read-only conversion is a converting constructor [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:382, 385], and its raw-pointer constructor is explicit [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:373]. Template argument deduction does not use converting constructors, and there is no derived-to-base path from view to const_view. So a parameter of type const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> cannot deduce Aligned or Dma from a writable view or from a bf16 pointer. The child's callers all pass raw pointers or a writable view's pointer: model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2861-2864 (row_of = slice of ks[ix].as_view(); ks is a non-const kv_buffer_t& at :2857 and a non-const as_view() returns a writable view [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:71]), :2920 (kout.data), :2883 and :2924 (alignas(64) bf16 conv[16][head_size], conv[0]), full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2645 and :2655 (bf16* dest), t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:401 and :405 (row.data(), got.data()). The design states the explicit-construction rule only in the V row-write bullets of section 5 [design-r3.txt:257; section 5 spans lines 228-293]. The K row [design-r3.txt:405] says the boolean template arguments "preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties" and "Wrap scratch without copying" but never states that a writable view or a raw pointer does not bind. A grep for "deduc" in design-r3.txt hits only line 257. Severity: the compiler rejects each unwrapped call and the fix is local, so an implementer would not build the wrong thing. One sentence in the row would save trial and error across four files, and round-2 N32's corrected recommendation already asked the row to name kout, conv[i], and dest at the call site, which the design reduced to "scratch". That makes the text change warranted at low risk: minor.

Rejected G43. Odd-append precondition contradicts the recommended poison test order

Candidate claim: Section 6 states that an odd cache append requires the pair to be initialized ('pair must be initialized', 'requires the even partner to have been initialized'). Section 8 tells the implementer to 'Poison the odd row' and then append its even partner. Poisoning the odd row is itself an odd cache append. In the existing test it is done into a fresh book whose pair has never been written, so the merge reads an indeterminate even half; the existing test relies on this being harmless, and the even append then overwrites the whole pair. The precondition and the recommended test order disagree. No runtime check can enforce 'initialized', so the risk is low, but an implementer reading section 6 alone may reorder the test and lose the dirty-buffer case.

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The central claim holds. The design states the odd-append precondition in three places: the table row "Odd cache append | Yes, pair must be initialized" [design-r3.txt:314], the bullet "append of an odd token requires the even partner to have been initialized" [design-r3.txt:353], and the append_v_row bullet "An odd destination merges into the initialized pair" [design-r3.txt:258]. Section 8 says "Retain scaled_v padding NaN. Poison the odd row, append its even partner through the page::set_v called by save_v_impl" [design-r3.txt:436]. The retained test case is TEST_CASE("scaled_v padding NaN") [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2658]. Its SECTION "single-token dirty-buffer reuse" [:2779] builds a fresh book_t bk(1) [:2780] and poisons row 1 with p->set_v(..., 1, nan_buf) [:2792] before any even write. That call takes the odd branch of page::set_v [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2304-2318]. The odd branch loads the pair with _mm512_load_si512 [:2312], merges with _mm512_ternarylogic_epi32 [:2314-2315], and stores [:2316]. It checks no precondition. The fresh book's arena comes from allocate_kv_group [:1199-1208], which calls try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite [:1202-1203]. That helper default-constructs elements only for non-trivially-constructible types [h/system/memory.hpp@2880c3aa9b:333-335], and uint8_t is trivial, so nothing clears the arena. The test calls no fill before the odd set_v. So the retained test performs an odd cache append into a never-written pair, and the design's stated precondition forbids that. The even set_v at [:2802] then overwrites the whole pair by zero-extension [kv_cache.hpp:2298-2302], which is why the test passes. The finding's file and line citations are all exact (the header path is h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp). Severity note is right: no runtime check can detect an unwritten pair, and the only risk is an implementer dropping the poison-into-unwritten-pair step.

The finding's factual reading of both sections is right, but its central claim (a contradiction that could make an implementer lose the dirty-buffer case) does not hold. What the design says. Section 6 gives the precondition twice: "Odd cache append | Yes, pair must be initialized | Even row is preserved" [design-r3.txt:314] and "append of an odd token requires the even partner to have been initialized" [design-r3.txt:353]. Section 5 says the same: "An odd destination merges into the initialized pair" [design-r3.txt:258]. Section 8 says: "Retain scaled_v padding NaN. Poison the odd row, append its even partner through the page::set_v called by save_v_impl, then compute a weighted sum with live count 1 token" [design-r3.txt:436]. Why the contradiction is not there. The finding assumes "Poisoning the odd row is itself an odd cache append". The design does not say how the test applies the poison. The same section-6 table offers a fixture path that needs no initialized pair: "Direct element update | No read of other elements required | Other elements unchanged; this does not establish cache readiness" [design-r3.txt:315], and the bullet under it says "Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append" [design-r3.txt:317]. The design also keeps the layout-blind whole-block poison fill (book::fill_random, fill_storage_slot) as an explicit test-support exception [design-r3.txt:274] and lists "poison fill" among the retained lifecycle cases [design-r3.txt:441]. An implementer who poisons the odd row by a direct element write or by fill_random satisfies both the section-6 precondition and the section-8 order. So section 6 "alone" is exactly where the fixture exception lives. Why the stated risk does not follow. Section 8 fixes the order: poison, then even append, then weighted sum with live count 1 token [design-r3.txt:436]. The only reordering that also satisfies "pair initialized" is to add an even append BEFORE the poison. The poison is then still present when the tested even append runs, so the dirty-buffer case (an even append clears an odd row that holds NaN) is still exercised. The design's own figure draws exactly this: "Reused pair: Old even row, Odd row: NaN poison -> Append even token -> Append odd token" [design-r3.txt:300-306]. No reordering that follows section 8 loses the case. Source facts confirmed. The odd set_v path loads the pair with _mm512_load_si512 and merges, with no precondition check [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2305-2316]. So the existing poison step does read an unwritten even half. That part of the finding is right. Why the contradiction does not hold. The design does not say the poison step must be an odd cache append. The same table has a third row, "Direct element update", which reads no other elements and needs no initialized pair [design-r3.txt:315]. The bullet under the table says "Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append" [design-r3.txt:317]. A fixture that poisons by direct element write, then appends the even partner through page::set_v, satisfies the precondition and the recommended order at the same time. The design also states that element storage stays uninitialized until written [design-r3.txt:346], so it already accepts that fixtures touch unwritten storage. The "pair must be initialized" cell is a production readiness rule for the pair's result. The poison step does not aim at a correct pair, so the rule does not apply to it. Why the consequence is nil. The recommended order came from the round-1 review itself: F01 asked for "poison an odd row, write the even partner through the same page method that save_v_impl calls, then check scaled_v with count = 1" [r1-findings.md:9]. Any reorder that keeps one even append after the poison still covers the dirty-buffer case. A reorder that puts the poison after the last even append makes the weighted sum read NaN, and REQUIRE_FALSE(std::isnan(...)) fails loudly [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2812-2822]. No silent loss of coverage is possible. An implementer cannot build the wrong parent PR from this text, and Ben's acceptance does not depend on it. Residue. The retained existing test performs one odd set_v on an unwritten pair. The design's literal precondition does not carve out that fixture step. An optional one-clause note would remove the strict reading. That is a note, not a change the design must make.
